2. Increased [vertical encroachment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s of 20 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. Increased maximum [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [height in feet](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [vertical encroachment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 2C.4.3. Height in Stories

Height in stories is defined as the vertical dimension of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) measured in [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

1. ##### Intent


1. Maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards are intended to provide adequate light, air, safety, and to protect the character of an area and the interests of the general public. Intended to help provide variation in [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) heights, maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards help ensure that [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) heights are not reduced to fit within a maximum [height in feet](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

2. Minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards are intended to provide a method of establishing a minimum level of intensity on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), and ensure that [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s are not underdeveloped.
2. ##### Applicability


1. Maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) where the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) specifies a maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standard.

2. Minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) where the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) specifies a minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standard.
3. ##### Standards


1. ###### Minimum Height in Stories


      1. ###### General


         Each portion of [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) used to meet the minimum [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standard specified by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) shall contain [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) for a depth no less than 15 feet on every [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) above the [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), up to, and including the minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) specified by the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).

      2. ###### Bonus Minimum Height in Stories


         1. When bonus minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) is specified by the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B), the minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) applies only to projects utilizing [bonus FAR](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.1.C.2. (Tier 1 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.1) or [Sec. 2C.4.1.C.3. (Tier 2 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.1).

         2. The minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) requirement does not apply to predominantly non-residential [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s. For the purposes of this rule, "predominantly non-residential" means a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) with more than 50 percent of the total [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) allocated to non- [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s (not including [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s in the eating & drinking, [personal services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), and [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [use group](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s).
2. ###### Maximum Height in Stories


      1. ###### Base


         [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s shall not exceed the base maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without meeting [Div. 9.3. (Community Benefits Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3).

      2. ###### Tier 1 Bonus


         1. [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s may exceed the base maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) up to the [tier 1 bonus height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) as allowed in [Div. 9.3. (Community Benefits Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3)), if the participating [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) provides the required [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s.

         2. [Project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s participating in incentive programs intended to implement State law, including the [State Density Bonus Program (Sec. 9.2.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), the [Opportunity Corridors Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), the [Corridor Transitions Incentive Program (Sec 9.2.4.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), [Transit Oriented Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.5), the [Permanent Supportive Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.4.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.1), or the [Accessory Dwelling Unit Incentive Program (Div. 9.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.5), may exceed the maximum [tier 1 bonus height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).
      3. ###### Tier 2 Bonus


         1. [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s may exceed the maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) up to the maximum [tier 2 bonus height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the applied [Form District (Part 2B)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) as allowed by [Div. 9.3. (Community Benefits Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3), or an applicable [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), [Supplemental District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), or [Special Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), if the participating [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) provides the required restricted affordable units and additional public benefits.

         2. [Project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s participating in incentive programs intended to implement State law, including the S [tate Density Bonus Program (Sec. 9.2.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), the [Opportunity Corridors Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), the [Corridor Transitions Incentive Program (Sec 9.2.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), [Transit Oriented Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.4.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), the [Permanent Supportive Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.4.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.1), or the [Accessory Dwelling Unit Incentive Program (Div. 9.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.5), may exceed the maximum [tier 2 bonus height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).
4. ##### Measurement


1. [Height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) is measured as the number of [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) above the [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) for each [module](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) as shown below. See [Sec. 14.2.9.D. (Building Module Method)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.9).
       [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.3.1.png.webp?itok=GwD4fMGC)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.3.1.png?itok=YCHxyBcq) [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.3.3.png.webp?itok=lBzyZ_om)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.3.3.png?itok=CvZTeSHm)
2. For determining [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), see [Sec. 14.2.10.A. (Ground Story)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10).

3. ###### Structures without Stories


      1. For determining the maximum allowed height for [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s that do not contain habitable [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) when the applied form district does not also regulate [height in feet](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), the maximum allowed height shall be determined by multiplying the maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) by 15 feet per allowable [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#). This resulting product shall be the maximum height allowed for a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) containing no habitable [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      2. When the applied form district includes a bonus maximum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), the number of bonus [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) specified shall be used to determine the maximum allowable height of [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s containing no habitable [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

3. A reduction in minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) may be granted as a Class 1 Conditional Use Permit. In addition to the findings otherwise required by [Sec. 13B.2.1. (Class 1 Conditional Use Permit)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.2.1), the [Zoning Administrator](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall also find that the reduction would be consistent with prevailing heights along the [block face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

4. A reduction in minimum [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 2C.4.4. City Hall Height Restriction

City Hall height restriction is defined as a restriction to the vertical dimension of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) based-on proximity and height relative to Los Angeles City Hall.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (City Hall Height Restriction) is to maintain the prominence of the historic Los Angeles City Hall tower in the Downtown Civic Center area by ensuring that the height of the tower remains significantly taller than any other [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) surrounding City Hall.

2. ##### Applicability


[City Hall height restriction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) where the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) specifies "Yes" for [City Hall height restriction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

3. ##### Standards


1. For portions of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s within 675 feet of City Hall, no portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) may be located above an [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) equal to 1.5 times its distance from City Hall plus the [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) at the base of City Hall, as measured from sea level.

2. For portions of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s located more than 675 feet from City Hall, no portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) may be located above the [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the topmost point of City Hall.

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.4.1.png.webp?itok=9BktN_VK)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.4.1.png?itok=JgbwWQW7)
4. ##### Measurement


1. ###### Maximum Height


      The maximum [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall be calculated using the following formula: 1.5(distance) + 295 feet = maximum [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) above sea level

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.4.3.png.webp?itok=_JzgLdCh)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.4.4.3.png?itok=N0OF4oaT)

2. ###### Distance from City Hall Tower


      Distance from City Hall is measured horizontally outward from the center point of its tower. The center point of the tower is considered to be located at the following geographic coordinates:

      X = -118.242757887301

      Y = 34.0536897906413

3. ###### Topmost point of City Hall Tower


      The topmost point of the City Hall tower is considered to be located at 745 feet above sea level. Any portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) located below this [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) is considered to be located below the topmost point of the tower.

4. ###### Base of City Hall Tower


      The base of City Hall is considered to be located at 295 feet above sea level.
5. ##### Relief


An increase in [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) height above the City Hall height restriction may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).


### Div. 2C.5. Building Mass

#### Sec. 2C.5.1. Building Width

Building width is defined as the horizontal dimension of any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or collection of [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Building Width) is to promote fine-grained patterns of development and prevent long [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s that are significantly out of context with traditional patterns by breaking wide [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s into multiple, clearly distinguished [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s, and to encourage larger [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s to provide open space for pedestrians and recreation.

2. ##### Applicability


[Building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of any [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#)- [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s. When the [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply, the standards only apply to those portions of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) located above the [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      1. No applicable [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or collection of [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s located on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall be wider than the maximum [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) specified by the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).

      2. In order to establish [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) as separate [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s for the purpose of measuring maximum [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), a [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall be provided between the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s.

      3. [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s that are located on separate [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s, share no interior circulation, and are structurally independent, are considered separate [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s for the purpose of measuring [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      4. A [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) on a [corner lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) within the [build-to zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [area of overlap](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) is allowed to exceed the maximum [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) by up to 40 feet along both [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s and [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s.

      5. All applicable [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s and collections of [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s located on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall be separated by at least the minimum [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) dimension for the full depth of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in order to establish them as separate [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s for the purpose of measuring [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      6. No [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall encroach into the [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), except where allowed in Subsection E. (Exceptions) below.
2. ###### Bonus Building Width


      1. Notwithstanding Paragraph 1. (General), above, [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s may exceed the maximum [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) up to the [bonus building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in feet of the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) as allowed by [Div. 9.3. (Community Benefits Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3), if the participating project provides the required [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s or other public benefits.

      2. [Project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s participating in incentive programs intended to implement State law, including the [State Density Bonus Program (Sec. 9.2.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), the [Opportunity Corridors Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), the [Corridor Transitions Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), [Transit Oriented Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.4.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), the [Permanent Supportive Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.4.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.1), or the [Accessory Dwelling Unit Incentive Program (Div. 9.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.5), may exceed the maximum [bonus building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).
4. ##### Measurement


1. [Building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) is measured horizontally and parallel to each [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) and [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) from one end of an applicable [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or collection of [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s to the opposite end.

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.5.1.1.png.webp?itok=Pkt8BHhn)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.5.1.1.png?itok=1qN8BdAk)

2. For [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#)- [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), see [Sec. 14.2.6. (Facing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.6).

3. For measuring [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) on irregular [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s, see [Sec. 14.2.14. (Irregular Lot lines)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.14).

4. A [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) is measured perpendicular to the outermost surface of each applicable portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) both vertically and horizontally.
       [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.5.1.3.png.webp?itok=EaCHMbgS)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.5.1.3.png?itok=t4rM6asL)
5. ##### Exceptions


1. ###### Encroachments


      The following are allowed to encroach into the [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), as listed below:



      |     |     |
      | --- | --- |
      | Allowed Horizontal Encroachments |
      | Architectural Details ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.a.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
      | Encroachment (max) | 2’ |
      | Clear width (min) | 3’ |
      | Roof Projections ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.b.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
      | Encroachment (max) | 2.5’ |
      | Clear width (min) | 3’ |
      | Unenclosed Structures: Above Ground Story<br>( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.d.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5) \- [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.d.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
      | Encroachment (max) | 5’ |
      | Clear width (min) | 3’ |
      | Mechanical/Electrical Equipment ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.f.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5) \- [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.g.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
      | Encroachment (max) | 1.5’ |
      | Clear width (min) | 3’ |

2. ###### Building Break Amenity Space Alternative


      As an alternative to a [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), a street-facing amenity space that meets the following standards may be used to establish [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s or collections of [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s as separate [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s for the purpose of measuring maximum [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#):

      1. The amenity space shall meet the design standards of an amenity space type pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.3. (Amenity Space Types)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3) and for outdoor space pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.4.C.1. (Outdoor Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.4).

      2. The amenity space width shall be at least two times the minimum [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) dimension specified in the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B), measured parallel to the applicable [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      3. The amenity space width shall not be greater than the maximum [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), measured parallel to the applicable [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      4. The amenity space depth shall be at least five times the minimum [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) dimension specified in the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B), measured perpendicular to the street [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      5. A minimum of 75 percent of the amenity space area shall meet the design standards in [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.2. (Pedestrian Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3).

      6. The amenity space may count toward the required minimum [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) required by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), provided it meets the requirements of [Sec. 3C.1.3.E. (Exceptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.1.3).

      7. Any portion of the amenity space may count toward [lot amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) and [residential amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), provided it meets all applicable standards.
          [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.5.1.5.png.webp?itok=KB1Ew9T4)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.5.1.5.png?itok=5zfllzUt)
6. ##### Relief


1. Increased [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of 20 percent or less or reduced [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of 20 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. Increased [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or reduced [building break](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

### Div. 2C.6. Upper-Story Bulk

#### Sec. 2C.6.1. Street Step-Back

Street step-back is a step-like recess in the massing of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) that requires upper [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) to be pushed back from the lower [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) from the street.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Street Step-Back) is to reduce the perceived bulk and mass of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) along [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s facing [public way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s, ensuring a height along the street that is appropriate to its neighboring context, while allowing for additional [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) height.

2. ##### Applicability


[Street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#), or a [facade modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) that face a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

3. ##### Standards


The following standards shall be met for a minimum of 85 percent of the [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#):

1. When the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) specifies a maximum number of [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without a step-back, all [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) above that maximum shall be stepped back from the [street-facing facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) by at least the minimum [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) depth, as specified by the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).

2. No [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall extend into a minimum [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) depth, except where allowed in Subsection E. (Exceptions) below.

3. [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s having a height less than the maximum [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) are not required to provide a [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.6.1.1.png.webp?itok=MQxxv5TU)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.6.1.1.png?itok=khqhMycG)
4. ##### Measurement


1. ###### Stories Without Street Step-back


      When the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) specifies a maximum number of [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without a step-back, that maximum is measured according to [Sec. 2C.4.3. (Height in Stories)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.3).

2. ###### Street Step-back Depth


      Minimum [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) depth is measured as the horizontal distance from the outermost edge of the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) with the topmost [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) to the outermost edge of the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of the stepped back [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#). [Street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) depth is required regardless of the provided or required [building setback](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.6.1.3.png.webp?itok=NaFnfB_8)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.6.1.3.png?itok=FIm9HqSU)
5. ##### Exceptions


The following are allowed to encroach beyond the [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) as listed below:



|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed Horizontal Encroachments |
| Architectural Details ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.a.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2’ |
| Roof Projections ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.b.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2.5’ |
| Unenclosed Structures ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.c.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5) \- [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.d.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 5’ |
| Enclosed Structures: Projecting ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.e.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2.5’ |
| Mechanical/Electrical Equipment ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.f.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5) \- [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.g.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 1.5’ |





|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed Vertical Encroachments |
| Mechanical/Electrical Equipment: Roof Mounted ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.b.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 5' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 3' |
| Architectural Elements ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.c.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 5' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 2' |
| Safety Barriers ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.e.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 4' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 0' |
| Unenclosed Structures ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.f.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 8 |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 2' |
| Flatwork ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.g.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2.5' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 1' |
| Vegetation ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.h.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | unlimited |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 1' |

6. ##### Relief


1. A reduced [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) depth of 20 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A reduced [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) greater than 20 percent may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

3. Increased [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without [street step-back](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 2C.6.2. District Boundary Height Transition

District boundary height transition is defined as a reduction in the maximum height of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) for a limited depth where [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) districts have substantially lower height allowances.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of this Section (District Boundary Height Transition) is to prevent looming impacts and reduce the perceived bulk and mass of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s along zoning district boundaries where maximum height standards change significantly.

2. ##### Applicability


1. [District boundary height transition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards apply to all [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) a zoning district that have a maximum height or [bonus height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) of less than or equal to the [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) district allowed height pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.2.D.1. (Abutting District Allowed Height)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.2) below, specified by the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).

2. All [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s located on an applicable [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall comply with [district boundary height transition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) standards unless listed as an exception in Subsection E. (Exceptions) below.
3. ##### Standards


1. Any portion of a [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) located above the maximum [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without height transition pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.2.D.2. (Stories Without Height Transition)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.2) below, shall be located no less than the minimum height transition depth pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.2.D.3 (Height Transition Depth)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.2) below, from any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) zoned with a district that specifies a maximum [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) height of less than or equal to the maximum [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) district allowed height pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.2.D.1. (Abutting District Allowed Height)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.2) below.

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.6.2.1.png.webp?itok=w8wgV5uk)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/2C.6.2.1.png?itok=7as6eO8v)

2. [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s are not required to provide a [district boundary height transition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) from [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) s.

3. No [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) or portion of a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) shall be located within the minimum height transition depth pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.2.D.3. (Height Transition Depth)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.2) below, except where allowed in Subsection E. (Exceptions).
4. ##### Measurement


1. ###### Abutting District Allowed Height


      [Abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) district allowed height is measured for every [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) which is zoned with a different zoning district than the subject [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#). The [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) district height is considered to be the maximum height or [bonus height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) allowed by the zoning district applied to the [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#).

2. ###### Stories Without Height Transition


      [Stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without height transition is measured according to [Sec. 2C.4.3. (Height in Stories)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.3).

3. ###### Height Transition Depth


      Height transition depth is measured as the horizontal distance from any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) zoned with a district that specifies a maximum [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) height of less than or equal to the maximum [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) district allowed height (Paragraph 1. (Abutting District Allowed Height) above) to the nearest point of any [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) located above the specified maximum [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without height transition pursuant to Paragraph 2. (Stories Without Height Transition) above.
5. ##### Exceptions


The following are allowed to encroach into the [district boundary height transition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) as listed below:



|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed Horizontal Encroachments |
| Architectural Details ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.a.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2’ |
| Roof Projections ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.b.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2.5’ |
| Unenclosed Structures ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.c.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5) \- [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.d.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 5’ |
| Enclosed Structures: Projecting ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.e.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2.5’ |
| Mechanical/Electrical Equipment ( [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.f.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5) \- [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.g.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 1.5’ |





|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| Allowed Vertical Encroachments |
| Mechanical/Electrical Equipment ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.b.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 5' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 3' |
| Architectural Elements ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.c.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 5' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 2' |
| Safety Barriers ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.e.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 4' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 0' |
| Unenclosed Structures ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.f.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 8 |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 2' |
| Flatwork ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.g.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | 2.5' |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 1' |
| Vegetation ( [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.h.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5)) |  |
| Encroachment (max) | unlimited |
| Setback from roof edge (min) | 1' |

6. ##### Relief


1. A reduced height transition depth of 20 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A reduced height transition depth may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

3. Increased [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) without height transition may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

# Article 3. Frontage

## Part 3A. Introduction

### Div. 3A.1. Orientation

#### Sec. 3A.1.1. Relationship to Zone String

A [zone string](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is composed of the following districts:

[![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.1.1.png.webp?itok=mFRS0VHi)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.1.1.png?itok=Tk5b-c_A)

The Frontage District is a separate and independent component of each zone.

#### Sec. 3A.1.2. How to Use Article 3. (Frontage)

1. ##### Identify the Applicable Frontage District


The second component in a [zone string](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is the Frontage District applied to a property.

2. ##### Determine Applicable Frontage District Standards


1. Frontage District standards are outlined in [Part 3B. (Frontage Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B). Each Frontage District page identifies the standards specific to that Frontage District.

2. Each Frontage rule category on a Frontage District page in [Part 3B. (Frontage Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) provides a reference to [Part 3C. (General Frontage Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C) or [Part 3D. (Character Frontage Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D), where the standards within that rule category are explained in detail. [Part 3D. (Character Frontage Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D) may reference [Part 3C. (General Frontage Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C) for standards that are common to both Character Frontage Districts and general Frontage Districts. Text in italics below a heading provides a definition of that heading.
       [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.2.1.png.webp?itok=CzUH3luK)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.2.1.png?itok=KdcMZOD9)

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.2.3.png.webp?itok=caE24SWD)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.2.3.png?itok=Waj5gopV)

#### Sec. 3A.1.3. Frontage District Diagrams

1. ##### General


Diagrams and illustrations are provided in this Article (Frontage) to assist users in understanding the purpose and requirements of the text and are not requirements but examples of compliance with a particular standard. In the event a conflict occurs between the text of this Article (Frontage) and any diagram or illustration, the text prevails.

2. ##### Lot Diagrams


[![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.1.png.webp?itok=UfFKWbEp)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.1.png?itok=QJ0yClAt)

1. ###### Lot Boundary


      This line represents the perimeter of the subject [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), serving as a reference for [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

2. ###### Build-To Zone


      This blue hatched shape represents the area on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), near the [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#). [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are required to occupy the [build-to zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) according to the minimum [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) specified by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

3. ###### Occupied Build-To Zone


      The part of the [build-to zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) with a blue background representing the width of the [build-to zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) applied toward [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) based on location of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s or location of [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s.

4. ###### Pedestrian Amenity Space


      This green shape represents the largest [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) applicable toward the [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) according to the maximum [pedestrian amenity allowance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) specified by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

5. ###### Building Footprint


      This shape represents the [building footprint](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) for the front portion of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) including the portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) occupying the [build-to zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), and serves as a reference for [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) that meets the build-to standards of the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).
3. ##### Facade Diagrams


[![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.3.png.webp?itok=49fAOi91)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.3.png?itok=czOGC8__)

1. ###### Lot Boundary


      This line represents the perimeter of the subject [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), serving as a reference for [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

2. ###### Pedestrian Amenity Space


      This paver-patterned shape represents the [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shown in the corresponding lot diagram, demonstrating the relationship between [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) requirements, and the standards of the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

3. ###### Story


      This volume represents a [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), serving as a reference for story height and [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards. The volume includes a line at the top and bottom of each [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), and an additional line near the top of each [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) indicating the bottom of a floor plate. The bottom of the floor plate is only depicted on the side of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

4. ###### Transparent Area


      This shape represents door and [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s on frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, serving as a reference for transparency standards.

5. ###### Active Wall Spacing


      This red-hatched shape represents one example measurement of [active wall spacing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), including the regulated [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) between one set of door or [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s. This shape does not represent all applicable [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s.

6. ###### Street-Facing Entrance


      This red outline represents a street-facing door openings, serving as a reference for [street-facing entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and [entrance spacing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards.
4. ##### Character Frontage Diagrams


[Character Frontage Districts (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) include a wider variety of diagrams, but use the same approach to representation established by the lot diagrams and facade diagrams. In addition to the elements depicted in [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and frontage diagrams, Character Frontage Districts represent articulation techniques, [focal entry feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, and exterior materials.

1. ###### Articulation Techniques


      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.5.png.webp?itok=UQkqMlHt)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.5.png?itok=OkalAjJG)

      Articulation standards often include a variety of regulatory elements, for example, [vertical band articulation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and [horizontal band articulation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) layers, and [articulating element](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s. While [articulating element](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are not depicted in Character Frontage District diagrams, [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) layers are represented with a red outline and banding is represented using a black outline around a translucent white shape.

2. ###### Focal Entry Features and Exterior Materials


      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.7.png.webp?itok=rCgiOTHq)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3A.1.3.7.png?itok=P2cr7AS2)

      1. [Focal entry feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are represented by a dashed red outline surrounding the area on a [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) that meets the [focal entry feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) requirements in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

      2. Primary and secondary exterior materials are represented using a variety of colors and textures to represent one or more of the exterior materials allowed by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

#### Sec. 3A.1.4. Frontage District Naming Convention

Frontage District names have two components: frontage category and variation number.

1. ##### Frontage Category


The first component of each Frontage District, frontage categories group all districts with similar characteristics, and are organized as follows:

1. Drive

2. Multi-Unit

3. General

4. Shopfront

5. Market

6. Large Format

7. Warehouse

8. Dual

9. Character
2. ##### Variation Number


The second component of each Frontage District, a variation number represents the order that the Frontage District falls within this Article (Frontage).


### Div. 3A.2. General Rules

#### Sec. 3A.2.1. Frontage

This Article (Frontage) regulates the portions of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and exterior [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s that impact the public realm. [Frontage Districts (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) help ensure that [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s respond to the public realm in a contextually appropriate manner. Frontage Districts range from minimal standards (for example Warehouse Frontages) to a robust set of standards (for example Shopfront Frontages) which require [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s to support a high-quality public realm that is active, comfortable, safe, and visually interesting, with strong connections between the public realm and [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s inside [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s.

#### Sec. 3A.2.2. Frontage Applicability

1. ##### General


All [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s filed after the effective date of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) must comply with the Frontage District standards and rules in this Article (Frontage), as further specified in the applicability statement of each Section in [Part 3C. (General Frontage Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C) and [Part 3D. (Character Frontage Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D). For vested rights, see [Sec. 1.4.5. (Vested Rights)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.4.5), and for continuance of existing development, see [Sec. 1.4.6. (Continuance of Existing Development)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.4.6).

2. ##### Applicable Components of Lots, Buildings, & Structures


1. ###### General


      Frontage standards apply only to the applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, portions of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), and [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) depth, as specified in Paragraph 3. (Frontage Applicable Facades) below. ## Part 3B. Frontage Districts

### Div. 3B.1. Drive Frontage Districts

Drive Frontages control the location of vehicular access, require planted [front yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, and provide flexible provisions for privacy through a combination of setbacks and frontage yard fence & wall standards.

\[Reserved\].

### Div. 3B.2. Multi-Unit Frontage Districts

Multi-Unit Frontages require higher [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), low transparency, and frequent [entrance spacing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#). This allows for greater privacy for tenants located on the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) while retaining an interplay between the private and public realms. Frequent entrances activate the public realm with pedestrian activity and visual interest.

### Div. 3B.4. Shopfront Frontage Districts

Shopfront Frontages require high [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, high levels of transparency, frequent [entrance spacing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), and [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) at or near [sidewalk grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#). This promotes a legible [street wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and activates the public realm with pedestrian activity and visual interest. The [at-grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [ground floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) allows for an increased connection between the interior uses and the pedestrian space.

### Div. 3B.9. Character Frontage Districts

Character Frontages provide standards for facade articulation, [entry feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) design, siding materials, and [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), in order to reinforce the prevailing architectural characteristics of the city’s historically and culturally significant neighborhoods and districts.

#### Sec. 3B.9.1. Historic Core (CHC1)

|     |
| --- |
| ##### A.Intent |
| The Historic Core Character Frontage ("Historic Core") ensures new development contributes to and reinforces the established architectural character of an urban historic core established in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, while supporting creative design and contemporary construction practices. Key architectural characteristics of the Historic Core include grand entrances adorned with pillars and archways, highly decorative [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s that clearly articulate the base, middle and top layers of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), deeply recessed windows, and roofs with prominent cornices. [Building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s in the Historic Core adhere to a well-defined [street wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) with high [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) activation. |
