### Div. 3D.9. Transparency

#### Sec. 3D.9.1. Ground Story

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Ground Story) is to ensure [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are designed with [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s that contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or district.

2. ##### Applicability


[Ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) when the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) requires [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency on [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.B.3. (Frontage Applicable Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2) located on the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.B.4. (Frontage Applicable Building Depth)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2).

3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      1. ###### Standards


         1. Frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s located on the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shall provide no less than the minimum transparency specified in the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

         2. Frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s located on the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shall provide no more than the maximum transparency specified in the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

         3. All [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shall meet the standards of [Sec. 3C.4.1.C. (Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.1).
      2. ###### Measurement


         For [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) measurement, see [Sec. 3C.4.1.D. (Measurement)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.1).
2. ###### Active Wall Spacing


      See [Sec. 3C.4.2. (Active Wall Spacing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.2).

3. ###### Window Recession


      The depth that a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is set back from the surrounding [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

      1. ###### Standards


         All [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s on applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall be recessed at a minimum depth as specified in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

      2. ###### Measurement


         [Window recession](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) depth is measured inward from the immediately surrounding [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) surface, exclusive of trim or accessory projecting [architectural detail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s, to the outermost element of the [window assembly](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).
4. ###### Bulkhead


      A [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) located beneath a display window on the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) that elevates a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) above the exterior [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and the interior finished floor surface.

      1. ###### Standards


         1. When listed as "required" in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), all [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s located on applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall be located between 18 and 30 inches above the finished floor of the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

         2. [Ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s located entirely above another [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) may be located greater than 30 inches from the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finished floor provided that no portion of the opening extends beyond the width of the lower [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

            [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.9.1.1.png.webp?itok=_wg6W1RD)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.9.1.1.png?itok=tzayLUfX)
      2. ###### Measurement


         [Bulkhead](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are measured as "provided" or "not provided" based on the compliance of all applicable [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s with the standards above.
5. ###### Symmetrical Lite Pattern


      Window panes that are arranged or designed so that the left-side of the [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) composition is a mirror image of the right-side of the [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) composition.

      1. ###### Standards


         When listed as “required" in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), all [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s provided on applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall meet the following standards:

         1. [Divided-lite](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and [simulated divided-lite](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall have a composition of muntins or grills that display reflective symmetry.

         2. Operable [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall have sashes that are reflectively symmetrical.

         3. [Window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) assemblies sharing a [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shall be composed in a way that reflective symmetry is displayed over the entirety of the [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).
      2. ###### Measurement


         In meeting [symmetrical lite pattern](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards, if a vertical line can be drawn through the [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), and the pattern and shape on both sides of the line appear approximately identical, the [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) or [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are considered in compliance with the [symmetrical lite pattern](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standard.

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.9.1.3.png.webp?itok=_nEi-Ef3)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.9.1.3.png?itok=crvHu5wf)
6. ###### Horizontal Sliding Windows


      1. ###### Standards


         When listed as "prohibited" in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s provided on applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall not include sashes that operate left to right or right to left.

      2. ###### Measurement


         Horizontal sliding [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are identified as either present or absent.
7. ###### Vinyl Windows


      1. ###### Standards


         1. When listed as "prohibited" in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), window assemblies provided on applicable facades shall not contain frames, sashes, rails, styles, muntins, mullions, or grills with a vinyl exterior finish.

         2. Other accessory [window assembly](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) components may be finished with vinyl products.
      2. ###### Measurement


         Vinyl windows are identified as either present or absent.
4. ##### Exceptions


[Ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency standards do not apply to [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s unless the applied development standards district requires the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) to be wrapped, see [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B).

5. ##### Relief


1. Up to a 15 percent increase to the total allowed [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A deviation from ground story transparency dimensional standard up to 15 percent may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. Deviation from any ground story transparency standard may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 3D.9.2. Upper Stories

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Upper Stories) is to ensure [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are designed with [upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s that contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or districts.

2. ##### Applicability


[Upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) when the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) requires [upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency on [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.B.3. (Frontage Applicable Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2) and [Sec. 3A.2.2.B.4. (Frontage Applicable Building Depth)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2).

3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      1. ###### Standards


         1. Applicable [upper story facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall provide at least the minimum transparency specified in the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

         2. Applicable [upper story facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall provide no more than the maximum transparency specified in the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

         3. All [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shall meet the standards of [Sec. 3C.4.1.C. (Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.1).
      2. ###### Measurement


         See [Sec. 3C.4.1.D.2. (Upper Stories)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.1).
2. ###### Window Recession


      See [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.3. (Window Recession)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1).

3. ###### Symmetrical Lite Pattern


      See [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.5. (Symmetrical Lite Pattern)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1).

4. ###### Sill


      The bottommost horizontal exterior surface of a [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) including a ledge or other [architectural detail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) that projects from the surrounding [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

      1. ###### Standards


         1. When required by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), all [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s provided on applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall include a [sill](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), ledge or comparable [architectural detail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) located at the bottommost exterior surface of a [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

         2. Required [sill](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall project a minimum of one inch beyond the immediately surrounding [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

         3. Required [sill](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall have a width of no less than the [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).
      2. ###### Measurement


         [Sill](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are measured as "provided" or "not provided" based on the compliance of all applicable [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s with the standards of subparagraph a above.
5. ###### Horizontal Sliding Windows


      See [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.6. (Horizontal Sliding Windows)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1).

6. ###### Vinyl Windows


      See [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.7. (Vinyl Windows)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1).
4. ##### Exceptions


[Upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency standards do not apply to [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s unless the applied [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B) requires the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) to be wrapped.

5. ##### Relief


1. Up to a 15 percent increase in the total allowed [upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A deviation up to 15 percent from [upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency dimensional standards may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. Deviation from any [upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) transparency standard may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

### Div. 3D.10. Exterior Materials

#### Sec. 3D.10.1. Principal Material Coverage

Principal material coverage is defined as the building products used as the primary [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finish materials of the exterior [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Principal Material Coverage) is to visually unify the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) with a dominant material and ensure that [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are finished with materials that contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or districts.

2. ##### Applicability


[Principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#). When the [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards apply, the standards apply to [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.B.3. (Frontage Applicable Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2) and any build-to [applicable story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) as specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9), and any portion of the frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) located above the last provided [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) where the number of [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) provided for any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is less than the specified build-to applicable [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      1. The total percentage of applicable [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finished in a primary material shall be no less than the minimum [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

      2. Only exterior material options specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) may be used as a primary material.

      3. Only one primary material may used to meet the [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standard.
2. ###### Exterior Material Options


      1. For exterior material options standards, see [Sec. 3D.10.3. (Exterior Material Options)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.10.3).
4. ##### Measurement


1. [Principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is calculated for each [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) separately.

2. The [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) percentage is the [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) covered in a principal material divided by the total applicable [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

3. The [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is measured as compliant or non-compliant based on whether it meets the standards and definition of one of the allowed exterior material options specified by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).
5. ##### Exceptions


[Principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards do not apply to [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s nor door openings.

6. ##### Relief


1. Up to a 10 percent reduction to the total required [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finished in an allowed primary exterior material may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. Deviation from any [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standard may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 3D.10.2. Accessory Material Coverage

Accessory material coverage is defined as the building products used as an [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finish material to accent or support the principal material.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Accessory Material Coverage) is to visually unify the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) with a consistent material palette and ensure that [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are finished with materials that contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or districts.

2. ##### Applicability


1. [Accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards shall apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#). When the [accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards apply, the standards apply to any [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.B.3. (Frontage Applicable Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2) and any build-to [applicable story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) as specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3.9), and any portion of the frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) located above the last provided [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) where the number of [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) provided for any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is less than the specified build-to applicable [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

2. All exterior materials cumulatively covering between five percent and 30 percent of the total applicable [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) are considered an accessory material and shall comply with all [accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), exterior material options, and number of accessory material standards.
3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      1. The total percentage of applicable [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finished in an accessory material shall not exceed the maximum [accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

      2. Only exterior material options specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) may be used as an accessory material.
2. ###### Exterior Material Options


      For exterior material options standards, see [Sec. 3D.10.3. (Exterior Material Options).](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.10.3)

3. ###### Number of Accessory Materials


      Individual accessory materials may not exceed the maximum number of accessory materials specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).
4. ##### Measurement


1. [Accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is calculated for each [building width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) separately.

2. [Accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) percentage is the [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) covered in the accessory material product divided by the total applicable [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

3. [Accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is measured as compliant or non-compliant based on whether it meets the standards and definition of one of the exterior material options specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).
5. ##### Exceptions


[Accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards do not apply to [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s nor door openings.

6. ##### Relief


1. Up to a 10 percent increase in the total allowed [facade area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finished in a secondary exterior material may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. Deviation from any accessory material standard may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 3D.10.3. Exterior Material Options

Exterior material options is defined as building products allowed for use as primary or accessory [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) finish material.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section is to ensure that [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s are finished with materials that contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or districts.

2. ##### Applicability


[Exterior material option](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s standards apply to all exterior materials provided and shall comply with [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) or [accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards as specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      Proposed principal and accessory materials shall meet all standards and definitions of one of the exterior material options specified by the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) to comply with [principal material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and [accessory material coverage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards.

2. ###### Exterior Material Options








      |     |
      | --- |
      | a.Brickwork |
      | Courses of rectangular masonry units made of hardened clay, laid with mortar exposed between bricks. Examples include solid brick construction, brick veneer and thin brick veneer. Other products required for installation that are visually incidental to the brick are also included. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.1.png.webp?itok=mRAogse_)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.1.png?itok=9dbAfWN9) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with a human scale, durability, and a connection to local history. The profile of brickwork creates a pattern of channels along the mortar beds and perpends providing shadow line effects and texture reflecting the scale of the individual brick units. The size of the brick units are of a commonly recognized scale related to its manual assembly which naturally helps observers relate to the overall scale of the structure and recognize the building as a result of tangible human activities rather than machined or synthetic installations. Brick assemblies provide lasting durability against weather and wear, reducing maintenance demands. Used as an exterior building material in some of Los Angeles most treasured historic buildings, brickwork connects observers to local history. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | i.Individual brick units shall have a height of between 1.5 and 8 inches. <br>ii.Individual brick units shall have a width of between 3.5 and 16 inches. |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | b.Stonework |
      | Stacked rocks quarried and worked into a specific size and shape for use as a building material. Solid stone includes mortar and other products required for installation that are visually incidental to the stone product. Examples include solid stone construction, stone veneer, and thin stone veneer. Solid stone excludes heavy aggregate concrete, terrazzo, engineered stone products, and comparable materials. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.3.png.webp?itok=Ool-Yebk)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.3.png?itok=376Tml88) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with a human scale, durability, and a connection to nature and local history. The profile of stonework provides dynamic shadow line effects relating to the scale of individual stones, helping observers to relate to the overall scale of the structure. The organic textures and deep natural colors of exposed stone faces provide observers with a connection to nature. Solid stone assemblies provide lasting durability against weather and wear, reducing maintenance demands. Used as an exterior building material in some of Los Angeles most treasured historic buildings, solid stone assemblies connect observers to local history. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | n/a |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | c.Concrete |
      | A cement based product either poured-in-place or pre-cast in a form or mold. Concrete includes engineered masonry products set in resin or cement such as terrazzo, terracotta, CMU, breeze block, and exposed columns and beams. Other products required for installation that are visually incidental to the concrete product are also included. Concrete excludes fiber cement products, brick, EFIS, and stucco. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.5.png.webp?itok=rQi3qZ5t)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.5.png?itok=f4wjCGEu) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with the lasting durability and a sense of weight and permanence through use of concrete. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | Not applicable |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | d.Metal |
      | Metal products designed and intended for architectural purposes. Examples include exposed structural steel, architectural metal panels, and decorative metal products. Other products required for installation that are visually incidental to the metal product are also included. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.7.png.webp?itok=ncvApxlX)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.7.png?itok=ok3nlgVt) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with the lasting durability and sense of permanence through use of metal. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | Not applicable |











      |     |
      | --- |
      | e.Wood |
      | Tree-based products milled into a particular shape and size for use as an exterior building material. Examples include wood panels, structural lumber such as cross laminated timber and glulam beams, plank siding, and shingles. Wood excludes products with exposed faces composed substantially of wood chips, particles, and fibers. Examples include structural composite lumber like PSL, LSL, and OSL, and composite panel products like OSB, fiberboard, and particleboard. Wood also excludes faux-wood products such as vinyl, aluminum, and fiber cement siding. Other products required for installation that are visually incidental to the wood product are also included. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.9.png.webp?itok=2FYu5N_1)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.9.png?itok=KWGUoyrT) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with a connection to nature and local history through use of wood. The organic patterns and warm natural colors of exposed wood provide observers with a connection to nature. Used as an exterior building material in some of Los Angeles most treasured historic buildings, wood products connect observers to local history. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | Not applicable |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | f.Glazed Tile |
      | Ceramic tile having porcelain or natural clay body, glazed for surfacing walls, typically attached to an exterior wall with mortar and finished by filling joints between tiles with a cement- or resin-based grout product. Examples include small or large format tile and structural facing tile. Other products required for installation that are visually subordinate to the tile product are also allowed. Glazed tile excludes terracotta and other non-ceramic tile products. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.11.png.webp?itok=aTpHabTV)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.11.png?itok=zW6pVPAO) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with a human scale, durability, and a connection to local history. The profile of glazed tile assemblies provides a regular pattern of channels along grout joints, creating shadow line effects and texture reflecting the scale of the individual tile units. Glazed tile assemblies provide lasting durability against weather and wear, reducing maintenance demands. Used as an exterior building material in some of Los Angeles most treasured historic buildings, glazed tile assemblies connect observers to local history with their familiar luster and sheen. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | Not applicable |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | g.Horizontal Plank Siding |
      | Courses of long, thin horizontal boards, often overlapping or interlocking horizontally but also including open joint systems. Horizontal plank siding includes clapboard, bevel, lap, weatherboard, shiplap, and rain screen siding and may be composed of a wide range of materials including wood, fiber cement products, and vinyl. Horizontal plank cladding excludes textured panel products with unit sizes exceeding 10 inches in height regardless of the pattern or texture. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.13.png.webp?itok=_5j45BwC)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.13.png?itok=B2cX45YZ) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide a human scale to buildings. The profile of the siding assembly creates a pattern of horizontal channels providing deep shadow line effects and texture reflecting the scale of the individual board units. The scale of the board units are of a commonly recognized scale related to its manual assembly which naturally helps observers to understand and relate to the overall scale of the structure and recognize the building as a result of tangible human activities rather than machined or synthetic installations. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | i.Individual board units shall have a height of between 2 and 10 inches. <br>ii.Overlapping or interlocking board units may have a height greater than 10 inches provided no board unit is exposed for a continuous height of more than 10 inches. <br>iii.Open joint systems shall not provide a gap greater than 3/4" between board units. |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | h.Vertical Plank Siding |
      | Courses of long, thin vertical boards, often overlapping or interlocking vertically but also including open joint systems. Vertical plank siding includes, board and batten, tongue and groove, shiplap, and rain screen siding and may be composed of a wide range of materials including wood, fiber cement products, and vinyl. Vertical plank cladding excludes textured panel products with continuous reveal dimensions greater than 16 inches in width regardless of the pattern or texture. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.15.png.webp?itok=eTduwHOF)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.15.png?itok=jPwPRA_A) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide a human scale to buildings. The profile of the siding assembly creates a pattern of vertical channels providing deep shadow line effects and texture reflecting the scale of the individual board units. The scale of the board units are of a commonly recognized scale related to its manual assembly which naturally helps observers to understand and relate to the overall scale of the structure and recognize the building as a result of tangible human activities rather than machined or synthetic installations. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | i.Individual board units shall have a width of between 1 and 16 inches. <br>ii.Overlapping or interlocking board units may have a width greater than 16 inches provided no board unit is exposed for a continuous width of more than 16 inches. <br>iii.Open joint systems shall not provide a gap greater than 3/4" between board units. |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | i.Shingle Siding |
      | Courses of short, thin building materials, overlapping horizontally. Shingle siding includes square, round, half-cove, and hexagon, shaped shingles and be composed of a wide range of materials including cedar, cementitious fiberboard, and vinyl. Shingle siding excludes asphalt roofing shingles and textured panel products with continuous reveal dimensions greater than 24 inches in width or 12 inches in height regardless of the pattern or texture. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.17.png.webp?itok=mwC0fjNE)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.17.png?itok=f4durTP0) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide a human scale to buildings. The profile of the shingle assembly creates a pattern of vertical and horizontal channels providing deep shadow line effects and texture reflecting the scale of the individual shingle units. The scale of the shingle units are of a commonly recognized scale related to its manual assembly which naturally helps observers to understand and relate to the overall scale of the structure and recognize the building as a result of tangible human activities rather than machined or synthetic installations. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | i.Individual shingle units shall have a width of between 2 and 24 inches. <br>ii.Individual shingle units shall have a height of between 2 and 12 inches. <br>iii.Shingle units may have a width greater than 24 inches or a height greater than 12 inches provided no individual shingle is exposed for a continuous width of more than 24 inches or a continuous height of more than 12 inches. |







      |     |
      | --- |
      | j.Stucco |
      | A building material composed primarily of Portland cement, finely ground limestone, sand and water, applied directly onto a building over a reinforcing base mesh. Stucco excludes textured panel products and synthetic stucco such as EIFS, elastomeric stucco, and acrylic stucco. |
      | [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.19.png.webp?itok=b8ZIU4XB)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.19.png?itok=GJUyyDJL) |
      | Intent |
      | To provide structures with durability and a connection local history. Stucco provides lasting durability against weather and wear, reducing maintenance demands. Used as an exterior building material in some of Los Angeles most treasured historic buildings, stucco connects observers to local history. |
      | Dimensional Standards |
      | Not applicable |
4. ##### Measurement


1. The height of individual board, brick, or shingle unit is measured as the greatest dimension from one end of the unit to the opposite end of the unit, measured vertically and based on the proposed installation pattern.

2. The width of individual board, brick, or shingle unit is measured as the greatest dimension from one end of the unit to the opposite end of the unit, measured horizontally and based on the proposed installation pattern.

3. Exposed width is measured as the largest horizontal dimension of a board or shingle unit that is uninterrupted by either, another board or shingle covering the first unit, or a gap or break in the board or shingle unit, for the full height of the unit.

4. Exposed height is measured as the largest vertical dimension of a board or shingle unit that is uninterrupted by either, another board or shingle covering the first unit, or a gap or break in the board or shingle unit, for the full height of the unit.

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.21.png.webp?itok=tKbJIrBv)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/3D.10.3.21.png?itok=P4Hi3uIU)

5. Gap between board units is measured as the distance between board units at the widest point.
5. ##### Relief


1. Deviation from [exterior material option](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.1. (Alternative Compliance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.1).

2. Up to a 10 percent modification to any [exterior material option](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) dimensional standard may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. Deviation from any [exterior material option](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standard may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

### Div. 3D.11. Roof Design

#### Sec. 3D.11.1. Roof Form

Roof form is defined as the shape of the external upper covering of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), including the frame for supporting the roofing.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Roof Design) is to ensure that [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) forms contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or districts.

2. ##### Applicability


1. [Roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) when the applied [Character Frontage District (Div. 3B.9.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9) requires a primary [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) on any [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#)- [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s.

2. A minimum of 70 percent of the total roof area of each applicable [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) shall meet [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standards, measured horizontally.
3. ##### Standards


1. ###### General


      All [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s shall have a [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) listed as a [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) option in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

2. ###### Roof Form Options


      1. ###### Flat


         A roof with a maximum pitch of 2:12 (two inch of vertical rise for every 12 inches of horizontal span) or less. Flat [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s include roofs with parapets up to six feet in height.
4. ##### Measurement


1. Roof pitch is measured by calculating a roof's vertical rise in inches divided by a foot of its horizontal span and is represented as a ratio.

2. [Roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) is measured as compliant or non-compliant based on whether it meets the standards and definition of one of the [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) options allowed by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).
5. ##### Relief


1. Up to a 10 percent reduction in the total required roof area having an allowed [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A deviation from [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) dimensional standard up to 10 percent may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. Deviation from any [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) standard may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 3D.11.2. Roof Materials

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Roof Materials) is to ensure that a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#)'s roof finishing materials contribute to the established architectural character of surrounding neighborhoods or districts.

2. ##### Applicability


This Section (Roof Materials) applies to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#). When roof materials standards apply, the standards apply to all portions of a required primary [roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) pursuant to [Sec. 3D.11.1. (Roof Form)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.11.1) on any [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#)- [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#).

3. ##### Standards


Only roof materials specified by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) shall be used to finish an applicable roof.

4. ##### Measurement


Roof materials are measured as compliant or non-compliant based on whether all applicable roofs meet the roof materials standards.

5. ##### Exceptions


Roof material standards do not apply to [accessory roof form](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#) s.

6. ##### Relief


1. Up to a 10 percent reduction in the total required roof area finished of an allowed roof material may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. Deviation from roof materials standards may be granted as a variance in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

# Article 4. Development Standards

## Part 4A. Introduction

### Div. 4A.1. Orientation

#### Sec. 4A.1.1. Relationship to Zone String

A [zone string](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is composed of the following districts:

[![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4A.1.1.1.png.webp?itok=3pQmXMdM)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4A.1.1.1.png?itok=jVJB5NXC)

The Development Standards District is a separate and independent component of each zone.

#### Sec. 4A.1.2. How to Use Article 4. (Development Standards)

1. ##### Identify the Applicable Development Standards District


The third component in a zone string is the Development Standards District applied to a property.

2. ##### Development Standards District Regulations


1. Development Standards District regulations are located in [Part 4B. (Development Standards Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B). Each Development Standards District page identifies the requirements specific to that Development Standards District.

2. Each standard or [standards package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) on a Development Standards District page in [Part 4B. (Development Standards Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B) provides a reference to [Part 4C. (Development Standards Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C) where the standard or [standards package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is explained in detail. Additionally, [Part 4C. (Development Standards Rules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C) includes general standards that apply across all Development Standards Districts. Text in italics below a heading provides a definition of that heading

      [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4A.1.2.1.png.webp?itok=zZiUkQ0C)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4A.1.2.1.png?itok=4__7_BNA)

#### Sec. 4A.1.3. Development Standards District Naming Convention

All Development Standards District names are identified as a number. All Development Standards Districts are numbered in the order they fall within this Article (Development Standards).

### Div. 4A.2. General Rules

#### Sec. 4A.2.1. Development Standards

This Article (Development Standards) regulates [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design including location and [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) characteristics, such as [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), parking, landscape, environmental features and other [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) features. Development Standards Districts consist of a combination of regulations that are appropriate to a variety of contexts ranging from auto-oriented to pedestrian-oriented.

#### Sec. 4A.2.2. Development Standards Applicability

1. ##### General


All [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s filed after the effective date of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) shall comply with the Development Standards Districts and rules in this Article (Development Standards), as further specified in the applicability statement of each Section in [Part 4C. (Development Standards Rules](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C)). For vested rights, see [Sec. 1.4.5. (Vested Rights)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.4.5), and for continuance of existing development, see [Sec. 1.4.6. (Continuance of Existing Development)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.4.6).

2. ##### Applicable Components of Lots and Structures


Unless otherwise provided, [Development Standards Districts (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B) apply to all portions of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and all [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

3. ##### Nonconformities


[Article 12. (Nonconformities)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12) may provide relief from the requirements of this Article (Development Standards) for existing [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) improvements, [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, and [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that conformed to the zoning regulations at the time they were established, but do not conform to current district standards or [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) permissions. All [project activities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall conform with Development Standards District regulations unless otherwise specified by [Div. 12.4. (Development Standards Exceptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12#12.4).

#### Sec. 4B.2.2. Development Standards District 5

1. ##### Intent


Development Standards District 5 prioritizes the pedestrian experience. [Pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standards facilitate pedestrian circulation by improving [pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from the public realm to the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s through frequent, direct and convenient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to [building entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s. Parking for automobiles is not mandated, contributing to a dynamic and walkable environment. When parking is provided, it must meet high design standards to ensure pedestrian mobility, safety, and comfort are not hindered. [On-site sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are sized and located to support a pedestrian-oriented public realm.

## Part 4C. Development Standards Rules

### Div. 4C.1. Pedestrian Access

#### Sec. 4C.1.1. Pedestrian Access Packages

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Pedestrian Access Packages) is to promote walkability, improve [pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from the public realm to the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, ensure that required entrances are conveniently and effectively accessible to pedestrians, and activate the public realm with [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) points and improve convenient pedestrian circulation through large [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s to an extent and [frequency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) appropriate to the context.

2. ##### Applicability


1. [Pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) package standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [site modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), and are applied to a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) as determined by the [pedestrian access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) assigned by the Development Standards District (Part 4B) as provided below:

      1. 'Site access' standards only apply to [street-facing entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s required by the applicable [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) and all [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

      2. 'Through Access' standards only apply when the [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is greater than 30,000 feet, or the [lot width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is equal to or greater than the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spacing minimum of the [pedestrian access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) assigned by the applicable [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B), or the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is a [through lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [abut](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s either a [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), [public access easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) zoned with an [Open Space Use District (Div. 5B.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.1) on at least two opposing [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, or any of the above [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) characteristics combined.

2. ##### Site Access


      1. ##### Pedestrian Accessway Type


         1. ##### Linked


            Where the applicable [pedestrian access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specifies "linked" as the [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) type, all required [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall meet the following standards:

            1. Be a minimum width of four feet.

            2. Connect from the sidewalk, or other publicly accessible pedestrian facility located along the applicable [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), to a [street-facing entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) required by the applicable [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) within the [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

            3. Be physically separated from and uninterrupted by [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s except where required to cross a [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) crossings shall be no wider than the minimum [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width specified in [Sec. 4C.4.3.C.13. (Parking Bay Dimensions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.3). Physical separation methods may include, curbs of no less than four inches in height or [bollard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, walls, raised planters or similar containment methods, no less than 30 inches in height and separated by no more than five feet.

               [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.9.png.webp?itok=iMtB31LM)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.9.png?itok=wnn-aJ1A)

            4. Where a [retaining wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), open drainage, or similar obstacle interrupts a required [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is designed to facilitate passage through or over the obstacle.

               [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.11.png.webp?itok=CcHZN6PK)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.11.png?itok=aIXIMFLk)
         2. ##### Direct


            Where the applicable pedestrian package specifies "direct" as the [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) type, all required [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall meet the following standards:

            1. Comply with Sub-subparagraph i. (Linked) above.

            2. A minimum of one [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is provided to each [street-facing entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) required by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).

            3. All portions of the [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) including the connection to the [public sidewalk](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is within 25 feet of the center of the [street-facing entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), measured parallel to the [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

               [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.13.png.webp?itok=t5RWKuC5)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.13.png?itok=aWvRpDEl)
      2. ##### Pedestrian Accessway Spacing


         A required [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall not be separated from another [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or the end of a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by a [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) greater than the maximum allowed [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spacing standard in the applicable [pedestrian access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      3. ##### Distance from Street Intersection


         A [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall not be separated from a street intersection by a [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) greater than the maximum allowed [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from intersection standard in the applicable [pedestrian access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
3. ##### Through Access


      1. ##### Pedestrian Passageway


         When the applicable [pedestrian access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) indicates a [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is required, a [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) meeting the following requirements shall be provided:

         01. [Uncovered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) portions having a minimum width of 15 feet and [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) portions having a minimum width of 25 feet.

         02. A minimum [clear height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) portions be 15 feet, with the exception of required [luminaire](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

             [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.15.png.webp?itok=6c-tqWX7)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.15.png?itok=eec_LcOY)

         03. For [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s having a [clear height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of less than 30 feet for any portion of its required minimum width, a maximum of 125 linear feet of the total passageway may be [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for any portion of the required minimum width, measured cumulatively.

             [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.17.png.webp?itok=fAAlyuH3)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.17.png?itok=gNP5rzH8)

         04. For [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s having a [clear height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of 30 to 45 feet for all portions of its required width, a maximum of 350 linear feet of the total passageway may be [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for any portion of the required minimum width, measured cumulatively.

         05. For [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s having a [clear height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) greater than 45 feet for all portions of its required minimum width, up to 100 percent of the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may be [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         06. Shall connect from the [public sidewalk](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) on the [primary street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to either the [public sidewalk](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), other [public way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) the [opposing lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) zoned with an [Open Space Use District (Div. 5B.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.1)

         07. The centerline of any portion of the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be located within 75 feet of centerline of the sidewalk access point on the [primary street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), measured perpendicular to the [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         08. Shall take access from the sidewalk along the [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) at least 125 feet from a street intersection.

             [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.19.png.webp?itok=TPB0UfNU)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.19.png?itok=UCNGd63n)

         09. Shall be physically separated from and uninterrupted by [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s except where required to cross a [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) crossings shall be no wider than the minimum [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width specified in [Sec. 4C.4.3.C.13. (Parking Bay Dimensions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.3). Physical separation methods may include curbs of no less than four inches in height, [bollard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, walls, raised planters, or similar containment methods, no less than 30 inches in height and separated by no more than five feet.

         10. The surface of the passageway shall be illuminated in accordance with [Sec. 4C.10.1.C.3. (Pedestrian-Oriented Lighting)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.10.1).

         11. No gates or other barriers may [block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) any portion of a [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from [pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from sunset to sunrise or during operational hours, whichever is longer, and a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be posted at every public entrance to the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with the standards in [Sec. 2C.3.4.C.10.b. (Publicly Accessible)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.4).

         12. Each [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall meet the side street transparency and entrance standards of the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B). For the purposes of determining which [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be considered as [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be considered a [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and measured in accordance with [Sec. 14.2.6.C. (Pedestrian Amenity Space & Public Amenity Space-Facing Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.6).

         13. A [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may count toward the amenity requirements, pursuant to [Div. 2C.3. (Amenity)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3), of the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) where the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) meets the specifications of an eligible amenity space type specified within [Div. 2C.3. (Amenity)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3).
4. ##### Pedestrian Passageway Spacing


      1. A required [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall not be separated from another [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or the end of a [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by a [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) greater than the maximum allowed [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spacing specified by the applied [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B).

      2. The maximum [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spacing requirement shall be met for each [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) individually and is not applicable to [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.
4. ##### Measurement


1. ##### General


      For measurement of the [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), see [Sec. 14.2.12. (Lot Line Determination)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12).

2. ##### Pedestrian Accessways


      1. [Pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spacing is measured as the distance between two [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, following the geometry of the [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). Measurement shall be taken from the edge of one accessway where the accessway meets the public sidewalk, to the nearest edge of the nearest accessway located on the same [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.21.png.webp?itok=f52cRWUP)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.21.png?itok=USoaUKJN)

      2. [Pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from a street intersection is measured from the intersection of two [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s to the nearest edge of a [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) measured along the applicable [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.23.png.webp?itok=eLnK8hTe)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.23.png?itok=zzzU0t7C)

      3. [Pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width is measured from one edge of the accessway perpendicularly to the opposite edge.

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.25.png.webp?itok=UZ3JGXaa)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.25.png?itok=G9zV9dJR)
3. ##### Pedestrian Passageways


      1. The cumulative linear feet of [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is measured along the centerline of the minimum [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width. Where any portion of the minimum width of the [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is not [open to the sky](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the length of the centerline having [covered area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) perpendicular to it counts as [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) length. The total [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) length is calculated as the sum of all portions of the centerline considered [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.27.png.webp?itok=YGnzh47p)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.27.png?itok=YJEXOZNW)

      2. [Pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from street intersection is measured from the point where two [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s intersect [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to a street corner to the nearest edge of a required [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), measured along the [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.29.png.webp?itok=yPv5GUjm)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.29.png?itok=To5v_S0W)

      3. [Pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spacing is measured as the horizontal [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) between designated [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, measured along the applicable [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) pursuant to [Sec. 4C.1.1.C.3.a.vi. (Pedestrian Passageway)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.1.1) above from the edge of one [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to the nearest edge of the next [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the end of a [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or street intersection, whichever is closest.

         [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.31.png.webp?itok=wqn5UQD5)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.1.1.31.png?itok=9nUhFrl4)
5. ##### Exceptions


[Site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) access standards do not apply to non-required entrances.

6. ##### Relief


1. Alternative Compliance from any [pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standard may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.1. (Alternative Compliance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.1).

2. A deviation from any [pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) dimensional standard of 10 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. A deviation from any [pedestrian access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standard may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 4C.1.2. Pedestrian Bridges & Tunnels

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Pedestrian Bridges & Tunnels) is to limit the creation of new pedestrian bridges and tunnels that create an inhospitable environment for pedestrians at the street level, and to ensure that, in the event pedestrian bridges and tunnels are deemed necessary to the feasibility of a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), that they positively contribute to the public realm and general pedestrian safety.

2. ##### Applicability


Pedestrian bridges and tunnels standards are applicable to the [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of pedestrian bridges and pedestrian tunnels.

3. ##### Standards


1. ##### General


      The construction and operation of a pedestrian bridge or tunnel shall be authorized in accordance with Sec. 13B.2.5. (Director Determination). In addition to the findings otherwise required by [Sec. 13B.2.5. (Director Determination)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.2.5), before granting approval, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall find that the proposed pedestrian bridge or tunnel meets the requirements in Paragraph 2\. (Performance Criteria) and Paragraph 3. (Justification Criteria) below. Conditions of approval may be applied by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) pursuant to Paragraph 4. (Additional Conditions of Approval) below.

2. ##### Performance Criteria


      A pedestrian bridge or tunnel shall meet all of the following performance criteria:

      1. The design of the pedestrian bridge or tunnel is visually compatible with the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s involved and the surrounding environment.

      2. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel does not have a detrimental effect on surrounding properties, [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or the movement of wildlife.

      3. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel includes features that enhance the streetscape and pedestrian safety.

      4. The pedestrian bridge shall not include exterior [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) age.

      5. Existing sidewalk widths shall not be reduced.

      6. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel shall not detract from the intended [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and activation of the [public sidewalk](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      7. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel is not located above any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) zoned with an [Open Space Use District (Div. 5B.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.1).
3. ##### Justification Criteria


      The proposed pedestrian bridge or tunnel is justified by one or more of the following criteria:

      1. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel is essential to the viability to, and only allowed for, one of the following [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s:

         1. [Civic facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)

         2. [School](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)

         3. [Hospital](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)

         4. Convention Center
      2. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel is essential to the health and safety of occupants of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s it serves or the general public.

      3. The pedestrian bridge or tunnel is essential to overcome physical constraints, such as [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) changes or public infrastructure.
4. ##### Additional Conditions of Approval


      Conditions of approval may be imposed by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to ensure the proposed pedestrian bridge or tunnel does not detract from the pedestrian experience or have detrimental effects on surrounding properties or the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or to meet any other performance criteria.

### Div. 4C.2. Automobile Access

#### Sec. 4C.2.1. Automobile Access Packages

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Automobile Access Packages) is to ensure automobile [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s is designed to support the safety of all users by minimizing conflicts with pedestrians, cyclists, transit [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, micro-mobility devices, and automobile traffic on the [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), and to avoid detrimental effects on the surrounding public realm, while providing sufficient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to automobile parking and [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

2. ##### Applicability


1. Automobile access package standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [site modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or a [lot modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), wherever a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) provides a [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from a [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), and are applied to a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) as determined by the [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) assigned by the [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B) and subject to the following:

      1. Where [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standards are specified for 'Boulevard or Avenue', the standards apply to [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that take [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from a street designated as a [boulevard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [avenue](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), as designated by the applicable community plan circulation map.

      2. Where the [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standards are specified for 'Collector or Local', the standards apply to [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that take [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from a street designated as a [collector street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [local street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), as designated by the applicable community plan circulation map.
3. ##### Standards
