02. ##### General


       1. ##### Design


          All [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall conform to [Sec. 4C.2.2. (Motor Vehicle Use Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2).

       2. ##### Queuing Depth


          [Access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s designated for ingress traffic shall have a depth no less than the minimum specified in the table below, based on the total number of parking stalls included within the parking facilities that the [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) serves.



          |     |     |     |
          | --- | --- | --- |
          | QUEUING Depth |
          | Total Parking Stalls | Queuing Depth |
          | Boulevard or Avenue | Collector or Local |
          | 1-10 | 20' min | 0' min |
          | 11-100 | 20' min | 20' min |
          | 101-300 | 40' min | 40' min |
          | \> 300 | 60' min | 60' min |



          1. Vehicle entry restriction devices, such as mechanical gates or ticket dispensers, are prohibited within the [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for the minimum [queuing depth](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

          2. [Automobile parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall not be [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) ed from the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for the minimum [queuing depth](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

          3. [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s providing internal circulation within a parking facility shall not intersect a [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that is providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from the street for its minimum [queuing depth](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
03. ##### Access Location


       1. ##### Limited


          Where an automobile access package specifies "Limited" for any [street designation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the following standards apply:

          1. [Access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall not take [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s unless the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) does not include a [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through which [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) can be taken.

          2. [Access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall not take [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s unless the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) does not include an [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through which [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) can be taken.

          3. For an [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to be considered eligible for automobile [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall have a minimum width of 12 feet.
       2. ##### Permitted


          Where an [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specifies "Permitted" for a [street designation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are permitted along the specified [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
04. ##### Number of Access Lanes


       The total number of [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s taking [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be no greater than the number specified by the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) based on the [lot width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Lot width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be measured along the [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from which [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is limited pursuant to Paragraph 3. (Access Location) above.

05. ##### Access Lane Width


       [Access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be no wider than the maximum and no narrower than the minimum width specified by the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). When more than one [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is permitted on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), two [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s may be conjoined to create a dual-lane [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the maximum width of which is the sum of two allowable single [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) widths. A [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may be no wider than the sum of all included [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) widths, excluding gutters of no more than 18 inches wide, curbs, and [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

06. ##### Drive Aisle Separation


       1. ##### From Intersection


          1. [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be separated from all street intersections by a [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) no less than the minimum [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specified by the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), measured parallel to the applicable [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

          2. Where the intersecting street only interrupts the opposite edge of the subject street [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) (ex: three-way intersection), the following standards apply:

             1. Where at least one of the intersecting street rights-of-way is not designated as a [local street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be located no less than half of the minimum [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specified by the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

             2. Where both intersecting streets are designated as [local street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, no [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) separation from the intersection is required.
          3. [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s may only be placed within the minimum street separation from intersection when the [lot width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is less than 170 feet on a [boulevard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [avenue](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and 85 feet on a Collector or Local, and [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are placed along the [side lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) located furthest from the street intersection. When there are multiple intersections from which separation is required, [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be placed at the midpoint between the street intersections.
       2. ##### From Other Drive Aisles


          [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be separated from all other [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s located on the same [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by a [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) no less than the minimum [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specified by the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), measured parallel to the applicable [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
07. ##### Drive-Throughs


       1. Where the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specifies that [drive-through facilities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) are "Not Allowed", no drive-through facility may be provided on the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

       2. Where the assigned [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specifies that [drive-through facilities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) are "Allowed", a drive-through facility may be provided on- [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) provided they meet the standards for [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s provided in [Sec. 4C.2.2.C.3. (Motor Vehicle Use Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2).
08. ##### Measurement


       1. For determining [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) measurements see [Sec. 14.2.12. (Lot Line Determination)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12).

       2. [Street designation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is determined by the applicable community plan circulation map.

       3. Number of [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s is calculated as the total number of [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) along an individual [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

       4. [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) separation from intersections is measured parallel to the [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) takes [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through, from the extension of the curb along the intersecting street to the edge of the nearest [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

       5. [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) separation from other [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s located on the same [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is measured following the geometry of the [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) takes [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) through, from edge of [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to edge of [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) separation from other [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s only includes [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s providing access to the subject [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and does not include [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s providing access to surrounding [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s. [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.2.1.2.png.webp?itok=2IwFHBv2)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.2.1.2.png?itok=Nw8H1W0m)
09. [Access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width is measured as the narrowest horizontal dimension from edge of [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to edge of [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for the full length of the [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

10. [Queuing depth](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is measured from the applicable [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), into the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and perpendicular to the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width, to the [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [vehicle entry restriction device](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

       [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.2.1.3.png.webp?itok=GD_crAw0)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.2.1.3.png?itok=9BYYQzyP)
4. ##### Relief


1. Alternative Compliance from any automobile [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standard may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.1. (Alternative Compliance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.1).

2. A deviation from any [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) separation, width or depth dimensional standard, or [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) separation of 20 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. One additional [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in excess of the maximum number of [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s permitted may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

4. A deviation from any automobile access standard may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 4C.2.2. Motor Vehicle Use Area

A motor vehicle use area is defined as portions of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) designed and intended for [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, including areas to be used by [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s for circulation, maneuvering, loading, staging, [queuing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), service areas and areas to be used for the sale or storage of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Motor Vehicle Use Area) is to ensure [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are designed in a manner that does not detract from the safety, comfort, or enjoyment of users of neighboring [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s or the public realm.

2. ##### Applicability


[Motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or a [site modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). When [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design standards apply, the standards apply to the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), including areas to be used by [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s for circulation, maneuvering, loading, staging, queuing, service areas and areas to be used for the sale or storage of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

3. ##### Standards


1. ##### General


      1. ##### Location


         1. [Motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall not be located in a [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         2. [Motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall not be located in the area between a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and the minimum [parking setback](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specified by the applicable [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).
      2. ##### Screening


         1. Where a [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [faces](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), [common lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or an [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) the entire length of the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be screened as follows:

            1. An [F-Screen 2 (Sec. 4C.8.1.C.2.b.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2) or an [F-Screen 3 (Sec. 4C.8.1.C.2.c.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3) is required between the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s for any portion of the length of the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that [faces](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

            2. A [T-Screen 1 (Sec. 4C.8.2.C.3.a.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1) is required between the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and [common lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s for any portion of the length of the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that [faces](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) a [common lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

            3. A [T-Screen 1 (Sec. 4C.8.2.C.3.a.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1) is required between the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s for any portion of the length of the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that [faces](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) an [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
         2. Screens located in a [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall comply with frontage yard fence & wall standards in the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B).
      3. ##### Containment Perimeter


         [Motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall include a containment perimeter that obstructs [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s from leaving the designated [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). The containment perimeter shall be provided using one or more of the following containment methods around the entire perimeter except for crossings and access points required for [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [pedestrian passageway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s:

         1. Continuous curbs of no less than four inches in height.

         2. Permanent [bollard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, walls, raised planters, or a similar containment method having a height no less than 30 inches and having a [clear width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of no more than 66 inches.

         3. A [planting area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) meeting [Sec. 4C.6.4.C.2. (Planting Areas)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.6.4) with no horizontal dimension less than five feet.
      4. ##### Surfacing


         1. All automobile [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be graded and drained to collect, retain and infiltrate surface water on- [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by applying [Low Impact Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) practices and standards in accordance with [Chapter VI. (Public Works and Property), Sec. 64.72. (Stormwater Pollution Control Measures for Development Planning and Construction Activities)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-162923) of this Code.

         2. [Motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be surfaced with hard, durable asphaltic paving which has been mixed at a plant and is at least two inches thick after compaction, with portland cement paving at least three inches thick or with an alternative paving material described in sub-subparagraph iii. below.

         3. Alternative paving materials include the following: porous asphalt, porous concrete, permeable interlocking concrete pavers, permeable pavers, decomposed granite, crushed rock, gravel, and restrained systems (a plastic or concrete grid system confined on all sides to restrict lateral movement, and filled with gravel or grass in the voids).

         4. Alternative paving materials are permitted for use in every [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), subject to the following standards:

            1. Any product installed within areas designated by the Fire Department as a fire lane must be approved by the Fire Department.

            2. Permeable interlocking concrete pavers and permeable pavers shall have a minimum thickness of 80 millimeters (3.14 inches).

            3. If plants are an element of the alternative paving material, the irrigation system shall not utilize potable water except for plant establishment.

            4. Products and underlying drainage material shall be installed per manufacturers' specifications. Sub-grade soils shall be compacted as required per the product installation specifications.

            5. Decomposed granite, crushed rock and gravel shall only be allowed for [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s and [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s serving a maximum of two [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.
2. ##### Freight Loading Areas


      Freight loading areas are areas designated for the on- [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) loading and unloading of freight [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

      1. ##### General


         All [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on- [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall meet the following standards:

         1. Shall meet [Sec. 4C.2.2.C.1. (Motor Vehicle Use Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2).

         2. Shall meet the following dimensional standards:



            |     |     |
            | --- | --- |
            | FREIGHT LOADING AREA Dimensional Standards |
            | Area (min) | 400 SF |
            | Width (min) | 10' |
            | Depth (min) | 20' |
            | Clear height (min) | 14' |

         3. Be located and designed so that [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s do not occupy any portion of the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) when stationary during loading and unloading.

         4. Loading and unloading activities will not occur in public streets, with the exception of loading areas designated by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         5. Loading and unloading activities will not encroach on or interfere with the use of sidewalks, [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, automobile [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, or [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

         6. Include one permanent “NO IDLING” [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for every 400 square feet of [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be at least 18 inches by 24 inches in dimension and installed to be [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and located within 10 feet of each [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) provided. When multiple [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are required to be [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) the same [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be spaced a minimum of 10 feet apart.
      2. ##### Required Freight Loading Areas


         [Lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that include a tenant space of 10,000 square feet or greater designated for public & institutional uses, [general commercial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [heavy commercial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [light industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, or [heavy industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, that [abut](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) an [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) having a width of 15 feet or greater, and have an [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) 50 feet or wider, shall meet the following additional standards.

         1. The [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for each tenant space shall meet the following minimum dimensional standards:



            |     |     |
            | --- | --- |
            | FREIGHT LOADING AREA Total Area |
            | Non-Residential Tenant Size | Area (Min) |
            | < 10,000 SF | None required |
            | 10,000 - < 50,000 SF | 400 SF |
            | 50,000 - < 100,000 SF | 600 SF |
            | 100,000 - < 200,000 SF | 800 SF |
            | \> 200,000 SF | +200 SF / each additional 200,000 SF <br>over 200,000 SF |

         2. The total required [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may be provided as a single consolidated loading area equal in size to the sum of the required minimum dimension for each tenant space, or as separated [loading space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that each meet the required minimum dimensions.

         3. Each required [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall have [direct access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to an alley for a minimum width of 12 feet, measured along the [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) access for a [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may be shared among multiple [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s and [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.
3. ##### Drive-Through Facilities


      A drive-through facility is a facility that provides goods or services to drivers in [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s. [Drive-through facilities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) include [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s consisting of [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

      1. Where the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specifies that [drive-through facilities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) are "Not Allowed", no drive-through facility may be provided on- [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      2. Where the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) specifies that [drive-through facilities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) are "Allowed", a drive-through facility may be provided on- [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and shall meet all of the following standards:

         1. Comply with Subsection C. (Standards) above.

         2. Provide a number of automobile [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s sufficient to accommodate the number of automobiles anticipated during peak demand, to the satisfaction of [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         3. Shall not encroach on or interfere with the use of sidewalks, [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to parking stalls, loading areas, or [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

         4. Each [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in a [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is a minimum of 20 feet in length and eight feet in width along straight segments of the [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). [Drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are a minimum of 12 feet in width along curved segments.

            [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.2.2.1.png.webp?itok=rYLOPYx8)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.4.0/4C.2.2.1.png?itok=wCgnxvyS)

         5. Any [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that take access directly from the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be regulated as a [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and subject to the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standards specified by the applicable [automobile access package](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for the minimum required depth of the [queuing depth](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         6. Reviewed and approved by LADOT to ensure the [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design does not create detrimental impacts on pedestrians bicyclists, transit [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s or riders, micro mobility device users, and automobile traffic and circulation on the [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
4. ##### Measurement


1. For [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) measurements see [Sec. 14.2.12. (Lot Line Determination)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12).

2. For [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) measurements see [Sec. 14.2.16.C.1. (Frontage yard)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.16).

3. For [parking setback](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) measurements see [Sec. 3C.2.1. (Parking Setback)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.2.1).

4. [Freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width is measured as the narrowest horizontal [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) between opposite edges of a designated [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

5. [Freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) depth is measured as the narrowest horizontal [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) measured perpendicular to the [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width from one edge of a designated [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to the opposite edge. A minimum [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) depth shall be met for all portions of the [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width.

6. [Freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) provided is measured as the total area of all areas designated as [freight loading area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) that meet all applicable requirements of [Sec. 4C.2.2.C.2. (Freight Loading Areas)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2).

7. Drive-through [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) depth is measured parallel to the [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from one end to the opposite end of the [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

8. Drive-through [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) width is measured perpendicular to the [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) length from one end to the opposite end of the [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
5. ##### Exceptions


[Parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s and [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are excluded from [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design standards. For [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s and [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design standards see [Sec. 4C.4.3. (Parking Area Design)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.3).

6. ##### Relief


1. A deviation from any [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design dimensional standard of 10 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A deviation from any [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) design standard may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

### Div. 4C.3. Bicycle Parking

#### Sec. 4C.3.1. Bicycle Parking Spaces

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Bicycle Parking Spaces) is to promote bicycling as an alternative to automobile transportation, and to ensure safe, secure, accessible, and convenient storage of bicycles for all users.

2. ##### Applicability


This Section (Bicycle Parking Spaces) applies to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [site modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or a [use modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

3. ##### Standards


The required number of short-term and long-term bicycle parking spaces are determined by [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) according to the following provisions:

1. ##### Residential


      For all [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s containing more than three [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, long-term and short-term bicycle parking shall be provided according to the ratios specified for each marginal increment of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s as indicated in the table below.




      | Required Bicycle Parking |
      | --- |
      |  | Short-Term<br>( [Sec. 4C.3.2.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.2)) | Long-Term<br>( [Sec. 4C.3.3.](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.3)) |
      | --- | --- | --- |
      | Residential |  |  |
      | 1st 25 [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)s | 1/10 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), (2 min) | 1/ [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) |
      | 26th-100th [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) | 1/15 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), (2 min) | 1/1.5 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) |
      | 101st-200th [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) | 1/20 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), (2 min) | 1/2 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) |
      | 201st + [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)s | 1/40 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), (2 min) | 1/4 [du](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) |



      1. Developments that include individually accessed private garages for each [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall not be required to provide long-term bicycle parking.

      2. Notwithstanding the above, for all [supportive housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, short-term bicycle parking shall be provided at a rate of one space per 10,000 square feet of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and long-term bicycle parking shall be provided at a rate of 1 space per 5,000 square feet of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). A minimum of two short-term and two long-term bicycle parking spaces shall be provided.

3. ##### City Operated Uses


      In all [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s or [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s used by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for government purposes, including government office [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, both short-term and long-term bicycle parking shall be provided at a rate of 10 percent of the required parking. However, no less than five short-term bicycle spaces and no less than five long-term bicycle parking shall be provided for the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
4. ##### Measurement


1. ##### Multiple Uses


      Where there is a combination of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the number of bicycle parking spaces required is the sum of the requirements of the various [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s. The exceptions provided in [Sec. 4C.4.1.E. (Exceptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.1) for automobile parking also apply to bicycle parking.

2. ##### Fractions


      When the application of these regulations results in the requirement of a fractional bicycle space, any fraction up to and including one-half may be disregarded, and any fraction over one-half is construed as requiring one bicycle parking space. Rounding shall occur after taking the sum of bicycle parking required across all proposed [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, and shall be calculated separately for long-term and short-term spaces.
5. ##### Exceptions


[Adaptive reuse project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s in accordance with [Sec. 9.4.5. (Downtown Adaptive Reuse Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.5) and [Sec. 9.4.6. (Citywide Adaptive Reuse Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.6) are not required to provide additional bicycle parking.

6. ##### Relief


1. A deviation from any required bicycle parking dimensional standard of 10 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

2. A deviation from any required bicycle parking standard may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 4C.3.2. Short-Term Bicycle Parking Design

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Short-Term Bicycle Parking Design) is to promote bicycling as an alternative to automobile transportation, ensure safe, secure, accessible, and convenient storage of bicycles for visitors and other short-term users, improve bicyclist [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from the public realm to the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, and ensure entrances are conveniently and effectively accessible to bicyclists.

2. ##### Applicability


This Section (Short-Term Bicycle Parking Design) applies to all short-term bicycle parking spaces required by [Sec. 4C.3.1. (Bicycle Parking Spaces)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.1).

3. ##### Standards


1. ##### General


      1. Adequate lighting shall be provided to ensure safe [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to bicycle parking facilities in accordance with [Sec. 4C.10.1. (Outdoor Lighting)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.10.1).

      2. Owners and operators shall not unreasonably interfere with the ability of bicyclists to safely and conveniently [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) bicycle parking, including the adoption of unreasonable property management rules. Unreasonable interference includes shorter operating hours for short-term bicycle parking than for the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or automobile parking, prohibitions on walking of bicycles in pedestrian areas that provide [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to bicycle parking, and prohibitions on bicycles in elevators where elevators are used to provide [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to bicycle parking. The provisions of this Subparagraph do not prohibit property owners from requiring bicycles to be walked in pedestrian-only areas.
2. ##### Bicycle Parking Space Design


      1. ##### General


         Required short-term bicycle parking shall consist of bicycle racks that do all of the following:

         1. Support the bicycle frame at two points, and support only the wheel of the bicycle are not permissible.

         2. Allow for the bicycle frame and at least one wheel to be locked to the racks.

         3. Allow for the use of a cable as well as a U-shaped lock.

         4. If bicycles can be locked to each side of the rack, each side can be counted toward a required space.

         5. Be securely anchored to a permanent surface.

         6. If more than 20 short-term bicycle parking spaces are provided, at least 50 percent of the bicycle parking spaces shall be 100 percent [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by a roof or overhang.

         7. [Bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) docks counted toward the requirements for short-term bicycle parking spaces as permitted in [Sec. 4C.3.2.C.3. (Siting Requirements)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.2) shall conform to [Sec. 4C.3.2.C.6. (Bicycle Share Station)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.2).
      2. ##### Horizontal Storage


         1. Short-term bicycle parking spaces shall be a minimum of two feet wide and six feet long.

         2. Individual racks installed beside each other that allow bicycles to be locked to either side of the rack shall be spaced a minimum of 30 inches on center.

         3. Racks installed parallel to walls shall be a minimum of 30 inches from the wall, except that bicycle parking spaces providing a tray or channel for insertion of bicycle wheels shall be placed a minimum of 20 inches from the wall.

         4. Bicycle parking spaces arranged in a vertically staggered layout that permits bicycles to be placed in and removed from each individual space without interference from bicycles in [adjoining](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spaces shall be spaced a minimum of 16 inches on center.
      3. ##### Stacked Storage


         1. Alternatively to Subparagraph b. (Horizontal Storage) above, short-term bicycle parking may be mounted so that bicycles are stored in a stacked, two-tier layout, provided such parking is an attended bicycle facility where facility staff parks the bicycles, or such racks provide mechanical assistance for lifting the bicycle. If stacked bicycle storage is provided as an [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the service must meet the standards outlined in Paragraph 7. (Attended Bicycle Parking Service) below.

         2. Racks installed parallel to [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall be a minimum of 14 inches from the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) if such spaces are on the upper level of a stacked, two-tier rack.
3. ##### Siting Requirements


      01. Required short-term bicycle parking shall be provided in one of the following location, or a combination of the following:

          1. On the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) as the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for which it is intended to serve.

          2. In a parking facility serving the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for which the bicycle parking is intended to serve.

          3. Immediately in front of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) within the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with Paragraph 4. (Bicycle Parking in the Public Right-of-Way) below.

          4. In a [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)-funded [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with Paragraph 5. (Bicycle Corrals) below.

          5. In a [bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with Paragraph 6. (Bicycle Share Stations) below.
      02. Bicycle parking shall be located so as to allow bicyclists safe and convenient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to and from the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      03. Bicyclists shall not be required to rely on stairways or escalators for [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or to share [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) with automobiles or other [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

      04. Elevators providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for bicyclists shall be sized to accommodate standard adult bicycle dimensions with both wheels on the floor (at least six feet by two feet).

      05. Short-term bicycle parking shall be located so as to provide safe and convenient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to visitors.

      06. For [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), at least 50 percent of short-term bicycle parking shall be located outside [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s or [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s; however, no more than eight short-term bicycle parking spaces per 100 linear feet of [street frontage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) are required to be outside.

      07. All short-term bicycle parking spaces located inside the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be located on the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) with a direct [pedestrian accessway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 4C.1.1.C.2.a.ii. (Direct)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.1.1) to a public street.

      08. For [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), short-term bicycle parking shall be located to maximize visibility from a pedestrian entrance.

      09. All short-term bicycle [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s located within [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s or [parking garage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s require [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s meeting the following standards:

          1. Permanently posted at the street entrance to each [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

          2. Legible and reflectorized.

          3. Indicate the availability and location of bicycle parking within the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

          4. All [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall comply with [Div. 4C.11. (Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11).
      10. Short-term bicycle parking spaces may be located no farther than 100 feet of [walking distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from a pedestrian entrance that provides [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that require the bicycle parking spaces.

      11. For [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s with more than one pedestrian entrance, short-term bicycle parking, with the exception of [bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, shall be distributed in approximately equal proportions among all pedestrian entrances. In [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s with three or more pedestrian entrances, no more than 50 percent of all short-term bicycle parking spaces shall be assigned to a single pedestrian entrance.
4. ##### Bicycle Parking in the Public Right-of-Way


      Business operators or property owners may install their own racks within the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) unless a [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) owned rack already exists, subject to compliance with all [LAMC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) requirements, including but not limited obtaining any necessary permit from the Bureau of Engineering and approval by [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

5. ##### Bicycle Corrals


      1. ##### City-Funded Bicycle Corrals


         Any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) located within 500 feet of a [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)-funded [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may count up to four bicycle parking spaces within the [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) towards their required short-term bicycle parking spaces.

      2. ##### Bicycle Corral Parking Incentive Program


         1. Businesses or property owners who have obtained approval from Bureau of Engineering and [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to install and maintain a [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in the [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in front of their property may count all the bicycle parking within the [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) toward their required number of short-term bicycle parking spaces. In such cases, short-term bicycle parking installed in such a manner cannot be counted towards the bicycle parking requirements of surrounding businesses.

         2. Business operators or property owners shall pay the construction and maintenance costs of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) said [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

         3. Multiple businesses or property owners may submit an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) as a group and split the costs to construct and maintain the corral.

            1. In such cases, a single property owner is responsible for assuming the maintenance responsibilities detailed in a recorded covenant maintenance agreement as outlined below in a form approved by LADOT.

            2. The property owner named in the covenant who is responsible for maintaining the [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may count the full amount of bicycle parking in the corral towards its short-term bicycle parking requirements.

            3. All other businesses may count up to half of the bicycle parking spaces in the corral towards their required short-term bicycle parking spaces.
         4. Business operators or property owners who choose to install [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s within the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be responsible for maintaining the racks according to the standards set forth in a covenant maintenance agreement approved by [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         5. If, for any reason, the responsibility for maintaining a [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is returned to the City of Los Angeles, it shall be considered a [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)-funded [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         6. If, for any reason, the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) determines that a [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) has been removed regardless of the reason, business owners shall no longer be able to count the spaces removed toward their required bicycle parking and the said businesses shall be required to provide any bicycle parking spaces lost in the removal of the [bicycle corral](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). Failure to comply may result in the revocation of a business's [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and a fine for code violation.
6. ##### Bicycle Share Stations


      1. [Bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall conform to Paragraph 3. (Siting Requirements) above.

      2. Business operators or property owners may allow a [bicycle share service provider](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to install one or more [bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on their property, provided that such [bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is part of a bicycle share system approved by [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and complies with all location criteria established by [LADOT](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for [bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

      3. Any [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) within 500 feet of a [bicycle share station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may count up to four [bicycle share dock](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s toward the required number of short-term bicycle parking spaces for a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). In all cases, the number of [bicycle share dock](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s counted toward the required number of short-term bicycle parking spaces cannot exceed 10 percent of the total number of short-term bicycle parking spaces required for the subject lot.

      4. Where [bicycle share dock](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are counted toward the required number of short-term bicycle parking spaces, [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and non-residential [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s may replace a percentage of the required automobile parking spaces with [bicycle share dock](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s in a manner consistent with the limitations and replacement ratio established in [Sec. 4C.4.1.E.10. (Substituting Required Automobile Parking with Bicycle Parking)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.1).

      5. If, for any reason, [bicycle share dock](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s are removed, the associated land [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s may no longer count the docks removed toward required bicycle parking and shall be required to replace the number of docks formerly counted toward required bicycle parking with an equivalent number of bicycle parking spaces.
7. ##### Attended Bicycle Parking Service


      1. A pick-up and drop-off location for short-term bicycle parking shall either comply with Paragraph 3. (Siting Requirements) above or be co-located with a valet automobile parking pick-up or drop-off location provided on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for the subject [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      2. Once stored, a bicycle left in the care of an attendant(s) shall be accessible only to the attendant(s), with the storage location not necessarily in the same location as the pick-up and drop-off point.

      3. If some or all required short-term bicycle parking spaces are provided by means of an [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the service shall be available to [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) occupants at all times during the hours the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is in operation.

      4. If, for any reason, an [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is discontinued, the associated land [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s may no longer count the [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) toward their required number of bicycle parking spaces and shall be required to provide a number of bicycle parking spaces equivalent to the number formerly provided by the [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).
4. ##### Measurement


\[Reserved\]

5. ##### Relief


1. An alternative to any short-term bicycle parking design standards may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.1. (Alternative Compliance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.1).

2. A deviation from any short-term bicycle parking design dimensional standard of 10 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. A deviation from any short-term bicycle parking design standard may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

#### Sec. 4C.3.3. Long-Term Bicycle Parking Design

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Long-Term Bicycle Parking Design) is to promote bicycling as an alternative to automobile transportation, ensure safe, secure, accessible, and convenient storage of bicycles for tenants and other long-term users, improve bicyclist [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from the public realm to the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, and ensure entrances are conveniently and effectively accessible to bicyclists.

2. ##### Applicability


This Section (Long-Term Bicycle Parking Design) applies to all long-term bicycle parking spaces required by [Sec. 4C.3.1. (Bicycle Parking Spaces)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.1).

3. ##### Standards


1. ##### General


      1. Adequate lighting shall be provided to ensure safe [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to bicycle parking facilities in accordance with [Sec. 4C.10.1. (Outdoor Lighting)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.10.1).

      2. Owners and operators shall not unreasonably interfere with the ability of bicyclists to safely and conveniently [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) bicycle parking, including through the adoption of unreasonable property management rules. Unreasonable interference includes shorter operating hours for long-term bicycle parking than for any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or automobile parking, prohibitions on walking of bicycles in pedestrian areas that provide [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to bicycle parking, and prohibitions on bicycles in elevators where elevators are used to provide [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to bicycle parking. The provisions of this Subparagraph. do not prohibit property owners from requiring bicycles to be walked in pedestrian-only areas.
2. ##### Bicycle Parking Space Design


      1. ##### General


         1. Long-term bicycle parking shall be secured from the general public and protected from inclement weather. All long-term bicycle parking shall be fully [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

         2. Acceptable examples of long-term bicycle parking include bicycle lockers, [bicycle room](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [bicycle cage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, or commercially operated attended bicycle facilities.

         3. Except in the case of lockers and commercially operated attended bicycle parking, all long-term bicycle parking shall provide a means of securing the bicycle frame at two points to a securely anchored rack.
      2. ##### Horizontal Storage


         Long-term bicycle parking spaces shall be sized to permit safe, efficient, and convenient access to each individual bicycle parking space without interference from bicycles in [adjoining](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spaces, as described below:

         1. Individual racks installed beside each other within [bicycle room](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s or [bicycle cage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s that allow bicycles to be locked to either side of the rack shall be spaced a minimum of 30 inches on center.

         2. Racks installed parallel to walls shall be a minimum of 30 inches from the wall, with the exception that bicycle parking spaces that provide a tray into which the bicycle wheels may be inserted may be placed a minimum of 20 inches from the wall, or 14 inches from the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) if such spaces are on the upper level of a stacked, two-tier rack.

         3. Triangular lockers with varying widths may be used so long as the opening is at least two feet wide.

         4. Bicycle parking spaces arranged in a vertically staggered layout that permits bicycles to be placed in and removed from each individual space without interference from bicycles in [adjoining](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) spaces may be spaced a minimum of 16 inches on center.

         5. If more than 20 long-term bicycle parking spaces are provided, a workspace of 100 square feet shall be provided [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to the long-term bicycle parking to allow bicyclists to maintain their bicycles. However, where long-term bicycle parking is provided in more than one location, a single workspace may be provided [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to the location with the greatest number of long-term bicycle parking spaces.
      3. ##### Vertical Storage


         Alternative to Subparagraph b. (Horizontal Storage) above, long-term bicycle parking may be mounted so that the bicycle is stored vertically. Such devices that hold the bicycle by the wheel shall be designed to support the bicycle without damaging the wheels. Vertically installed bicycle parking shall be a minimum of four feet deep and six feet in height.

      4. ##### Stacked Storage


         Alternative to Subparagraph b. (Horizontal Storage) and Subparagraph c. (Vertical Storage) above, long-term bicycle parking may be mounted so that bicycles are stored in a stacked, two-tier layout, provided such parking is an attended bicycle facility where facility staff parks the bicycles, or such racks provide mechanical assistance for lifting the bicycle.
3. ##### Siting Requirements


      1. Long-term bicycle parking spaces shall be provided in one of the following locations, or in a combination of the following locations:

         1. On the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) within 100 feet of the major entrance to the lobby. There shall be safe and convenient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) between the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the bicycle parking space, and the lobby area.

         2. In the off-street automobile [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), subject to the following limitations:

            1. Long-term bicycle parking inside a [parking garage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may be no more than 200 feet from a pedestrian entrance to the main [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), and located so as to provide reasonably convenient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) from the bicycle parking to the nearest walkway, ramp, or elevator providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

            2. Long-term bicycle parking inside a [parking garage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be located within the space available on the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)’s pedestrian entry level, after required handicapped-accessible parking stalls and other elements required by federal, state and local laws have been provided.
         3. One level above or below the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), within 100 feet of the elevator, ramp, walkway, or other [building entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) on that [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#). In such cases, elevator or ramp access to the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be provided.

         4. [Residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) long-term bicycle parking may be provided in common storage facilities on [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) floors in accordance with [Sec. 4C.3.3.C.2. (Bicycle Parking Space Design)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.3.3). If [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) long-term bicycle parking is provided on [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) floors, the amount of bicycle parking on each floor shall be equal to or greater than 50 percent of the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on the same floor.
      2. For [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s with multiple [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, long-term bicycle parking may be provided in one or more bicycle parking facilities within 200 feet of each [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      3. For [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s with multiple [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, required bicycle parking may be [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) d in one or more bicycle parking facilities within 200 feet of each [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      4. Bicycle parking shall be located so as to allow bicyclists safe and convenient [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to and from the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      5. Bicyclists shall not be required to rely on stairways or escalators for [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) or to share [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) with automobiles or other [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.

      6. Elevators providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for bicyclists shall be sized to accommodate standard adult bicycle dimensions with both wheels on the floor (at least six feet by two feet).
4. ##### Showers and Personal Lockers


      Showers and personal lockers are required for long-term bicycle parking in non-residential [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s in accordance with [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Sec. 91.6307. (Shower and Locker Facilities)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-177422) of this Code and shall remain available for the use of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) occupants arriving by bicycle.

5. ##### Attended Bicycle Parking Service


      1. A pick-up and drop-off location for long-term bicycle facilities shall either comply with Paragraph 3. (Siting Requirements) above or be co-located with a valet automobile parking pick-up or drop-off location provided on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) for the subject [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

      2. Once stored, a bicycle left in the care of an attendant(s) shall be accessible only to the attendant(s), with the storage location not necessarily in the same location as the pick-up and drop-off point.

      3. If some or all required bicycle parking spaces are provided by means of an [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), the service shall be available to [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) occupants at all times during the hours the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is in operation.

      4. If, for any reason, an [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is discontinued, the associated land [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s may no longer count the [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) toward the required number of bicycle parking spaces and shall provide a number of bicycle parking spaces equivalent to the number formerly provided by the [attended bicycle parking service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) and required to meet the minimum parking requirement.
4. ##### Measurement


\[Reserved\]

5. ##### Relief


1. An alternative compliance to any long-term bicycle parking design standards may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.1. (Alternative Compliance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.1).

2. A deviation from any long-term bicycle parking design dimensional standard of 10 percent or less may be granted in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2).

3. A deviation from any long-term bicycle parking design standard may be granted as a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) in accordance with [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3).

### Div. 4C.4. Automobile Parking

[faq](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)

#### Sec. 4C.4.1. Automobile Parking Stalls

An automobile parking stall is defined as a space within a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or a private or public parking area, exclusive of [driveway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, ramps, columns, office, and work areas, for the parking of one automobile. Automobile parking stalls do not include bicycle parking.

1. ##### Intent


The intent of the standards of this Section (Automobile Parking Stalls) is to accommodate the arrival to a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) by automobile at a level appropriate to the demand generated by a particular [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) within different mobility contexts without creating detrimental effects on surrounding properties or [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#).

2. ##### Applicability


[Automobile parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) standards apply to [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), a [site modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or a [use modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) to [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), or [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), and as determined by the automobile parking package assigned by the applicable [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B).

3. ##### Standards


1. ##### General


      1. [Project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall provide the minimum number of [automobile parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s specified in the Required Automobile Parking Table, Table 1 below, based on the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)'s [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#)(s) and the parking package assigned by the applied [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B).

      2. When a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) is used for a combination of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s, the parking requirements are the sum of the requirements for each [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), and no parking stall for one [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) may be included in the calculation of parking requirements for any other [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#), with the following exceptions:

         1. As allowed in [Sec. 4C.4.3.C.2. (Shared Parking)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.3).

         2. When parking requirements for a single [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) with a combination of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s results in a fraction, then the total parking required for all [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) shall be calculated based on the sum prior to the rounding of parking requirements for each [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) followed by rounding the total amount of parking required for a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) based on the combination of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s.
      3. In addition to the above, [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) s shall comply with the electric [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#) charging space requirements in [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Article 9. (Green Building Code)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-214608) of this Code.
