### Sec. 10.3.8. Private Street Names

1. [Private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) names shall be established or changed pursuant to the procedures set forth in this Division (Private Street Regulations) in the event no [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) map is required under [Sec. 10.3.2. (Applicability)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.3.2) or [Sec. 13B.7.7. (Private Street Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7.7).

2. [Application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s to establish or change the name of a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall be filed with the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). [Application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s shall be signed by a majority of the owners of properties [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) the [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or that portion of the street to be named or renamed, and be accompanied by:

1. Payment of the required [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) processing fees;

2. A map, drawn to scale, delineating the location, extent, width, and alignment of the [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), the approximate location and frontage dimensions of said [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s on said street, and the location of existing public streets which it may ingress or egress; and

3. Identity of the maker of the map, and the names and addresses of owners of record of property [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) the [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or that portion of the street to be named or renamed.
3. The [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) may initiate proceedings to name or rename a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). In such event, the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) action shall be referred to the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). That office shall process the action in the manner set forth in Subsection E. (Private Street Names) below, and, if necessary or appropriate under the circumstances, shall prepare a map in the manner which satisfies the requirements set forth in Paragraph 2. of Subsection B. (Private Street Names) above.

4. Where there is an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) filed to name or rename a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and no new [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) map is required pursuant to [Sec. 13B.7.7. (Private Street Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7.7), or there is a [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)-initiated request, a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) may be named or renamed to a requested new name and the necessary documents recorded by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) with respect to the new name, pursuant to the following procedure:

1. The [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall determine whether the proposed new name or change of name of a street is in the public interest and will not create confusion, be misleading, be unduly long, or carry connotations offensive to good taste and decency.

2. The [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall give notice of the proposed new street name or name change to the record owners and occupants of all real property [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) such [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). The notice shall designate the location of the [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or portion of the street to which the proposed new name is to apply. The street, or the affected portion of the street, shall be described in the notice with reference to other streets, and by the name or names, if any, which it bears or by which it, or any portion of it, may be or may have been known, and the notice shall also state the proposed new street name. The notice shall further set forth whether or not the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)’s determination recommends disapproval of the proposed name for reasons provided in Paragraph 1. of this Subsection, and shall state that any written objections with respect to the proposed new name or name change or the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)’s recommendation, shall be filed with the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) within 30 days after a date designated on the notice as applicable for said purpose, and that the objections shall be signed by each person so objecting.

3. In the event any objections are filed within the 30-day time limit, or any objections are filed with respect to a [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)’s recommendation of disapproval within the 30-day time limit, the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall forward these, together with the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)’s determination and recommendations and the applicable file to the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). The [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall set the matter for hearing and the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) Clerk shall thereupon notify by mail each person objecting to the proposed street name or to the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)’s recommendation of disapproval and inform that person of the time and place for hearing. At the time specified, the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall hear all objections and shall thereafter approve or disapprove the proposed street name. The [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)’s decision shall be final and conclusive.

4. In the event no objections are filed with the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) within 30 days of the date prescribed on the notice, and the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) has not recommended disapproval of the proposed new name, the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for that name shall be deemed approved. In the event the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) has recommended disapproval of the proposed name, and no objections to that recommendation have been filed, the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall be deemed denied.

5. If the new name is either approved by the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or in the event no [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) hearing was required and the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) is deemed approved, the new [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) name shall be effective, and the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall cause any necessary indexing or recordation of documents to be accomplished and shall provide a copy of the determination to all [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) Departments rendering emergency service to the affected properties and to the United States Postal Service.
5. The approval or deemed approval of a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) name as provided for in this Division (Private Street Regulations) is not, and shall not be construed to be, an acceptance of a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) as a public street, nor shall it create any public warranty or liability or legal status as a public street, nor should it be so construed.


## Div. 10.4. Parks Fees & Dedications

### Sec. 10.4.1. Intent

New [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s increase demand on existing park and recreational facilities and create the need for additional facilities. The intent of this Division (Parks Fees & Dedications) is to enable the acquisition of land and the collection of fees to be used for the purpose of developing new or rehabilitating existing recreational facilities in order to create a healthy and sustainable [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

### Sec. 10.4.2. Types of Fees

The type and amount of park and recreation impact fees associated with a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) depends on the type of [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) being developed. [Subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s consisting of more than 50 [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s are subject to a Quimby in-lieu fee. All other [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s are subject to a park mitigation fee. Collectively, these fees are referred to in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) as [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

### Sec. 10.4.3. Applicability

All new [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s and joint living and work quarters shall be required to dedicate land, pay a fee or provide a combination of [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and fee payment for the purpose of acquiring, expanding, and improving park and recreational facilities for new [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s. For the purposes of this Division (Parks Fees & Dedications), [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, [accessory dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, [junior accessory dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, and household business: joint living & work quarters shall be referred to as [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

1. ##### Residential Subdivision Projects That Contain More Than 50 Dwelling Units


A [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) containing more than 50 [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s shall be required to participate in early consultation with the Department of Recreation and Parks and [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.4. (Residential Subdivision Projects with More than 50 Dwelling Units)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.4), and may be required to dedicate land, make park improvements, pay [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, or provide a combination of [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) payment.

2. ##### All Other Residential Projects


For [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s containing 50 or fewer [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s or for non-subdivision [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s that are seeking a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) that contains any number of net new [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall pay a [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.5. (All Other Residential Projects)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.5). Applicants may choose to dedicate land or new park and recreational facilities, or improve existing park and recreational facilities in lieu of payment of a [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

3. ##### Exemptions


    The following types of development shall not be required to pay a [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#):

1. Modifications, renovations, or [addition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s to an existing [residential building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) where no additional [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s are created.

2. Replacement of existing [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s on the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) resulting in no net increase of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

3. The replacement of a [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or partially [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or damaged [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) where no additional [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s are created.

4. Affordable housing pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.7. (Affordable Housing Exemption)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.7).

5. [Accessory dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s and [junior accessory dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

6. Non-residential development.

### Sec. 10.4.4. Residential Subdivision Projects With More Than 50 Dwelling Units

1. ##### Early Consultation


Applicants shall meet with the Department of Recreation and Parks and [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) staff in advance of submitting a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) of more than 50 [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s. The intent of this early consultation is to discuss the potential [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) requirements of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and to discuss credits available to the applicant, if any. The Department of Recreation and Parks shall provide written verification of the consultation to the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) applicant within 10 business days of the meeting. Written verification of this consultation shall be required before the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) accepts a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

2. ##### Formula for Park Land Dedication


1. The Department of Recreation and Parks shall calculate the amount of land to be dedicated by determining the number of net new, non-exempt, pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.3.C. (Exemptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.3), [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s in the proposed [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and multiply that number by the average number of people per occupied [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and multiplying that by the park service factor:

      LD = (HU x P) x F

      LD: Land to be dedicated in acres.

      HU: Total number of new market-rate [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

      P: Average number of people per occupied [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) as determined by the most recent version of the U.S. Census for the City of Los Angeles.

      F: Park service factor, as indicated by the Department of Recreation and Parks rate and fee schedule.

2. Any land dedication for park and recreation purposes shall not be deducted from a site's [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) when calculating [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) density.

3. If after recording the [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) there is an increase in the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s to be built or a change in the number or type of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s designated, which increases the number of [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s served by the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) applicant shall be required to dedicate additional land or pay additional fees, as determined by the Department of Recreation and Parks and the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).
3. ##### Park Land Dedication Radius


Any [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for park and recreation purposes shall be located within a certain radius from the [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), as specified below:

1. Neighborhood Park: within a two-mile distance

2. Community Park: within a five-mile distance

3. Regional Park: within a 10-mile distance
4. ##### Review of Land Dedication


1. Upon receiving the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall transmit the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) that involves a proposed [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) to the Department of Recreation and Parks.

2. After receipt of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), the Department of Recreation and Parks shall determine whether the [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) proposal complies with the Department of Recreation and Park's existing park and recreation standards and requirements.

3. If the Department of Recreation and Parks determines that the [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) proposal meets the standards and requirements of the department, the General Manager of the Department of Recreation and Parks shall prepare a report to the Board of Recreation and Parks Commissioners regarding the proposed dedication. The Board of Recreation and Parks Commissioners may accept or decline the [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).
5. ##### Payment of Park Fee


If the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) is not required to dedicate land for park and recreational purposes, the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) applicant shall pay a [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.5. (All Other Residential Projects)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.5).


### Sec. 10.4.5. All Other Residential Projects

1. ##### Fees & Fee Schedule


The [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) amount depends on the type of [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). The Department of Recreation and Parks shall collect these fees pursuant to [Sec. 15.9.3. (Park Fees)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#15.9.3) and the Department of Recreation and Parks rate and fee schedule.

2. ##### Fee Calculation


The Department of Recreation and Parks shall calculate the amount of the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) due for each [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) by determining the number of new non-exempt [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.3.C. (Exemptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.3), in the proposed [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and multiplying the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s by the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) amount per [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) according to the following formula:

Project Park Fee = HU x PRF

HU: Total number of new, non-exempt [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.3.C. (Exemptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.3)

PRF: Park Fee per [dwelling](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) unit

3. ##### Fee Expenditure Radius


Recreational sites and facilities shall be located within a certain radius from the [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), as specified below:

1. Neighborhood park: within a two-mile distance.

2. Community park: within a five-mile distance.

3. Regional park: within a 10-mile distance.
4. ##### Indexing


Any fee imposed by this Division (Parks Fees & Dedications) shall be adjusted on July 1st of each year by a percentage equal to a weighted average of:

1. The percentage change in the Construction Cost Index for Los Angeles, as published by Engineering News Record, or its successor publication, for the 12-month period between March in the year in which the adjustment is made and the month of March in the immediately preceding year; and

2. The percentage change in the Federal Reserve Economic Data All-Transactions House Price Index for Los Angeles-Long Beach-Glendale, CA (MASD) as published quarterly by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, or its successor publication, from the fourth calendar quarter most recent to the year in which the adjustment is made to the fourth calendar quarter immediately preceding it.
5. ##### Fee Payment Timing


1. ###### Residential Subdivision Projects


      The [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s shall be calculated and collected prior to final [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) map approval. [Subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) maps that are phased or unitized may be calculated and paid in phases permitting that the phased map and the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s on each phased map has been confirmed by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

2. ###### Residential Non-Subdivision Projects


      For other [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall be calculated and collected prior to the issuance of the [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

### Sec. 10.4.6. Park Fee as Additional Requirement

The [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) enacted by this Division (Park Fees & Dedications) is a fee imposed on [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s reflecting each [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)'s proportionate share of the cost of providing park land and improvements necessary to meet the needs created by each respective development. As such, the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) is additional and supplemental to, and not in substitution of, [lot amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or [residential amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) required by this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A), a [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or any other planning document.

### Sec. 10.4.7. Affordable Housing Exemption

1. Notwithstanding any other provision contained in this Division (Park Fees & Dedications), new [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s which are rented or sold to [very low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, [low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, or [moderate income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s shall receive an affordable housing exemption from the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) and land dedication requirement, subject to the following:

1. A [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall receive an exemption from the requirement for [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for park and recreational purposes or payment of the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) if the [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) is affordable to a household at or below 120 percent of [AMI](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

2. In [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s with a mix of market-rate and [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, only the [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s shall receive this exemption.
2. For any [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) qualifying for an exemption, a covenant acceptable to the Los Angeles Housing Department shall be recorded with the Los Angeles County Recorder, guaranteeing that the affordability criteria will be observed for at least 55 years from the issuance of the [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or a longer period of time if required by any applicable construction or mortgage financing assistance program, mortgage assistance program, or rental subsidy program.

3. The Los Angeles Housing Department shall evaluate the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) to ensure it meets the above requirements and shall advise the Department of Recreation and Parks and the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) about whether the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) meets those requirements.

4. Should any qualifying [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) cease to operate as a qualifying [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) before the 55-year period has expired, [LAHD](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall notify the Department of Recreation and Parks, and the parks fee for each said [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall be paid to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) at the then-current rate.


### Sec. 10.4.8. Credits

1. ##### Public Land Dedication or Improvement to Dedicated Land


1. ###### Public Land Dedication


      In lieu of paying the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or any portion of the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), land may be dedicated to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) of Los Angeles for public park and recreational purposes, at the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#)'s option. This may be with or without recreational facility improvements. The amount of land to be dedicated shall be determined pursuant to one of the following formulas, and credit shall be granted, square foot for square foot, for any land dedicated to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#):

      1. ###### Subdivision Projects:


         LD = (HU x P) x F1

         LD: Land to be dedicated in acres.

         HU: Total number of net new, non-exempt, pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.3.C. (Exemptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.3), [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

         P: Average number of people per occupied [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) as determined by the most recent version of the U.S. Census for the City of Los Angeles.

         F1: Park service factor for [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, as indicated by the Department of Recreation and Parks rate and fee schedule.

      2. ###### Non-Subdivision Projects:


         LD = (HU x P) x F2

         LD: Land to be dedicated in acres.

         HU: Total number of net new, non-exempt, pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.3.C. (Exemptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.3), [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.

         P: Average number of people per occupied [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) as determined by the most recent version of the U.S. Census for the City of Los Angeles.

         F2: Park service factor for non-subdivision [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s, as indicated by the Department of Recreation and Parks rate and fee schedule.
2. ###### Improvement to Dedicated Land


      In lieu of paying the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or any portion thereof, the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) may permit improvements to be made to dedicated [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) parkland, or land being dedicated as a [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) park or recreational facility.

3. ###### General


      1. The total amount of credits shall not exceed 100 percent of the calculated requirement for the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or land dedication.

      2. Credit shall be granted for the property dedicated pursuant to this Division (Park Fees & Dedications), dollar for dollar, in satisfaction of any [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) required to be paid. The cost and subsequent credit should bear a reasonable relationship to an independent assessment of the construction cost for the facility, such as the estimates provided by RSMeans Building Construction Cost Data or similar measure. Credits may be awarded for on-site or off-site land dedication or park improvements.

      3. The Department of Recreation and Parks shall determine whether the proposal complies with the Department's park and recreational standards and requirements. If the Department determines the proposal meets the Department's standards and requirements, the General Manager of the Department of Recreation and Parks shall prepare a report to the Board of Recreation and Parks Commissioners regarding the proposed dedication or improvement. The Board of Recreation and Parks Commissioners may accept or decline the [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), new park and recreational facility, or improvement to existing park and facilities.

      4. If the dedication or improvement is accepted by the Board of Recreation and Parks Commissioners in lieu of the [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or any portion thereof, the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall reduce or waive the fee, or [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or any portion thereof, upon dedication of the property or guarantee of the improvement. The guarantee of the improvement shall be to the satisfaction of the Department of Recreation and Parks and shall be by a deposit with the Department of Recreation and Parks of an irrevocable deposit instrument issued by a bank, savings and loan association or other depository whose deposits are insured by an instrumentality of the federal government. The deposit shall be fully insured by such instrumentality. The deposit instrument shall be in a form that permits collection by the City of Los Angeles at maturity without further consent of any other party.
2. ##### Privately Owned Park & Recreational Facilities


1. Where facilities for park and recreational purposes are provided in a proposed [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) development and such facilities will be privately owned and maintained by the future owners of the development, the areas occupied by such facilities shall be partially credited against the requirement of [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for park and recreational purposes or the payment of a [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) thereof, provided that all the following standards are met to the satisfaction of the Department of Recreation and Parks:

      1. That each facility is available for use by all the [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s of the [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) development;

      2. That the area and the facilities satisfy the recreation and park needs of the [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) development so as to reduce the need for public recreation and park facilities to serve the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s.
2. The amount of credits for non-publicly accessible park and recreational facilities shall not exceed 35 percent of the calculated requirement for the park and recreation impact fee or [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). Credits may be awarded for on-site or off-site private facilities.

3. The amount of credits for [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), privately owned and maintained park and recreational facilities shall not exceed 100 percent of the calculated requirement for the park and recreation impact fee or [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). Credits may be awarded for on-site or off-site private facilities.

4. Private park and recreational facilities shall include a variety of active and passive amenities, as determined by the Department of Recreation and Parks.

5. Credit shall be granted, dollar for dollar, for any recreational and park impact fees required to be paid for the property pursuant to this Division (Park Fees & Dedications), as determined by the Department of Recreation and Parks. The cost and subsequent credit should bear a reasonable relationship to an independent assessment of the construction cost for the facility, such as the estimates provided by RSMeans Building Construction Cost Data or similar.

6. Credits shall not be given for any [lot amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or [residential amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) required to be maintained by this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A), [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), or any other planning document, with the exception of [public amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s provided in accordance with [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.3. (Public Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3).

7. The granting of credits shall also be subject to all the following:

      1. The private ownership and maintenance of the facilities shall be adequately provided for by written agreements;

      2. The use of the private facilities, whether [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or non-publicly accessible, is restricted for park and recreational purposes by recorded covenants acceptable to the Department of Recreation and Parks that run with the land and that cannot be defeated or eliminated without the consent of the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#);

      3. The proposed facilities are reasonably adaptable for use for park and recreational purposes, taking into consideration such factors as size, shape, topography, geology, access, and location of the private open space land;

      4. The proposed non-public facilities are available for use by all the [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s of the proposed [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) development;

      5. Any proposed [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), privately owned and maintained park and recreational facilities are accessible for use by the general public with no discrimination between [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s and non-residents, are open at hours comparable to those of [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) parks and facilities, and have appropriate signage indicating that the space is public; and

      6. The facilities are in substantial accordance with, and meet the policies and standards for, the development of park and recreational facilities.
3. ##### Dwelling Unit Construction Tax Credit


A credit shall be allowed whenever a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) construction tax previously has been paid pursuant to [Chapter II. (Licenses, Permits, Business Regulations), Sec. 21.10.3. (Dwelling Unit Construction Tax)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-127121) of this Code for [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s constructed on land for which a fee is required to be paid in accordance with the provisions of this Division (Park Fees & Dedications). Said credit shall be equal to the amount of the tax previously paid, but shall not exceed the amount of any fee required to be paid under the provisions of this Division (Park Fees & Dedications).

4. ##### Credit Request Timing


The [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) applicant shall submit any requests for credit, and the Department of Recreation and Parks may only approve such requests, prior to the approval of the [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or prior to the date of final inspection, or the date of the [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#), whichever is earliest and applicable, and prior to any [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) or payment of any [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).


### Sec. 10.4.9. Park Fee Account & Accounting

1. ##### Park Fee Account


The City of Los Angeles establishes a separate park and recreation fee trust fund account ("account") to which any [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) collected by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall be posted. The funds of the account shall not be commingled with any other funds or revenues of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). Any interest accrued by the account shall be used solely for the purposes of park and recreational facility acquisition, addition, and improvement.

2. ##### Park Fee Accounting


Within 180 days after the last day of each fiscal year, the Department of Recreation and Parks shall report to the Board of Commissioners of Recreation and Parks on the amount of the fee income (including interest income), expenditures, status of the trust fund account, and interfund transfers. The Department of Recreation and Parks shall also report on each of the park and recreational facilities on which fees were committed in the last fiscal year and the approximate date by which the construction of the park and recreational facilities will commence. The [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) shall maintain accounts and prepare reports in accordance with [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66001](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66001.&lawCode=GOV).

3. ##### Refund of Fees Under the California Government Code


1. [Park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s collected pursuant to this Division (Park Fees & Dedications) shall be committed by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) within five years of receipt of payment for a [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) to serve or benefit [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for which the fees were collected.

2. If the fees are not committed as specified in this Division (Park Fees & Dedications), Quimby fees shall be refunded in accordance with [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66477](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66477.&lawCode=GOV). All other [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s shall be refunded in accordance with [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66001](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66001.&lawCode=GOV).
4. ##### Other Refunds


In the event that an applicant requests a refund for reasons not set forth in [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66001.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66001.&lawCode=GOV) or [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66477.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66477.&lawCode=GOV), the applicant shall submit a claim for a refund with the Department of Recreation and Parks. Upon the Department of Recreation and Park's determination, the fee payer may receive a refund, without interest, of the fees paid pursuant to this Division (Park Fees & Dedications); however, the portion of any fee revenue received by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) as reimbursement of its costs in administering the provisions of this Division (Park Fees & Dedications) shall not be refunded. The fee payer shall submit an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for a refund to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) within one year of payment. Failure to timely submit the required [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) for refund shall constitute an absolute waiver of any right to the refund.


### Sec. 10.4.10. Use of Park Fees or Lands Dedicated

1. The dedicated lands or [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) s collected pursuant to this Division (Park Fees & Dedications) shall be used for the acquisition, improvement, and expansion of public parks and recreational facilities. The fees shall be committed and expended in accordance with the provisions and procedures established in this Division (Park Fees & Dedications). The [park fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) may be used to pay the principal sum and interest and other finance costs on bonds, notes or other obligations issued by, or on behalf of, the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) to finance such park and recreational facility improvements; and any administrative costs incurred by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) in accordance with this Division (Park Fees & Dedications).

2. Interest accrued on Quimby in-lieu fees collected pursuant to this Division (Park Fees & Dedications) may be applied outside the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) development for which the original fees were collected, provided that the Department of Recreation and Parks holds a public hearing prior to committing the interest, and uses the interest to develop new or rehabilitate existing neighborhood or community parks or recreational facilities within the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#). All such public parks and recreational facilities shall comply with the principles and standards set forth in the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#).

3. The park or recreational facilities acquired, improved or expanded shall be publicly accessible and serve or benefit the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#) that dedicated the land or paid the fees.

# Article 11. Division of Land

## Div. 11.1. General Rules

### Sec. 11.1.1. General

1. ##### Scope


1. No [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may subdivide land in the City of Los Angeles unless a [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) (for [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s of five or more [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) (for [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s of four or less [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s) has been recorded as provided in this Article (Division of Land) and in accordance with [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7).

2. No building or structure shall be constructed or enlarged on any land which has been subdivided in violation of the provisions of this Article (Division of Land) and [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7), nor shall any permit be issued for such land.

3. The provisions of this Article (Division of Land) shall not be construed as preventing the recording of a [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) containing less than five [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s or creating fewer than five [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) units in accordance with the procedures outlined in [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7) and the [Subdivision Map Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).
2. ##### Applicability


The provisions of this Article (Division of Land) are applicable to a [commercial/industrial conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), [commercial/industrial to residential conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), [residential conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), or [residential to commercial/industrial conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), as defined in [Div. 14.3. (Glossary)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.3), except as follows:

1. ###### Stock Cooperative Conversions


      The provisions of this Article (Division of Land) do not apply to any conversion for [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) purposes that satisfies either of the following criteria:

      1. The [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) for [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) (DRE Form 658 or its equivalent) was filed with the [California Department of Real Estate](https://www.dre.ca.gov/) prior to July 1, 1979; or

      2. A [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) public report for [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) was issued in accordance with [California Business and Professions Code, Sec. 11018.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=11018.&lawCode=BPC) prior to November 10, 1979.
2. ###### New Stock Cooperatives


      The provisions of this Article (Division of Land) do not apply to any [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) for which the application for [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) (DRE Form 658 or its equivalent) was filed with the [California Department of Real Estate](https://www.dre.ca.gov/) prior to March 21, 1980, with the exception of [commercial/industrial conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, [commercial/industrial to residential conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, [residential conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, or [residential to commercial/industrial conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, which must meet the criteria outlined in Paragraph 1. (Stock Cooperative Conversions) above in order to qualify for exemption.

3. ###### Subdivision of Air Space


      The provisions of this Article (Division of Land) apply to any division of the space above or below a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) with a definite width, length, and upper and lower [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) occupied or to be occupied by a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), group of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s or portions of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, and [accessory building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s or portions of [accessory building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, or [accessory use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s. ( [Air space lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), as defined in [Div. 14.3. (Glossary)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.3)).
3. ##### Intent


1. The intent of this Article (Division of Land) is to regulate and control the division of land within the City of Los Angeles, to provide for the [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), the payment of fees in lieu of [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), or a combination of both, for the acquisition and development of park and recreation sites and facilities to serve the future inhabitants of the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), to supplement the provisions of the [Subdivision Map Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) concerning the [subdivision design](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), [subdivision improvement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) and survey data of [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, the form and content of [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), and [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s. The procedure to be followed in securing the official approval of the City of Los Angeles on such maps shall be completed in accordance with [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7), in a manner that is consistent with the applicable general and specific plans as well as the public health, safety, and welfare.

2. It is also the intention of this Article (Division of Land) that the subdividing of land in the City of Los Angeles be done in accordance with the [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) regulations of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) contained and set forth in [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Article 1. (Building Code)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-172105) of this Code and to establish, when possible, beauty and attractiveness in the hills consistent with watershed drainage, erosion, and fire control requirements, and good engineering practices.
4. ##### Interpretation


1. ###### Private Streets


      This Article (Division of Land) and [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7) is not to be interpreted or construed to invalidate any previous act on the part of the City approving or authorizing [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, or authorizing the issuance of [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s for structures on [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s served by [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s.

2. ###### Planning Commission


      Unless otherwise specified, further references in this Article (Division of Land) to “Planning Commission” mean either the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), whichever has authority.

### Sec. 11.1.2. Advisory Agency

1. ##### Additional Authority


1. The [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) has the authority to grant deviations of no more than 20 percent from the applicable [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), and height requirements. The [subdivider](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall ask for adjustments at the time of filing for a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

2. In permitting adjustments, the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall make the findings contained in [Sec. 13B.5.2. (Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.2). The reductions or deviations shall be included in the written decision of the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

3. Notification and appeal rights to such reductions or deviations shall conform to [Sec. 13B.7.2. (Parcel Map Exemption/Lot Line Adjustment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7.2).

### Sec. 11.1.3. Subdivision Design Standards

01. ##### Conformance to the General Plan


    1. Each [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall be designed in compliance with the zoning applicable to the property or approved by the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) for change, or will be subject to a condition requiring compliance with such zoning prior to the recordation of the [final map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

    2. Where a [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) involves land for which a [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) including [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) densities has been adopted by the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), and the land is also in a [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), the number of [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s on the map shall be limited so that the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s permitted by the applicable zoning regulations does not substantially exceed the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) densities shown on the plan.

    3. Each [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall substantially conform to all other elements of the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). In computing the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, only the area being designated for [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s and land that is being dedicated for public & institutional uses shall be considered, excepting, however, land set aside for street purposes, or [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) required for park and recreation purposes in accordance with [Article 10. (Streets & Parks)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10).

    4. ###### Dwelling Unit Density in the Hillside Area


       1. In the [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), which is designated in the "Minimum Residential" [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) land use designation, the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) density shall not exceed that allowed by the following formula:

          [![](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/large/public/zcode_images/2025.1.0/11.1.3.1.png.webp?itok=VjSCjaHE)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/styles/larger/public/zcode_images/2025.1.0/11.1.3.1.png?itok=G7Dpl1hm)

          Where :

          D = the maximum number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s per gross acre allowable; and

           S = the [average natural slope](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) of the land in percent.

       2. Where the total allowable number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s per [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) calculated under the above formula results in a number other than a whole number, it shall be rounded to the nearest whole number as follows:

          1. Where the fractional portion of the total allowable number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s equals 0.5 or more, the total number of allowable [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s shall be rounded to the next larger whole number;

          2. Where the fractional portion of the total allowable number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s equals less than 0.5, the total number of allowable [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s shall be rounded to the next smaller whole number.
       3. In no case may the permitted density be less than 0.05 [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s per gross acre. Where the total allowable number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s per [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) calculated under the above formula results in a number less than one, it shall be rounded up to allow one [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) per [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). Where previous [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) makes it difficult to determine [average natural slope](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) using the above formula, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall determine the [average natural slope](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) in a manner to carry out the purpose and intent of this Section (Subdivision Design Standards).
02. ##### Streets


    1. ###### Public Right-of-Way & Roadway Widths


       All streets and [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s shall be designed to conform with the Planning Commission’s adopted standards. The requirements and exceptions set forth in [Article 10. (Streets & Parks)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10), however, do apply.

    2. ###### Street Grades


       1. [Grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s of all streets shall be as flat as consistent with adequate surface drainage requirements and the approved development of the proposed [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). The minimum [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) permitted is 0.4 percent, except in extremely flat areas where a [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) of 0.2 percent may be used. The maximum [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) permitted for streets designated as [boulevard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [avenue](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) is 6 percent, except where a [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) not to exceed 10 percent will eliminate excessive curvature, fill, or excavation. The maximum [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) permitted for [collector street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s is 10 percent and for [local street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s is 15 percent. Variations from these requirements may be granted by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) upon recommendation by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) in individual cases in accordance with the provisions of [Sec. 13B.7.7. (Private Street Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7.7).

       2. Changes in [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) greater than 0.4 percent shall be connected by vertical curves. The length of vertical curves shall conform to standards for sight distance and riding qualities established by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).
    3. ###### Future Streets


       In the event certain streets or [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) are to be reserved for future public use and they have been approved as to location and width, they shall be indicated on the [final map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) and offered for dedication as future streets or future [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s. Certificates providing that the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may accept the offer to dedicate such [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) at any time shall be shown on the [final map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

    4. ###### Corner Cut-Off


       At all [block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) corners, the property line shall be rounded. On all [boulevard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s and [avenue](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, the corner shall have a 20-foot radius curve and on all other streets, a 15-foot radius curve; provided, however, that where commercial development is permitted, a diagonal cutoff of 15 feet × 15 feet in lieu of a 20-foot radius curve and a ten-foot × ten-foot cutoff in lieu of a 15-foot radius curve may be used. In industrial districts, the curves shall have a minimum radius of at least 40 feet.

    5. ###### Horizontal Curves


       The centerline radii of curves shall be as large as possible, consistent with conditions. All curves shall have sufficient length to avoid the appearance of an angle point. Reversing curves shall be connected by tangents of length approved by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) as sufficient to safely reverse the unbalanced centrifugal force. In any case, horizontal curves shall have the following minimum centerline radii:

       1. [Boulevard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s and [avenue](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s: 1,000 feet

       2. [Collector street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s: 500 feet

       3. [Local street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s: 300 feet

       4. [Local street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in a [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#): 125 feet
    6. ###### Intersections


       Street intersections shall be as near to a right angle as possible. No jogs are allowed in the continuity of an arterial street. Jogs in a non-arterial street where crossing an arterial street shall be held to a minimum. Multiple intersections of more than four approaches should be avoided. In [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, special conditions may be required.

    7. ###### Cul-de-Sac Streets


       Cul-de-sac streets should be avoided, except in locations where physical constraints prohibit the continuation of the street (such as where a river or railroad infrastructure is present) or where made necessary by historical development patterns. Where cul-de-sac streets are approved, they shall be terminated by a turning area conforming to the latest standards approved by the Planning Commission. Where feasible, existing cul-de-sacs should be modified and new cul-de-sacs should be designed to include a passageway for bicycles and pedestrians to access the surrounding area.

    8. ###### General


       1. All streets within or immediately adjacent to the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall be improved with curbs and gutters, unless not required by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) upon recommendation of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

       2. Streets within or immediately adjacent to the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall be improved with sidewalks, except that in mountainous, hillside or rural areas, sidewalks may be omitted or may be provided on only one side of the street with the approval of the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).
03. ##### Alleys


    1. [Alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s shall be not less than 20 feet in width. [Alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s serving [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in an [Industrial Use District (Div. 5B.7.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.7) shall be not less than 30 feet wide, unless otherwise approved by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

    2. All dead-end [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s shall be constructed with adequate turning areas.

    3. Whenever practicable, [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s are required at the rear of all [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s that are in [Residential Use Districts (Div. 5B.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.3) and that front an arterial street. [Alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s may also be required at the rear of [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in [Commercial-Mixed Use Districts (Div. 5B.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.5) or [Industrial Use Districts (Div. 5B.7.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.7).

    4. Where two [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s intersect, a triangular corner cut-off of not less than 10 feet along each [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) line shall be provided.

    5. [Residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) waste collectors shall not be required to collect from an unpaved [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) at the rear of a property or from:

       1. A blind [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#);

       2. An [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) less than 15 feet wide;

       3. An [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) which is "L" or "T" shaped and not wide enough to be safe for the waste collection truck to turn without damage to the truck or to adjacent improvements on private property; or

       4. An [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) the surface of which could endanger the safety or the convenient operation of the trucks at all seasons of the year.
04. ##### Pedestrian Walkways


    If the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) determines that inner-block [pedestrian walkway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s are necessary for the public health, safety or welfare, they shall be dedicated to a width of not less than 12 feet. The [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), however, shall only impose such a dedication requirement after finding that the dedication bears an essential nexus and rough proportionality to a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#)'s impact.

05. ##### Blocks


    [Block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in [Residential Use Districts (Div. 5B.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.3), [Residential-Mixed Use Districts (Div.5B.4.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.4), and [Industrial Use Districts (Div. 5B.7.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.7) areas shall not exceed 1,700 feet in length, except in a [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). [Block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in [Commercial-Mixed Use Districts (Div. 5B.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.5) shall not exceed 800 feet in length except in locations where the prevailing [block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) length (within 1/2-mile) is less than 800 feet. In such instance, the new [block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall not exceed the average prevailing [block](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) length.

06. ##### Lot Size


    01. Every [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall have a minimum width and area to comply with the requirements specified in the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).

    02. When the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) determines that traffic access, topography, and drainage conditions will safely allow [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) averaging, and when the [subdivider](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) has demonstrated to the satisfaction of the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) in a written report that such averaging is consistent with proper [subdivision design](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), and in addition will produce one or more of the following benefits: require less [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) than a conventional [subdivision design](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) not using [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) averaging, result in improved [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) design, or produce other environmental benefits, the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may permit the width and area of not more than 20 percent of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) located in a [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), to be reduced as specified below, provided that the average area of all [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) is not less than the required minimum for the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).




        | Lot Area in Square Feet |
        | --- |
        | Form District | Lot Width (min) | Lot Area (min) | Lot Average (min) |
        | --- | --- | --- | --- |
        | Rural-Limited | 63 feet | 14,000 | 17,500 |
        | Estate-Limited 5 | No Reduction | 32,00 | 40,000 |
        | Estate-Limited 4 | 72 feet | 16,000 | 20,000 |
        | Estate-Limited 3 | 72 feet | 12,000 | 15,000 |
        | Estate-Limited 2 | 63 feet | 8,800 | 11,000 |
        | Estate-Limited 1 | 60 feet | 7,200 | 9,000 |

    03. In computing such average, that portion of any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) exceeding 150 percent of the average requirement shall not be included, provided however, that in Rural-Limited Form Districts, the maximum area of any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) that may be used in computing the average shall be 24,500 square feet.

    04. In a tract where one or more [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s have less than the average requirement for the applicable [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B), no [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may be rearranged or divided unless:

        1. The average requirement for the original [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) is maintained; and

        2. Such rearrangement or division is accomplished by recording a new [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), or by securing determination that the proposed rearrangement or division is exempt from the [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) procedure in [Sec. 11.4.1.B.3.c. (Scope)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.4.1).
    05. Where it finds it necessary in order to promote the general welfare, the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may require that [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s that are contiguous or nearby to existing [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s on the same street be increased in size to be compatible with the size of the existing [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s. However, in no case may the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) require such [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s to contain an area of over 50 percent more than that required by the applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) or [Alternate Typology (Article 7.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/7).

    06. Property in a [Commercial-Mixed Use District (Div. 5B.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.5) or [Industrial Use District (Div. 5B.7.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B.7) need not be divided into more than one [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) where such property is to be operated as a unit.

    07. Each portion of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) which is platted to be divided by a City or County boundary line shall be given a separate letter or number on the recorded [tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

    08. Side [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s shall be approximately at right angles to the streets, or radial to the street on curved streets, except where topography or other conditions make this impracticable.

    09. Where it finds that there will be no material increase in the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) density permitted by the applied zone, and that the public health, safety or welfare, and good subdivision design would be promoted by the dedication of public streets to a width in excess of the approved standards provided for in this Article (Division of Land), or the dedication of service roads, or the dedication or reservation of land for public parks, public [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s or other open areas, the Advisory Agency may permit the required area of one or more of the lots in a subdivision in an Rural-Limited or Estate-Limited Form Districts to be reduced to the extent of such dedication or reservation. Provided, however, that in no event may such a reduction exceed 15 percent, and no [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) in the Rural-Limited or Estate-Limited Form Districts in a [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall be reduced below the minimum [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) specified in the table in Paragraph 2. (Lot Size) above.

    10. Where the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) finds the project is consistent with the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) density permitted by the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), and that the public health, safety or welfare, and good [subdivision design](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) will be promoted by the preservation of [protected vegetation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may permit the required area of one or more of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) in Rural-Limited, Estate-Limited, or House-Limited Form Districts to be reduced by an amount sufficient to provide for [protected vegetation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) preservation in accordance with [Sec. 11.1.3.P. (Protected Vegetation Regulations)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.1.3). In no event may the reduction exceed 50 percent of the required [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#); [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in Rural-Limited or Estate-Limited Form Districts may not be reduced below 50 feet in width; [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s in House-Limited Form Districts may not be reduced below 40 feet in width.
07. ##### Easements


    1. [Easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s for public utilities, water systems, sewers, street lights, storm drains or flood control channels, and slope rights, shall be provided wherever determined necessary by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) upon recommendation of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

    2. Wherever it is determined that future [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s are necessary, a certificate shall be placed on the [final map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) indicating that the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) will accept such [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s at any time.
08. ##### Grading in Hillside Areas


    [Subdivision design](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) requirements in a [Hillside Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall meet the [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) standards established by the Board of Public Works and the [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) regulations established in [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Article 1. (Building Code)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-172105) of this Code. Such requirements may also include providing soil reports prepared by a [registered civil engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) specializing in soil mechanics or reports on geological investigations.

09. ##### Problem Areas


    Areas designated by resolution of the Board of Public Works as [problem areas](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall not be subdivided except when approved by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) upon recommendation of the Superintendent of Building and the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

10. ##### Grading Plans


    1. The [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may require a proposed [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) plan with the [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) of any [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). Upon recommendation of the Superintendent of Building or the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), or where it appears that cuts and fills will occur in the [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) of the property that may be contrary to the objectives of this Article (Division of Land), the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may require the [subdivider](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) to submit [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) plans for all or part of the tract before action on the [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) will be taken. Any [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) plan submitted shall contain a statement of the quantities (in cubic yards) of cut and fill and quantities of export or import material involved. If the amount of earth material to be imported to or exported from a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) site is 1,000 cubic yards or more, statements of the following shall also be included:

       1. The proposed borrow or disposal site;

       2. The proposed haul route;

       3. The total gross weight with load of the proposed haul vehicles; and

       4. Any other pertinent data which the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) may require.
    2. Failure to furnish a grading plan (where necessary to complete the investigation of the [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) within the time specified in the written notice requesting its submission) will be cause for the disapproval of the [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) or [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), unless an extension of the time for acting on the map is mutually agreed upon between the [subdivider](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) and the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#).

    3. If changes in the design of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s or street system can be made to correct the conditions set forth in Subsection H. (Grading in Hillside Areas) above, either by increased [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) sizes or changes in [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s, such modifications shall be made.
11. ##### Storm Drains


    Storm drains shall be designed in conformance with standards approved by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). Storm drain facilities to intercept and convey all runoff to a suitable point of disposal are required when runoff from the entire area tributary to and including the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) exceeds the limiting depth of street flow as determined by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#). These storm drain requirements shall also include the following:

    1. In areas without sumps, storm drains shall be designed to remove all runoff from a storm of 10-year frequency.

    2. In sump areas, storm drains shall be designed to remove all runoff from a storm of 50-year frequency.

    3. Storm drains shall be of sufficient capacity in all cases to prevent flooding of [building site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s from a storm of 50-year frequency.

    4. On hillside limited streets, the maximum depth of water as determined by the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) shall be based on a storm of 50-year frequency.
12. ##### Installation of Utilities


    1. Utility lines, including but not limited to those required for electricity, communication, street lighting, and cableservices necessary for the general [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) owners in the [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#), shall be installed or guaranteed to be installed in the same manner as other required [subdivision improvement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#) s.

    2.
