      The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall render a determination on any [Certificate of Compatibility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within 75 days after the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is deemed complete, unless the applicant and the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) mutually consent in writing to a longer period.

9. ###### Transmittal


      A copy of the determination shall be mailed to the applicant, the Historic Preservation Board, and any other interested parties. No [Certificate of Compatibility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be deemed approved or issued until the time period for appeal has expired.
5. ##### Standards for Issuance of a Certificate of Compatibility for New Building Construction or Replacement, and the Relocation of Buildings or Structures Not Dating from the Preservation Zone’s Period of Significance Onto a Lot Designated as a Non-Contributing Element


In making a determination on a [Certificate of Compatibility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) (on appeal) shall consider each of the following:

1. If no Preservation Plan exists, whether the following aspects of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) do not impair the essential form and integrity of the [historic](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) character of its surrounding built environment, considering the following factors:

      01. Architectural design;

      02. Height, bulk, and massing of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s and [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s;

      03. [Lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) coverage and orientation of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s;

      04. Color and texture of surface materials;

      05. [Grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) development;

      06. [Landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#);

      07. Changes to [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s;

      08. Steps, [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, fencing, doors, [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, screens, and security grills;

      09. [Yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s and setbacks;

      10. Off street [parking](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#);

      11. Light fixtures and street furniture;

      12. Antennas, satellite dishes and solar collectors; or

      13. [Sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s; and
2. [New construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall not destroy [historic](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) features or materials that characterize the property. The design of new construction shall subtly differentiate the [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) from the surrounding [historic](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) built fabric, and shall be contextually compatible with the massing, size, scale, and architectural features of nearby [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s in the [HPOZ](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#); or

3. Whether the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) complies with the Preservation Plan approved by the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for the [HPOZ](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
6. ##### Scope of Decision


See [Sec. 13A.2.7. (Scope of Decision)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.7).

7. ##### Appeals


1. ###### General Procedures


      See [Sec. 13A.2.8. (Appeals)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.8).

2. ###### Decision Maker


      The [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is the appellate [decision maker](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

3. ###### Filing


      1. An appeal may be filed by the applicant, any aggrieved party, the [Mayor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), or a member of the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). Unless a Historic Preservation Board member is an applicant, he or she may not appeal any initial decision of the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) as it pertains to this Section.

      2. An appeal shall be filed in triplicate, and the Planning Department shall forward a copy of the appeal to the Historic Preservation Board and the [Cultural Heritage Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
4. ###### Public Hearing


      Before acting on any appeal, the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall set the matter for hearing, giving notice in the manner specified in Subsection C. (Notice) above.

5. ###### Appellate Decision


      1. The [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) may grant, conditionally grant, or deny the appeal.

      2. The [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall render its decision within 75 days after the expiration of the appeal period or within an additional period as may be agreed upon by the applicant and the appellate body.

      3. Failure of the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) to submit a timely decision shall be deemed a denial of the appeal, and the original action on the matter shall become final.
8. ##### Modification of Entitlement


1. ###### Modification of an Approved Certificate of Compatibility


      Once a [Certificate of Compatibility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) becomes effective, any subsequent proposed modification to the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall require review by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), who shall approve the modification if he or she finds the modification to be substantially in conformance with the original approved [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). If the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) finds that the proposed modification does not substantially conform to the original approved [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), then the applicant shall resubmit the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for a new [Certificate of Compatibility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

2. ###### Modification Procedure


      To modify an approved [Certificate of Compatibility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), an applicant shall submit to the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) plans, [building elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, or details of the proposed modification and any additional information determined necessary for conformance review. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) may forward proposed modifications to the Historic Preservation Board and/or the [Cultural Heritage Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)’s designee for consultation.

### Div. 13B.9. Coastal Development

#### Sec. 13B.9.1. Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification)

Purpose. It is the purpose of this Section to provide for the approval or denial of Coastal Development Permits, prior to the certification of the [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), in accordance with [California Public Resources Code, Sec. 30600(b)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30600.&lawCode=PRC). In adopting the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976 the State Legislature finds and declares:

•That the California [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is a distinct and valuable natural resource of vital and enduring interest to all the people and exists as a delicately balanced ecosystem.

•That the permanent protection of the State's natural and scenic resources is a paramount concern to present and future [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s of the State and nation.

•That to promote the public safety, health, and welfare, and to protect public and private property, wildlife, marine fisheries, and other ocean resources, and the natural environment, it is necessary to protect the ecological balance of the [coastal zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and to prevent its deterioration and destruction.

1. ##### Applicability


1. ###### Definitions


      For the purpose of this Section the following words and phrases are defined:

      Aggrieved Person: Any person who, in person or through a representative, appeared at a hearing on the application for a Coastal Development Permit, or appeal hearing in connection with the decision or action appealed, or who, by other appropriate means prior to a hearing, informed the permit issuing authority, or appeal body of the nature of his or her concerns or who for good cause was unable to do either. "Aggrieved person" includes the applicant for a Coastal Development Permit.

      Coastal Zone: That land and water area within the City as specified on maps prepared by the California Coastal Commission, copies of which are on file with the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and the Office of [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). Such "Coastal Zone" extends seaward to the City's outer limit of jurisdiction, and generally extends inland 1000 yards from the mean high tide line of the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). In significant coastal estuarine, habitat and recreational areas it extends inland to the first major ridgeline paralleling the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or five miles from the mean high tide line of the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), whichever is less, and in developed urban areas the zone extends inland 1000 yards.

      Development: On land, in or under water, the placement or erection of any solid material or structure; discharge or disposal of any dredged material or of any gaseous, liquid, solid, or thermal waste; grading, removing, dredging, mining, or extraction of any materials; change in the density or intensity of the use of land, including, but not limited to, [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s pursuant to the [Subdivision Map Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) (commencing with [Sec. 66410 of the California Government Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66410.&lawCode=GOV)), and any other division of land, including, but not limited to, parcel maps and [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) divisions, lot splits, lot reconfigurations, and mergers, except where the land division is brought about in connection with the purchase of such land by a public agency for public recreational use; change in the intensity of use of water, or of access thereto; construction, [reconstruction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), demolition, or alteration of the size of any structure, including any facility of any private, public, or municipal utility; and the removal or harvesting of major vegetation other than for agricultural purposes, kelp harvesting, and timber operations which are in accordance with a timber harvesting plan submitted pursuant to the provisions of the [Z'berg-Nejedly Forest Practice Act of 1973 (commencing with Sec. 4511 of the California Public Resources Code)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=4511.&lawCode=PRC). As used in this definition, "structure" includes, but is not limited to, any building, road, pipe, flume, conduit, siphon, aqueduct, telephone line, and electrical power transmission and distribution line.

      Feasible: Capable of being accomplished in a successful manner within a reasonable period of time, taking into account economic, environmental, social and technological factors.

      Local Coastal Program (LCP): The City's land use plans and other applicable general plan elements, zoning ordinances, zoning district maps, and proposed implementing actions, which when taken together, meet the requirements of, and implement the provisions and policies of, the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976.

      Permit: Any license, certificate, approval, or other entitlement for use granted, conditionally granted, or denied by any public agency, which is subject to the provisions of this Section.

      Public Project: Any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) initiated by the Department of Public Works or any of its bureaus, any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) initiated by any other department or agency of the City, and any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) initiated or to be carried out by any other governmental agency which is required to obtain a local government permit. Public Project shall not include any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by any department or agency of the City or any other governmental entity which otherwise requires action by or approval of the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or the Office of Zoning Administration, or any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by any department or agency of the City or any other government entity for which a permit from the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is required. Public Project shall also not include any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on tidelands, submerged lands, or on public trust lands, whether filled or unfilled. (Definition Amended by Ord. No. 173,268, eff. 7/1/00, Oper. 7/1/00.)

      Sea: The Pacific Ocean and all harbors, bays, channels, canals, estuaries, salt marshes, sloughs and other areas subject to tidal action through any connection with the Pacific Ocean, excluding non-estuarine rivers, streams, tributaries, creeks, and flood control and drainage channels.

2. ###### Use


      No [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be undertaken in the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) unless and until an application for such [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) has been submitted to the City for a Coastal Development Permit and such Permit has been obtained from the appropriate City Department in conformance with the provisions of this Section and has become final. Where the particular coastal [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) requires a Coastal Development Permit from the Commission in addition to the one obtained from the City, no [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) may be commenced until both such permits have been obtained, and both have become final.

      Exception

      The provisions of this Section shall not apply to [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s which do not need locally issued Coastal Development Permits under the Coastal Act of 1976 or [Division 5.5 Title 14 California Coastal Commission Regulations, of the California Code of Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Browse/Home/California/CaliforniaCodeofRegulations?guid=I7C4EEF405B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3&originationContext=documenttoc&transitionType=Default&contextData=(sc.Default)). A current copy of these regulations is on file with the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and the Office of [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). This exception shall not relieve any person from obtaining from the proper authority a Coastal Development Permit for a [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) where such permit is required but can only be issued by the California Coastal Commission or the Executive Director. The provisions of this Section shall also not apply to any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on tidelands, submerged lands, or on public trust lands, whether filled or unfilled; any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by a public agency for which a local government permit is not otherwise required; any emergency repair authorized by [Sec. 30611 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30611.&lawCode=PRC); any permits authorized to be issued by the Executive Director of the California Coastal Commission pursuant to [Sec. 30624 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30624.&lawCode=PRC); and any other permits over which the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is not authorized to exercise the option provided for in [Subdivision (b) of Sec. 30600 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30600.&lawCode=PRC).
2. ##### Initiation


Proceedings for a Permit shall be initiated by the filing of a verified application upon a form or forms prescribed for that purpose. An application for a Coastal Development Permit for a [public project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), or for a private [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) where the approval for the underlying permit is within the jurisdiction of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be filed in the public office of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). All other applications for Coastal Development Permits shall be filed in a public office of the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

1. All applications filed with the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be accompanied by the following data:

      1. An adequate description of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) including, but not limited to maps, plans, photographs, drawings, etc., of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and vicinity sufficient to determine whether the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) complies with all relevant policies of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976. Each application shall contain sufficient information concerning land and water areas in the vicinity of the site of the proposed [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), (whether or not owned or controlled by the applicant) so that the permit issuing authority will be adequately informed as to present uses and plans, both public and private, insofar as they can reasonably be ascertained for the vicinity surrounding the [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). The description of the [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall also include any [feasible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) alternatives or any [feasible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) mitigation measures available which would substantially lessen any significant adverse impact which the [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) may have on the environment. For purposes of this Section the term "significant adverse impact on the environment" shall be defined as in the [California Environmental Quality Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and the State and City Guidelines adopted pursuant thereto.

      2. A description and documentation of the applicant's legal interest in the property on which the [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is to be located if the application were approved (e.g., ownership, leasehold, enforceable option, authority to acquire the specific property by eminent domain.)

      3. A dated signature by or on behalf of each of the applicants, attesting to the truth, completeness, and accuracy of the contents of the application and, if the signer of the application is not the applicant, written evidence that the signer is authorized to act as the applicant's representative and to bind the applicant in all matters concerning the application.

      4. A statement of the status of the environmental documentation for the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and a copy of the required environmental documentation.

      5. Any additional information as may be required by the permit granting authority.
2. ###### Filing Exception


      Despite any other provisions of this Section or Code, an applicant may file an application for a Permit at any point of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) approval process relating to his or her [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). However, upon initiation of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) approval process by the applicant, said applicant shall sign and notarize a form prescribed for this purpose which shall contain the following:

      1. A statement advising the applicant that no permits or permission for a [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) in the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be issued unless and until a Permit has been approved in accordance with the provisions of this Section.

      2. A statement relieving the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of any legal or other responsibility in the event that failure to apply for a Permit results in, or contributes to, a violation of Sec. [65950](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=65950.&nodeTreePath=11.1.15.5&lawCode=GOV), [65951](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=65951.&nodeTreePath=11.1.15.5&lawCode=GOV), or [65952](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=65952.&nodeTreePath=11.1.15.5&lawCode=GOV) of the California Government Code.
3. ##### Notice


1. ###### Notice of Application – Posting


      At the time the application is submitted for filing, the applicant must post, at a conspicuous place, easily read by the public and as close as possible to the site of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) a notice that an application has been made for a Coastal Development Permit. Such notice shall contain specific information as to the nature of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and be in a form as prescribed for that purpose.

2. ###### Notice of Public Hearing – Mailing


      1. ###### Hearing on Coastal Development Permit Combined with Other Hearing


         The applicant shall furnish to the City, accompanying the application, a list containing the name and address of each property owner of record and the addresses of all residences, including apartments within 300 feet from each boundary of the site of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). Where the hearing on the Coastal Development Permit is to be combined with a public hearing otherwise required by this Code for the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), and the provisions of this Code require notification to persons beyond 300 feet of the site of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), no separate list shall be required, and all persons notified of the hearing for the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall also be notified that the hearing shall include the application for a Coastal Development Permit. Notice of such hearing, at least 24 days prior, shall also be sent to an occupant of all residences, including apartments within 300 feet of the boundary of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), all persons known, or thought to have a particular interest in the application, the Certified Neighborhood Council representing the area in which the property is located, and all other persons requesting notice.

      2. ###### Hearing on Coastal Development Permit Only


         For those [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s for which no hearing would otherwise be required by law, the appropriate City agency shall notify by mail, at least 24 days prior to the hearing, the following:

         1. Those persons whose names appear on the list of property owners within 300 feet of the boundary of the site of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#);

         2. An occupant of all residences, including apartments, within 300 feet of the boundary of the site of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). This requirement can be met by mailing such notice to "occupant" of the subject residence;

         3. Those persons known or thought to have a particular interest in the application;

         4. The Certified Neighborhood Council representing the area in which the property is located; and

         5. All other persons requesting notice.
3. ###### Charges for Notification


      No person requesting notification of any application, hearing, or decision by any permit granting authority or any notification of hearing or decision on any appeal therefrom shall be required to bear the cost of any such notification.
4. ##### Decision


1. ###### Proceedings and Hearing


      1. To the extent possible, any Permit application for a [Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be processed in accordance with established policies and procedures of a permit granting authority in conformance with the provisions of this Code.

      2. At the public hearing, all interested persons shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to testify and present evidence.
2. ###### Determination


      1. ###### Authority


         A permit granting authority, including any appellate body, shall have the authority to approve, conditionally approve, or disapprove any application for a Permit under the provisions of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976; and, standards as established by [Division 5.5 Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Browse/Home/California/CaliforniaCodeofRegulations?guid=I7C4EEF405B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3&originationContext=documenttoc&transitionType=Default&contextData=(sc.Default)).

      2. ###### Conditions of Approval


         In approving an application for a permit under the provisions of this Section, the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall impose such reasonable terms and conditions as it deems necessary to assure a [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that is in accordance with the provisions of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976 and those other criteria set forth in Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section.
3. ###### Notification of Determination


      A copy of the permit granting authority's action approving, conditionally approving, or disapproving any application for a Coastal Development Permit, along with any findings made and conditions imposed in connection therewith, shall be mailed to the applicant and to any person or persons who, in writing, request a copy of such action.

4. ###### Transmittal of Notice of Final Action to the Coastal Commission


      1. After the decision of the last appeal body, or the time within which any appeal can be taken has expired, the permit granting authority, including any appeal body whose action became final on the permit, shall [transmitted](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) a copy, by mail, with return receipt requested, of the notice of permit issuance or permit denial to the Executive Director of the Coastal Commission. Such notice shall include the requisite findings, a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) description, and a verbatim copy of any conditions attached to the permit, all as required by [Sec. 13302(g) of the California Coastal Commission Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I817460E85B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3?viewType=FullText&listSource=Search&originationContext=Search+Result&transitionType=SearchItem&contextData=(sc.Search)&navigationPath=Search%2fv1%2fresults%2fnavigation%2fi0a93d7db00000193d70ebbc9d6982e80%3fppcid%3df23b83f1bc474eefa7b2e293fe0d322a%26Nav%3dREGULATION_PUBLICVIEW%26fragmentIdentifier%3dI817460E85B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3%26startIndex%3d1%26transitionType%3dSearchItem%26contextData%3d%2528sc.Default%2529%26originationContext%3dSearch%2520Result&list=REGULATION_PUBLICVIEW&rank=1&t_T1=14&t_T2=13302&t_S1=CA+ADC+s). Notice shall also be mailed to the applicant, the appellant, and any persons who, in writing, requested such notice.

      2. The decision of the permit granting authority, or any appeal body to approve issuance of a permit shall not be deemed to be final and no Coastal Development Permit may be issued until 20 working days have expired from the date said notice of permit issuance is deemed received by said Executive Director and without an appeal having been taken to the Coastal Commission.

      3. If a timely, valid appeal is taken to the Coastal Commission, the operation and effect of the Coastal Development Permit is stayed pending final action on the appeal by the Coastal Commission, and the City shall within five working days of the receipt of such notice, deliver to the Executive Director copies of all relevant documents and materials used by the City in its consideration of the permit application.

      4. If no appeal is taken within 20 working days of the date of the notice of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)'s decision to issue a permit is deemed received by the Executive Director, the applicant may commence utilization of the permit. If no timely appeal is taken from the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)'s decision to deny a permit, such decision is final.

      5. Neither an applicant nor any other party may appeal the approval, conditional approval, or disapproval of any permit to the Coastal Commission unless and until the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) has completed its review of the permit application, has taken final action, and has formally notified the Coastal Commission that the Coastal Development Permit is final.
5. ##### Standards for Review and Required Findings


The permit granting authority shall have the authority to approve, conditionally approve or disapprove any application for a Permit under the provisions of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976; and, standards as established by [Division 5.5 Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Browse/Home/California/CaliforniaCodeofRegulations?guid=I7C4EEF405B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3&originationContext=documenttoc&transitionType=Default&contextData=(sc.Default)). In making its determination under the provisions of this Section, the permit granting authority, including any appellate body, shall not approve, or conditionally approve a permit unless it makes written findings, including specific factual findings, supporting the following conclusions:

1. That the [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is in conformity with [Chapter 3](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayexpandedbranch.xhtml?tocCode=PRC&division=20.&title=&part=&chapter=&article=&nodetreepath=43) of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976 (commencing with [Sec. 30200 of the California Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30200&lawCode=PRC)).

2. That the permitted [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) will not prejudice the ability of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) to prepare a [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that is in conformity with [Chapter 3](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayexpandedbranch.xhtml?tocCode=PRC&division=20.&title=&part=&chapter=&article=&nodetreepath=43) of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976.

3. That the Interpretative Guidelines for Coastal Planning and Permits as established by the California Coastal Commission dated February 11, 1977 and any subsequent amendments thereto have been reviewed, analyzed, and considered in the light of the individual [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) in making its determination.

4. That the decision of the permit granting authority has been guided by any applicable decision of the California Coastal Commission pursuant to [Sec. 30625(c) of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30625&lawCode=PRC).

5. If the [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is located between the nearest public road and the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or shoreline of any body of water located within the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that the [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is in conformity with the public [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and public recreation policies of [Chapter 3](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayexpandedbranch.xhtml?tocCode=PRC&division=20.&title=&part=&chapter=&article=&nodetreepath=43) of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976.

6. Any other finding or findings as may be required for the [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by the [California Environmental Quality Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
6. ##### Scope of Decision – Extension of Permits


1. Prior to the expiration of a Coastal Development Permit, an applicant may apply to the initial [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of the original permit for an extension of the permit for a period of one year. This request shall automatically extend the expiration date of the permit until the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) has acted upon the request and the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)'s action becomes effective. However, if construction has not commenced at the time the application for extension is made, construction may not commence during the period of the automatic extension until the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) has acted upon the request and it becomes effective. The application shall state the reasons for the request and shall be accompanied by evidence of a valid, unexpired permit and of the applicant's continued legal ownership interest in the property. The applicant shall also furnish to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) the information required in Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section.

2. The [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), in considering the request for extension, shall determine whether there are changed circumstances that may affect the consistency of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) with the findings required under Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section.

3. If the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) determines that there are no changed circumstances that may affect the consistency of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) with the findings required under Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section, notice of the determination, including a summary of the procedures set forth in this Subsection, shall be posted on the subject property by the applicant and shall be mailed, by first class mail by the appropriate [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) agency, to all [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s who testified at any public hearing on the original permit and left their names and addresses, or submitted written testimony or to any other [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s requesting notice.

4. If no written objection to the determination is received within 10 working days of the posting and mailing, the extension shall be approved.

5. If the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) determines that, due to changed circumstances, the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is no longer consistent with the findings required in Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section, or if objection is made to the determination of consistency, the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall set the matter for public hearing and give notice in accordance with the provisions of Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section. In addition, the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall notify any persons who objected to the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)'s determination of consistency.

6. The [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall make a determination based on the facts presented at the public hearing. If the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is determined to be consistent with the findings required in Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section, the extension shall be approved. If the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is determined to be inconsistent with these requirements, the extension shall be denied.

7. Notice of any action taken by the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on an application for an extension of a permit shall be provided as set forth in Subsection D.3 (Decision; Notification of Determination) of this Section.

8. Any action taken by the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on an application for an extension of a permit is appealable to the first [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) appellate body referenced in Subsection G. (Appeals) of this Section in the same manner as an appeal of the original permit as set forth in Subsection G. (Appeals) of this Section.

9. The notification procedures and the procedures applicable to appeals to the Coastal Commission set forth in Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section are applicable to applications for extensions of permits.
7. ##### Appeals


1. ###### Appellate Procedures


      Appeals from the approval, conditional approval, or disapproval of a permit under the provisions of this Section, may be taken by the applicant or any [aggrieved person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) as follows:

      1. Where a Coastal Development Permit hearing has been combined with the hearing on the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) itself, an appeal may be taken to the appellate body that would hear and decide the appeal from the underlying [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). If the appeal from any underlying [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is further appealable to a second appellate body, the Coastal Development Permit is likewise further appealable. The appellate body may be the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), or [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) depending on the underlying [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). The time within which to appeal shall be the same as that provided for an appeal of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) itself, but the decision of the permit granting authority on the coastal permit may be separately appealed, without appealing the action on the underlying [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). The times for notification of hearing and action on such appeal shall be the same as for the underlying [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), whether or not such underlying [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is also appealed.

      2. Where a Coastal Development Permit application is for a [public project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), the action of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) may be appealed to the Board of Public Works. Such appeal shall be filed with the Office of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within 15 calendar days (including at least 10 working days} of the mailing of the decision of the permit granting authority.

      3. Where a Coastal Development Permit (other than for a [public project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)) involves an underlying activity, which is not otherwise appealable, the action of a permit-granting authority on an application may be appealed to the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). That appeal shall be filed with the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within 15 calendar days (including at least 10 working days) of the mailing of the decision of the permit-granting authority.

      4. Any appeal filed with either the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall be heard and decided within 30 calendar days of the filing of the appeal. Notice shall be mailed to the required parties at least 10 calendar days prior to the hearing.

      5. Action on any appeal shall be in writing. If the action of any appeal body is further appealable within the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)'s appeal structure, notice of such intermediate appeal body's action approving, conditionally approving or disapproving any appeal of a Coastal Development Permit along with the findings and conditions imposed in connection therewith, as set forth in Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section, shall be mailed to the applicant, the appellant, and to any [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or persons who, in writing, request a copy of such action.

      6. No fee shall be charged for appeals of a Coastal Development Permit.
8. ##### Amendments to Permits


1. The holder of a Coastal Development Permit may apply to amend the permit by filing a written application with the initial [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) who approved the original permit. The [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall contain a description of the proposed amendment, the reason for the amendment, together with maps, plans or any other information as may be required by the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), and shall be accompanied by evidence of a valid, unexpired permit and of the applicant's continued legal ownership interest in the property. The applicant shall also furnish to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) the information required in Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section. If the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is deemed complete and accepted, the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall determine if the requested amendment constitutes an immaterial or material change to the permit.

2. For [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s representing immaterial changes, the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall prepare a written notice containing the same information required for the notice of the original [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for a Coastal Development Permit, a description of the proposed amendment and a summary of the procedures outlined in this Subsection. The notice shall be posted on the subject property by the applicant and shall also be mailed, by first class mail by the appropriate [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) agency, to all persons who testified at any public hearing on the original permit and left their names and addresses, or submitted written testimony or to any other persons who requested to be notified. If no written objection is received by the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within 10 working days of the posting and mailing, the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall approve the amendment provided the following findings are made:

      1. That the proposed amendment will not lessen or avoid the intended effect of the original permit, as approved or conditioned consistent with the findings required in Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section, unless the proposed amendment is necessitated by a change in circumstances, and the applicant has presented newly discovered material which he or she could not, with reasonable diligence, have discovered and produced before the original permit was granted;

      2. That the proposed amendment will not lessen or eliminate any conditions imposed for the purpose of protecting a coastal resource or coastal access consistent with the findings required by Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section;

      3. That all of the findings required by Subsection E. (Standards for Review and Required Findings) of this Section can still be made;

      4. That the proposed amendment will not result in any increase in the density or intensity of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#); and

      5. That the proposed amendment will not cause any adverse impact on surrounding properties.
3. For [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s representing material changes, applications whose immateriality has been challenged or applications for amendments which affect coastal resource or coastal [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) protection as required by [Sec. 30604 of the California Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30604.&lawCode=PRC), the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall set the matter for public hearing and shall give notice in accordance with the provisions of Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section. The [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall also notify all persons who objected to the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)'s determination of immateriality. If the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) can make the findings contained in Subdivision 2. above, it shall approve the application for amendment to the permit. If the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) cannot make the findings referenced above, the application for amendment shall be denied.

4. Notice of any action taken by the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on an application for an amendment to a permit shall be provided as set forth in Subsection D.3 (Decision; Notice of Determination) of this Section.

5. Any action taken by the [approving authority](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on an application for an amendment to a permit is appealable in the same manner as an appeal on the original permit as set forth in the Subsection G. (Appeals) of this Section.

6. The notification procedures and the procedures applicable to appeals to the Coastal Commission set forth in Subsection D.4 (Decision; Transmittal) of this Section are applicable to [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s for amendments to permits.
9. ##### Enforcement


1. ###### Violations


      Any violation of the provisions of this Section and Code relating to the processing of permits shall be subject to enforcement and penalties of [Chapter 9](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayexpandedbranch.xhtml?tocCode=PRC&division=20.&title=&part=&chapter=&article=&nodetreepath=43) of the [California Coastal Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of 1976 and subsequent amendments thereto.

2. ###### Revocation


      Any permit [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) filed or approved under the provisions of this Section or Code may be immediately terminated or revoked by the permit granting authority upon a finding that one or more of the following grounds exist:

      1. That inaccurate, erroneous or incomplete information was filed or presented in conjunction with said permit [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

      2. That names and addresses of all property owners as shown on the records of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or of the County Assessor, were not provided within the required radius of the involved property in conformity with the requirements of this Section and Code.

      3. That the addresses of all residential occupancies within 300 feet of each boundary of the site of the proposed [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) were not provided.

      4. That the applicant failed to post and maintain the required notice at the [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) in accordance with Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section.

#### Sec. 13B.9.2. Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification)

1. ##### Applicability


1. ###### Requirement of a Coastal Development Permit


      A Coastal Development Permit issued by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) in conformance with the provisions of this Section is required for all [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) located within an area of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) covered by a certified [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), unless:

      1. The [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is exempted under Paragraph 4. (Exemptions) below; or

      2. The proposed [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) site lies completely within the Coastal Commission Permit jurisdiction; or

      3. The Coastal Commission previously issued a Coastal Development Permit for the [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
2. ###### Amendments


      Amendments to these procedures are not effective until certified by the Coastal Commission.

3. ###### Definitions


      The following definitions apply to the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) within areas subject to certified [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s. Words and phrases not defined here shall be construed as defined in [Sec. 12.03. (Definitions) of Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lapz/0-0-0-886) of this Code or the California Coastal Commission Regulations, if defined there.

      Appealable Area: The area identified in [Sec. 30603 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30603.&lawCode=PRC). The area that meets this criteria includes, but is not limited to, the area shown on the “Post- [LCP](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) Certification Permit and Appeals Jurisdiction Map” certified by the Coastal Commission in accordance with the provisions of [Sec. 13576 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I840BD4A55B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3?viewType=FullText&originationContext=documenttoc&transitionType=CategoryPageItem&contextData=(sc.Default)) and attached as an exhibit in each certified coastal [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

      Appealable Development: In accordance with [Sec. 30603(a) of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30603.&lawCode=PRC), any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that constitutes a major public works project or a major energy facility, or any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) located in the [Appealable Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

      Applicant: The person, partnership, corporation, or other entity or state or local government agency applying for the Coastal Development Permit.

      Approving Authority: The initial [decision maker](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and appeal body, including the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [Zoning Administrator](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), Board of Public Works, [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or other applicable decision-making person or body within the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), which has the authority to approve a Coastal Development Permit pursuant to this Section or by reason of jurisdiction over other permits and approvals sought in conjunction with an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for a Coastal Development Permit.

      Categorically Excluded Development: A [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), which is excluded from the Coastal Development Permit requirements pursuant to a categorical exclusion order adopted by the Coastal Commission that sets forth the specific categories of [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that qualify for the exclusion within a specific geographic area, and which establishes that those categories of [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) in the specified geographic areas will have no potential for significant adverse effects, either individually or cumulatively on coastal resources or on public access to or along the coastline.

      Coastal Bluff: The upper termination of a bluff, cliff, or seacliff. In cases where the top edge of the cliff is rounded away from the face of the cliff as a result of erosional processes related to the presence of the steep cliff face, the bluff line or edge shall be defined as that point nearest the cliff beyond which the downward gradient of the surface increases more or less continuously until it reaches the general gradient of the cliff. In a case where there is a steplike feature at the top of the cliff face, the landward edge of the topmost riser shall be taken to be the cliff edge. The termini of the bluff line, or edge along the seaward face of the bluff, shall be defined as a point reached by bisecting the angle formed by a line coinciding with the general trend of the bluff line along the inland facing portion of the bluff. The minimum length of bluff line or edge used in making these determinations is 500 feet.

      Coastal Development: Any of the following on land, in or under water: the placement or erection of any solid material or structure; the discharge or disposal of any dredged material or of any gaseous, liquid, solid or thermal waste; the grading, removing, dredging, mining or extraction of any materials; any change in the density or intensity of use of land, including, but not limited to, [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s pursuant to the [Subdivision Map Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) (commencing with [California Government Code Sec. 66410](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66410.&lawCode=GOV)), and any other division of land, including lot splits, except where the land division is brought about in connection with the purchase of the land by a public agency for public recreational use; any change in the intensity of use of water or of access to the water; construction, [reconstruction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), demolition or alteration of the size of any structure, including any facility of any private, public or municipal utility; and the removal or harvesting of major vegetation other than for agricultural purposes, kelp harvesting, and timber operations, which are in accordance with a timber harvesting plan submitted pursuant to the provisions of the Z’berg-Nejedly forest Practice Act of 1973 (commencing with [Sec. 4511 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=4511.&lawCode=PRC)).

      Coastal Zone: That land and water area specified on the maps cited in [Sec. 30103 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30103.&lawCode=PRC), extending seaward to the State’s outer limit of jurisdiction, including all offshore islands, but with some additional criteria for special areas as specified in [Sec. 30103.5](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30103.5.&nodeTreePath=43.2&lawCode=PRC) and [30166 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30166.&lawCode=PRC).

      Disaster: Fire, flood, wind, earthquake, or other natural or man-made disaster.

      Emergency: A sudden, unexpected occurrence demanding immediate action to prevent or mitigate loss or damage to life, health, property or essential public services.

      Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area: Any officially mapped area in which plant or animal life or their habitats are either rare or especially valuable because of their special nature or role in an ecosystem and which could easily be disturbed or degraded by human activities and developments, and any area identified as a [wetland](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), an environmentally sensitive habitat or as a Sensitive Coastal Resource Area, in a certified [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), a certified land use plan or a certified [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

      First Public Road Paralleling the Sea: That road nearest to the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), as defined in [Sec. 30115 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30115.&lawCode=PRC), which: (a) is lawfully open to uninterrupted public use and is suitable for that use; (b) is publicly maintained; (c) is an improved, all-weather road open to motor vehicle traffic in at least one direction; (d) is not subject to any restrictions on use by the public except when closed due to an [emergency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or when closed temporarily for military purposes; and (e) does, in fact, connect with other public roads, providing a continuous access system, and generally parallels and follows the shoreline of the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) to include all portions of the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) where the physical features, such as bays, lagoons, estuaries and [wetland](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s cause the waters of the [sea](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) to extend landward from the generally continuous coastline.

      Public Project: Any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) initiated by the Department of Public Works or any of its bureaus, any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) initiated by any other department or agency of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), and any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) initiated or to be carried out by any other governmental agency that is required to obtain a local government permit. Public Project shall not include any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by any department or agency of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or any other governmental entity that otherwise requires action by or approval of the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), or the office of Zoning Administration, or any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by any department or agency of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or any other government entity for which a permit from the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is required. Public Project shall also not include any [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on tidelands, submerged lands, or on public trust lands, whether filled or unfilled.

      Wetland: Lands within the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), which may be covered periodically or permanently with shallow, water and include saltwater marshes, freshwater marshes, open or closed brackish water marshes, swamps, mudflats and fens.

4. ###### Exemptions


      The following types of [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) are exempt from the requirement to obtain a Coastal Development Permit in accordance with the provisions of this Section:

      1. ###### Improvements to Existing Structures


         1. Improvements to any existing [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) are exempt. For purposes of this Section, in order to qualify as an improvement, the [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall retain 50 percent or more of the existing exterior walls of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). In addition, the following shall be considered a part of an existing [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#):

            1. All fixtures and other [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s directly attached to the existing [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#); and

            2. For single-family residences, in addition to Sub-subparagraph a. above, structures on the property normally associated with a single-family residence, such as garages, swimming pools, [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s and storage sheds, but not including guest houses or self-contained [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, shall also be considered part of that [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
         2. Despite the exemption provided in Subparagraph i. above, the following improvements require a Coastal Development Permit:

            01. Improvements to any structure on a beach, [Wetland](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), stream or lake, seaward of the mean high tide line, where the structure or proposed improvement would encroach within 50 feet of the edge of a [Coastal Bluff](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), stream or in areas of natural vegetation designated by resolution of the Coastal Commission as a significant natural habitat, or identified in a certified local coastal plan or [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) as a significant natural habitat; or within 100 feet of the edge of a [Coastal Bluff](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) if the structure is a single family dwelling;

            02. Any significant alteration of land forms, including the removal or placement of vegetation, on a beach, [Wetland](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or sand dune, or within 100 feet of the edge of a [Coastal Bluff](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or stream or in areas of natural vegetation designated by resolution of the Coastal Commission or in a certified [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) as a significant natural habitat; or within 50 feet of the edge of a [Coastal Bluff](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) if the [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is a single family [dwelling](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#);

            03. The expansion or construction of water wells or septic systems;

            04. Improvements to any structure on property located in the [Appealable Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that would result in:

                1. An increase of 10 percent or more of internal floor area of the existing structure; or

                2. An additional improvement of 10 percent or less where an improvement to the structure has previously been undertaken pursuant to [Public Resources Code Sec. 30610(b)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30610.&lawCode=PRC); and/or

                3. An increase in height by more than 10 percent of an existing structure.
            05. Improvements to any structure on property in the non-appealable area that would result in an increase of 10 percent or more of internal floor area of the existing structure;

            06. Improvements to any structure in significant scenic resource areas as designated by the Coastal Commission or in a certified [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that would result in:

                1. An increase of 10 percent or more of internal floor area of the existing structure; or

                2. An additional improvement of 10 percent or less where an improvement to the structure has previously been undertaken pursuant to [Public Resources Code Sec. 30610(b)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30610.&lawCode=PRC); and/or

                3. An increase in height by more than 10 percent of an existing structure.
            07. In areas the Coastal Commission has previously declared, by resolution after public hearing, to have a critically short water supply that must be maintained for the protection of coastal resources or public recreational use, the construction of any specific major water-using [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) including, but not limited to, swimming pools, or the construction or extension of any [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) irrigation system;

            08. Any improvement to a structure where the development permit issued for the original structure by the Coastal Commission indicated that any future improvements would require a Coastal Development Permit;

            09. Any improvement to a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that results in a Change in the intensity of Use of the [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#); and

            10. Any improvement made pursuant to a conversion of an existing [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) from a multiple unit rental [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or visitor-serving commercial [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) to a use involving a fee ownership or long-term leasehold, including, but not limited to, a [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) conversion, [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) conversion or hotel/motel timesharing conversion.
      2. ###### Repair and Maintenance Activities of Public Utilities


         Repair and maintenance activities of public utilities as specified in the repair, maintenance and utility hook-up exclusion adopted by the Coastal Commission on September 5, 1978.

      3. ###### Other Repair and Maintenance


         Repair and maintenance activities that do not result in a material addition to or an enlargement or expansion of the object of those activities, except as otherwise specified by the Coastal Commission in [Sec. 13252 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I80F67E595B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3?viewType=FullText&originationContext=documenttoc&transitionType=CategoryPageItem&contextData=(sc.Default)), and any amendments subsequently adopted, except if the repairs or maintenance involve any of the following:

         1. Any method of repair or maintenance of a seawall revetment, bluff retaining wall, breakwater, groin, culvert, outfall or similar shoreline work that involves:

            1. Repair or maintenance involving substantial alteration of the foundation of the protective work including pilings and other surface or subsurface structures;

            2. The placement, whether temporary or permanent, of rip-rap, artificial berms of sand or other beach materials, or any other forms of solid materials, on a beach or in coastal waters, streams, [Wetland](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, estuaries and lakes or on a shoreline protective work except for agricultural dikes within enclosed bays or estuaries;

            3. The replacement of 20 percent or more of the materials in an existing structure with materials of a different kind; or

            4. The presence, whether temporary or permanent, of mechanized construction equipment or construction materials on any sand area or bluff or within 20 feet of coastal waters or streams.
         2. Any method of maintenance dredging that involves:

            1. The dredging of 100,000 cubic yards or more within a 12 month period;

            2. The placement of dredge spoils of any quantity within an [Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), on any sand area, within 50 feet of the edge of a [Coastal Bluff](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or within 20 feet of coastal waters or streams; or

            3. The removal, sale or disposal of dredge spoils of any quantity that would be suitable for beach nourishment in an area that the Coastal Commission has declared by resolution, or has been identified in a certified [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), to have a critically short sand supply that must be maintained for protection of structures, coastal [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or public recreational use.
         3. Any repair or maintenance to facilities or structures or work located in an [Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), any sand area, within 50 feet of the edge of a [Coastal Bluff](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or within 20 feet of coastal waters or streams that includes:

            1. The placement or removal, whether temporary or permanent, of rip-rap, rocks, sand or other beach materials or any other forms of solid materials; or

            2. The presence, whether temporary or permanent, of mechanized equipment or construction materials.
         4. Unless [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by [Disaster](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), the replacement of 50 percent or more of a seawall, revetment, bluff retaining wall, breakwater, groin or similar protective work under one ownership is not repair and maintenance under [Sec. 30610(d) of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30610.&lawCode=PRC), but instead constitutes a replacement structure requiring a Coastal Development Permit.
      4. ###### Replacement Structures


         The replacement of any structure [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) by a [Disaster](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) if the replacement structure conforms to applicable existing zoning requirements, is for the same use as the [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) structure, does not exceed either the floor area, height, or bulk of the [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) structure by more than 10 percent and is sited in the same location on the affected property as the [destroyed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) structure.

         1. As used in this Subdivision, “bulk” means total interior cubic volume as measured from the exterior surface of the structure.

         2. As used in this Subdivision, “structure” includes [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and any erosion control structure or device, which is similar to that which existed prior to the occurrence of the [Disaster](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
      5. ###### Categorically Excluded Development


         Any [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) that has been categorically excluded pursuant to a categorical exclusion approved by the Coastal Commission.

      6. ###### Geologic Testing


         Geologic testing that does not require other [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) permits, does not involve cutting access roads and does not remove significant vegetation.

      7. ###### Temporary Events


         1. A temporary event that meets all of the following criteria:

            1. Does not involve a charge for general public admission or seating; and

            2. Will not restrict public [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or use of [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, or recreational areas; and

            3. Will not either directly or indirectly impact [Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s, rare or endangered species, significant scenic resources, or other coastal resources, such as water-oriented activities, visitor facilities, marine resources, biological resources, agricultural lands, and archaeological or paleontological resources.
         2. Any temporary event which has previously received a Coastal Development Permit, will be in the same location, during the same time period, will be operated in the same manner, and was not the subject of previous complaints.
2. ##### Initiation


1. ###### General


      An [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for a Coastal Development Permit shall be filed with either the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) on a form provided by the [Department](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and include all information required by the instructions on the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and any applicable adopted guidelines.

      1. Within 30 days of the submittal of the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and the payment of fees, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), whichever has jurisdiction, shall determine whether the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is complete.

      2. Prior to deeming an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) complete, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall determine, and if necessary, advise the Applicant, of the processes to be followed, any additional information required, and the fees to be paid. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall adopt guidelines and use them to determine when an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is deemed complete.
2. ###### Jurisdiction


      1. An [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for a Coastal Development Permit for a [public project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), or for a private [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) where the approval of the underlying permit is within the jurisdiction of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), shall be filed in the office of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).

      2. All other [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) s for Coastal Development Permits shall be filed in a public office of the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#).
3. ###### Preliminary Notice of Jurisdiction


      1. At the time an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) for [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is submitted, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), whichever has jurisdiction, shall determine whether:

         1. The [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is within the Coastal Commission’s jurisdiction or the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#)’s jurisdiction; and

         2. The [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is located within the appealable or non-appealable jurisdiction of the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#); and

         3. The [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is within an area designated by a certified [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or within the area subject to the provisions of [Sec. 12.20.1 (SL Ocean - Submerged Land Zone) of Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lapz/0-0-0-4504) of this Code; and

         4. The [development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is exempt or categorically excluded according to the criteria of Subsection A.4. (Applicability; Exemptions) of this Section.
      2. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall use the following criteria: the certified [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), including any maps, the Post [LCP](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) Certification Permit and Appeals Jurisdiction Map certified by the California Coastal Commission, land use designations, special programs and zoning ordinances that are certified as part of the [Local Coastal Program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) and categorical exclusion orders granted by the Coastal Commission.

      3. If the preliminary notice of jurisdiction of the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is challenged by the Applicant or an interested person within 15 days after the determination is made, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) may request an opinion of the Coastal Commission Executive [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#). The decision of the Executive [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or the Coastal Commission pursuant to [Sec. 13569 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I83ECB3ED5B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3?viewType=FullText&originationContext=documenttoc&transitionType=CategoryPageItem&contextData=(sc.Default)) shall apply.
4. ###### Notice of Exemption


      1. After jurisdiction has been established and the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) has determined that the [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) is exempt pursuant to Subsection C. (Notice) of this Section, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#), whichever has jurisdiction, shall issue a notice of exemption for a [Coastal Development](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) which is exempt from the Coastal Development Permit requirements. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) or [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#) shall mail a copy of the notice of exemption to the Applicant and the Coastal Commission.

      2.
