Certificate of Appropriateness: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), certificate of appropriateness is defined as an approved certificate issued for the construction, additions over established thresholds outlined in [Sec. 13B.8.4. (Review of Conforming Work)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8.4), [demolition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), reconstruction, [alteration](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), removal, or relocation of any publicly or privately owned [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within a [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is identified as a [contributing element](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the zone, including street features, furniture or fixtures.

Certificate of Compatibility: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), certificate of compatibility is defined as an approved certificate issued for the construction of a new [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [demolition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) replacement of an element, identified as noncontributing, or not listed, in the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the zone.

Certificate of Occupancy: Certificate of Occupancy is defined as a certificate issued by the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in accordance with [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Sec. 91.109. (Certificate of Occupancy)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-173160) of this Code authorizing the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land, a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or portion thereof, or a trailer park or portion thereof. See [Sec. 1.4.2.C. (Certificate of Occupancy)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.4.2).

Chamfered Corner: Chamfered corner is defined as an [architectural element](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at a corner of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to a street intersection where a tertiary [building face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) transitions between two otherwise intersecting primary [building face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s at an angle between 30 and 60 degrees measured from both primary [building face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. For an illustrative example, see [Sec. 3C.1.3.C.2. (Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.1.3).

Change of Use: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.6.a. (Change of Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), change of use is defined as work that includes a change or expansion in the permitted [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of any portion of an [existing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from one [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) defined in [Part 5D. (Use Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D) to any other [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) defined in [Part 5D. (Use Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D). Change of use does not include any [temporary use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. For [temporary use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, see [Sec. 14.2.15.B.7. (Temporary Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15).

Character Frontage: Character frontage is defined as a Frontage District established in [Div. 3B.9. (Character Frontage District)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.9).

Citation: For the purposes of [Sec. 5C.3.2. (Home-Sharing Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), citation is defined as any enforcement citation, order, ticket or similar notice of violation, relating to the condition of or activities at a [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)’s [primary residence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or property, issued by the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), Los Angeles Housing Department, Los Angeles Police Department, or Los Angeles Fire Department, including an Administrative Citation issued pursuant to [Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning), Article 1.2. (Administrative Citations)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-225704) of this Code.

City: City is defined as the City of Los Angeles, California.

City Council: City Council is established by [City Charter, Sec. 200 (City Officers)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-2). See also [Sec. 13A.1.2. (City Council)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.1.2).

City Engineer: City Engineer is defined pursuant to [Article 6. (City Engineer)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-50391) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

City Hall Height Restriction: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.4. (City Hall Height Restriction)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.4), City Hall height restriction is defined as a restriction to the vertical dimension of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) based on proximity and height relative to Los Angeles City Hall.

City Planning Commission: City Planning Commission is defined pursuant to [City Charter, Sec. 551. (City Planning Commission)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-2427).

Civic Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.2. (Civic Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.2), civic facility is defined as any [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) facility that provides governmental or cultural services to the general public and is operated by or in partnership with a governmental institution. A civic facility includes a post office, civic center, community center, public museum, courthouse, government office, or library.

Civic Facility: Local: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.2.A. (Civic Facility: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.2), civic facility: local is defined as a [civic facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that occupies no more than 50,000 square feet of total [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include similar [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that occupy more than 50,000 square feet of total [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.2.B. (Civic Facility: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.2).

Civic Facility: Regional: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.2.B. (Civic Facility: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.2), civic facility: regional is defined as a [civic facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that occupies more than 50,000 square feet of total [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include similar [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that occupy 50,000 square feet or less of total [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.2.A. (Civic Facility: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.2).

Civic Fleet Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.3. (Civic Fleet Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.3), civic fleet services include maintenance, storage, and management of government or publicly operated [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, such as school buses, municipal transit vehicles, emergency response vehicles, public utility vehicles, or waste hauling vehicles, in service of any [civic facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Where [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, such as dispatch, do not include [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) maintenance or storage, they are allowed pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.2. (Civic Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.2).

Clear Depth: Clear depth is defined as the horizontal dimension of the [occupiable](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at the narrowest point.

Clear Height: Clear height is defined as the vertical dimension of the [occupiable](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at the shortest point.

Clear Width: Clear width is defined as the horizontal dimension of the [occupiable](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at the narrowest point (unless otherwise noted).

Coastal Bluff: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2), coastal bluff is defined as the upper termination of a bluff, cliff, or seacliff. In cases where the top edge of the cliff is rounded away from the face of the cliff as a result of erosional processes related to the presence of the steep cliff face, the bluff line or edge shall be defined as that point nearest the cliff beyond which the downward gradient of the surface increases more or less continuously until it reaches the general gradient of the cliff. In a case where there is a steplike feature at the top of the cliff face, the landward edge of the topmost riser shall be taken to be the cliff edge. The termini of the bluff line, or edge along the seaward face of the bluff, shall be defined as a point reached by bisecting the angle formed by a line coinciding with the general trend of the bluff line along the inland facing portion of the bluff. The minimum length of bluff line or edge used in making these determinations is 500 feet.

Coastal Development: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2), coastal development is defined as any of the following on land, in or under water: the placement or erection of any solid material or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); the discharge or disposal of any dredged material or of any gaseous, liquid, solid or thermal waste; the [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), removing, dredging, mining or extraction of any materials; any change in the density or intensity of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land, including, but not limited to, subdivisions pursuant to the [Subdivision Map Act (commencing with California Government Code, Sec. 66410)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&division=2.&title=7.&part=&chapter=1.&article=1.), and any other division of land, including [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) splits, except where the land division is brought about in connection with the purchase of the land by a public agency for public recreational use; any change in the intensity of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of water or of [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to the water; construction, reconstruction, [demolition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or alteration of the size of any [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including any facility of any private, public or municipal utility; and the removal or harvesting of major vegetation other than for agricultural purposes, kelp harvesting, and timber operations, which are in accordance with a timber harvesting plan submitted pursuant to the provisions of the [Z’bergNejedly Forest Practice Act of 1973 (commencing with Sec. 4511 of the Public Resources Code)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=4511.&lawCode=PRC).

Coastal Zone: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2), coastal zone is defined as that land and water area specified on the maps cited in [Sec. 30103 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=30103.&lawCode=PRC), extending seaward to the State’s outer limit of jurisdiction, including all offshore islands, but with some additional criteria for special areas as specified in [Sec. 30103.5 and 30166 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayexpandedbranch.xhtml?lawCode=PRC&division=20.&title=&part=&chapter=2.5.&article=&goUp=Y).

Collection Bin: Collection bin is defined as any box, canister, receptacle, or other container that can be opened and closed, and is used for collecting salvageable personal property, including, but not limited to, clothing, shoes, books, and household items for periodic off-site processing and/or redistribution. For purposes of this definition, salvageable personal property shall not include recyclable materials not intended for re-use, including, but not limited to, newspapers, plastic, glass, aluminum, electronics, toxic or hazardous materials, and solid waste; nor any personal property that, because of its size, does not fit inside the collection bin. See [Sec. 13B.10.3.A.2. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.10.3).

Collector Street: Collector street is defined as any [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated as a collector street on the Citywide General Plan Circulation System maps of the [Circulation Element](https://planning.lacity.gov/odocument/523f2a95-9d72-41d7-aba5-1972f84c1d36/Mobility_Plan_2035.pdf) of the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Commercial Message: For the purposes of [Sec. 4C.11.1.E.3. (Original Art Murals, Vintage Original Art Murals & Public Art Installations)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.1), commercial message means any message that advertises a business conducted, services rendered, or goods produced or sold.

Commercial Vehicle: Commercial vehicle is defined as any vehicle, excluding household moving rental trucks and utility rental trailers, which when operated upon a highway is required to be registered as a commercial vehicle by the Vehicle Code of the State of California, or by any other jurisdiction, and that is used or maintained for the transportation of persons for hire, compensation, or profit, or designed, used, or maintained primarily for the transportation of property.

Commercial/Industrial Conversion Project: For the purposes of [Div. 11.5. (Condominiums, Community Apartments, & Stock Cooperatives)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.5) commercial/industrial conversion project is defined as an [existing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for commercial or industrial purposes, or both, proposed for conversion to a [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to be [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for commercial or industrial purposes, or both through approval of a [tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For purposes of this definition, the term existing means that the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was constructed prior to 1945, or if it was built after 1945, a [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was issued for the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) prior to the time of map [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Commercial/Industrial to Residential Conversion Project: For the purposes of [Div. 11.5. (Condominiums, Community Apartments, & Stock Cooperatives)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.5) commercial/industrial to residential conversion project is defined as an [existing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for commercial or industrial purposes, or both, proposed for conversion to a [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or community apartment to be [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) purposes through approval of a [tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For purposes of this definition, the term existing means that the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was constructed prior to 1945 or, if it was built after 1945, a [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was issued for the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) prior to the time of map [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Commissary Kitchen: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.2. (Commissary Kitchen)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.2), a commissary kitchen is defined as a kitchen facility used for cooking and preparing food to be primarily served and consumed off-site. This definition includes multi-tenant shared kitchen facilities, order fulfillment kitchens, and catering kitchen facilities. The following [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are allowed when incidential to the kitchen facility: research and teaching facilities, commercial food processing, and order fulfillment pick-up lobbies.

Common Indoor Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.5. (Common Indoor Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3), common indoor amenity space is defined as a type of amenity space that is [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), is legally required to be open to all tenants of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), is intended to create opportunities for social and recreational activity for tenants, and meets all of the standards in [Sec. 2C3.3.C.5. (Common Indoor Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C3.3).

Common Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.B.3. (Common Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), common lot line is defined as any [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shared by multiple [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Common lot lines include all [side lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [rear lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and may include [special lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s in [Dual Frontage Districts (Div. 3B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.8).

Common Outdoor Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.1. (Common Outdoor Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3), common outdoor amenity space is defined as a type of amenity space that is outdoors, open to all tenants of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and meets the standards of [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.1. (Common Outdoor Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3).

Community Apartment Project: Community apartment project is defined pursuant to [California Business and Professions Code, Sec. 11004](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=BPC&division=4.&title=&part=2.&chapter=1.&article=1.).

Community Assembly: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.8. (Community Assembly)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8), community assembly is defined as any non-residential and not-for-profit facility that is oriented around an assembly space used primarily for the temporary gathering of people for a shared social purpose. Access to the general public may be limited based on association. Community assembly includes any place of worship, community meeting room, private club, event space, assembly hall, social club, or union hall.

Community Assembly: Local: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.8.A. (Community Assembly: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8), community assembly: local is defined as any [community assembly](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes an assembly space 2,000 square feet or less. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include similar [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that occupy more than 2,000 square feet of total assembly space [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.8.B. (Community Assembly: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8).

Community Assembly: Regional: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.8.B. (Community Assembly: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8), community assembly: regional is defined as any [community assembly](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes an assembly space larger than 2,000 square feet. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include similar [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that occupy 2,000 square feet or less of total assembly space [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.8.A. (Community Assembly: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8).

Community Care Facilities: See [community care facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Community Care Facility: Community care facility is defined as any place licensed by the State of California that is maintained and operated as a residential facility or as a social rehabilitation facility to provide non-medical residential care, day treatment, adult day care, or foster family agency services for persons in need of services, supervision, or assistance essential for sustaining the activities of daily living, as deﬁned in the [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 1502 (a). (Definitions)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1502.). The term includes halfway house, non-medical assisted living, and substance abuse treatment operation. For residential community care facility see [Sec. 5D.2.4.A. (Supportive Housing: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.4). For non-residential community care facility see [Sec. 5D.3.10. (Social Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.10).

Community Plan Implementation Overlay: Community Plan Implementation Overlay is defined as a zoning overlay adopted for a community plan area, which provides supplemental development regulations by defined subareas, which may include, public benefits incentives programs available, amount of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) awarded for public benefits incentives programs, applicable local affordable housing incentive program sets, and development standards. See [Sec. 8.2.2. (Community Plan Implementation Overlay)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.2).

Community Redevelopment Agency: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, Community Redevelopment Agency is defined as the former Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of Los Angeles, which was dissolved on February 1, 2012.

Community Redevelopment Law: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, community redevelopment law is defined as the Community Redevelopment Law of the State of California (California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 33000 et seq.).

Community Redevelopment Agency - Designated Local Authority: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, Community Redevelopment Agency - Designated Local Authority is defined as the public body formed pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 34173(c)(3) to serve as the successor agency to the former [CRA](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Condominium: Condominium is defined pursuant to [California Civil Code, Chapter 1, Sec. 783](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=783#:~:text=A%20condominium%20is%20an%20estate,in%20Section%204125%20or%206542.).

Contributing Element: For the purposes of [Div. 13.B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13), contributing element is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) identified on the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as contributing to the Historic significance of the [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which has been altered, where the nature and extent of the [alteration](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are determined reversible by the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Controlled Drilling Site: Controlled drilling site is defined as that particular location within an oil drilling district in an [urbanized area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) upon which surface operations for the drilling, deepening, or operation of a hole or well associated with an [oil, gas, or hydrocarbon well](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or any incidental operation are permitted subject to the conditions prescribed by written determination by the [Zoning Administrator](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Conversion Project: For the purposes of [Article 11. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11), a conversion project is an [existing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) proposed for conversion to a [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or community apartment through approval of a [tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For purposes of this definition, the term existing means that the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was constructed prior to 1945 or, where built after 1945, a [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was issued for the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) prior to the time of map [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Conversion project includes [residential conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [residential to commercial/industrial conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and [commercial/industrial to residential conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Corner Lot: Corner lot is defined as a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) situated at the intersection of two or more streets having an angle of intersection of not more than 135 degrees.

Covered: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.2.A.1. (Covered)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.2), covered is defined as a space or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with less than 25 percent of its area [open to the sky](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Covered Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.2. (Covered Area (%))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.2), covered area is defined as the measurement of how open an [occupiable space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is to the sky.

Cultural: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), cultural is defined as anything pertaining to the concepts, skills, habits, arts, instruments or institutions of a given people at any given point in time.

Cultural Heritage Commission: Cultural Heritage Commission is defined pursuant to [Article 1. (Cultural Heritage Commission)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-48548) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

### D

Day Laborer: Day laborer is defined as any person who offers themselves to be hired as a laborer for a day, or some other temporary basis.

Decision Maker: Decision maker is defined as the agency or official charged with rendering a formal decision on an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) subject to [Article 13. (Administration)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13). For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.11.1. (Environmental Review Procedures)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.11.1), see [Sec. 13B.11.1.D.2. (Decision Maker)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.11.1).

Dedication of Land: Dedication of land is defined as a conveyance of land in fee simple or as an [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by its owner for public uses, reserving to themselves no other rights than such as are compatible with the full exercise and enjoyment of the public uses to which the property has been devoted.

Demolition: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.8. (Demolition)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), demolition is defined as the removal of an entire [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For the purposes of [Sec. 4C.15.1. (Housing Projects that Result in the Demolition of Dwelling Units)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.15.1) and [Sec. 4C.15.2. (Non-Housing Projects that Result in the Demolition of Dwelling Units)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.15.2), this definition shall not apply. For the purposes of [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), demolition is defined as the removal of more than 50 percent of the perimeter wall framing, the removal of more than 50 percent of the roof framing, or the substantial removal of the exterior of a [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the Street-Visible Area.

Density Bonus: Density bonus is defined as a density increase over the otherwise [maximum allowable residential density](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) under the applicable zoning code, and zoning designation, or [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), granted pursuant to an applicable incentive program established in [Article 9. (Public Benefit Systems)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9).

Department: Department is defined as the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), unless otherwise indicated. See [City Charter, Sec. 550. (Powers and Duties of the Department)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-2422).

Department of Building and Safety: The Department of Building and Safety is defined pursuant to [Sec. 22.20. (The Department)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-47413) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Department of City Planning: Department of City Planning is defined pursuant to [City Charter, Sec. 550. (Powers and Duties of the Department)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-2422).

Designated Historic Resource: Designated historic resource is defined as a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), object, [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) element, or natural feature listed or designated as an individual resource or as a contributor to a historic district, at the local, state, or national level, including but not limited to listing in the National Register of Historic Places or California Register of Historical Resources, or designation as a Historic-Cultural Monument or as an [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) ( [HPOZ](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)).

Destroyed: Destroyed is defined as damaged so as to not be habitable, or having lost 75 percent of replacement value, as determined by the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Detention Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.4. (Detention Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.4), detention facility is defined as any facility where persons are incarcerated, or otherwise involuntarily confined under the jurisdiction and custody of a governmental entity. Detention facilities include correctional facilities and penal institutions.

Development: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.1. (Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.1), development is defined as: on land, in or under water, the placement or erection of any solid material or structure; discharge or disposal of any dredged material or of any gaseous, liquid, solid, or thermal waste; grading, removing, dredging, mining, or extraction of any materials; change in the density or intensity of the use of land, including, but not limited to, subdivisions pursuant to the [Subdivision Map Act (commencing with Sec. 66410. of the California Government Code)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&division=2.&title=7.&part=&chapter=1.&article=1.), and any other division of land, including, but not limited to, [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) divisions, lot splits, lot reconfigurations, and mergers, except where the land division is brought about in connection with the purchase of such land by a public agency for public recreational use; change in the intensity of use of water, or of access thereto; construction, reconstruction, [demolition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or alteration of the size of any [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including any facility of any private, public, or municipal utility; and the removal or harvesting of major vegetation other than for agricultural purposes, kelp harvesting, and timber operations which are in accordance with a timber harvesting plan submitted pursuant to the provisions of the [Z'berg-Nejedly Forest Practice Act of 1973 (commencing with Sec. 4511 of the California Public Resources Code)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=4511.&lawCode=PRC). As used in this definition, "structure" includes, but is not limited to, any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), road, pipe, flume, conduit, siphon, aqueduct, telephone line, and electrical power transmission and distribution line.

Development Project: For the purposes of [Article 15. (Fees)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15), development project is defined as any activity involving or requiring the issuance of a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that results in additional housing units, additional non-residential [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), additional single-family residential [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or a [change of use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from non-residential to [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Development Standard: For the purposes of [Sec. 9.2.1. (State Density Bonus Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), [Sec. 9.2.2. (Affordable Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), [Sec. 9.2.3. (Opportunity Corridors Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), [Sec. 9.2.4. (Corridor Transitions Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), and [Sec. 9.2.5. (Transit Oriented Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.5) development standard is defined as [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or construction condition applicable to a development pursuant to any ordinance, land use plan, law, policy, resolution, regulation or other local condition that is adopted or imposed by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) through its various powers, as defined in California Government Code Sec. 65915(o)(2). This includes, but is not limited to standards like height, yards, [floor area ratio](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), open space requirements, parking space requirements, and [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) treatments.

Digital Display: Digital display is defined as a [sign face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [building face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or structural component that displays still images, scrolling images, moving images, or flashing images, including video and animation, through the use of grid lights, cathode ray projections, light emitting diode displays, plasma screens, liquid crystal displays, fiber optics, or other electronic media or technology that is either independent of, attached to, integrated into, or projected onto a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or structural component, and that may be changed remotely through electronic means.

Direct Access: Direct access is defined as the ability of a [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to move to and from a facility or space, without necessitating travel through any intermediate space.

Director: Director is defined as the Director of the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or the Director’s designee. See Sec. 13A.1.6. (Director of Planning).

Disabled Veteran: Disabled Veteran shall be as defined pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 18541.

Disaster: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2), disaster is defined as fire, flood, wind, earthquake, or other natural or man-made disaster.

Distance: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.3.A.1. (Distance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.3), distance is defined as the amount of space between two points.

District Boundary Height Transition: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.2. (District Boundary Height Transition)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.2), district boundary height transition is defined as a reduction in the maximum height of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for a limited depth where [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) districts have substantially lower height allowances.

Divided-Lite: Divided-lite is defined as separate pieces of glass glazed between muntin bars.

Domestic Use: Domestic use is defined as for use or consumption within the [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that cultivates, manufactures, or generates a good. Domestic use includes goods gifted outside of the [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) provided there is no reciprocal or monetary exchange.

Drilling & Production Site in the Los Angeles City Oil Field Area: Drilling & Production site in the Los Angeles City oil field area is defined as locations within an oil drilling district in the [Los Angeles City Oil Field Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) upon which surface operations for the drilling, deepening or operation of a hole or well associated with an [oil, gas, or hydrocarbon well](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or any operation incident thereto, are subject to the conditions prescribed by written determination by the [Zoning Administrator](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Drip Line: Drip line is defined as a line which may be drawn on the ground around a tree, directly under its outermost branch tips, and which identifies that location where rainwater tends to drip from the tree.

Drive Aisle: Drive aisle is defined as an [access lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in a [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that accommodates [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) circulation and [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to [parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Drive aisle may accommodate one-way or two-way [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) traffic, depending on the drive aisle width provided in accordance with [Sec. 4C.4.3. (Parking Area Design)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.3).

Drive-Through Facilities: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.2.2.C.3. (Drive-Through Facilities)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2), a drive-through facility is defined a facility that provides goods or services to drivers in [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Drive-through facilities include [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s consisting of [queuing space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Drive-Through Facility: See [drive-through facilities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Drive-Through Lane: A drive-through lane is defined as an automobile lane providing [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to a service [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) through which goods or services are provided directly to drivers in [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Driveway: A driveway is defined as a space along a [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is designed to accommodate [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to a [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Driveways are formed by a sloping break or cut in the curb along the roadway to allow a [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to drive over the curb and into the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Dual Frontage: Pursuant to [Div. 3B.8. (Dual Frontages)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B.8), apply frontage standards along special [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, in addition to primary and side street lot lines, on [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s where multiple [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are prioritized for a prescribed set of design and activation standards.

Dwelling: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.1. (Dwelling)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.1), a dwelling is defined as a housing accommodation serving as a primary residency or having an occupancy of greater than 30 consecutive days. A dwelling includes [household dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and group dwelling.

Dwelling Unit: A dwelling unit is defined as a habitable residential unit serving as a residence having an occupancy of greater than 30 days consecutively. Includes [household dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

For the purposes of the [State Density Bonus Program (Sec. 9.2.1.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), [Maximum Allowable Residential Density (Sec. 14.2.19.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.19), and a [one hundred percent affordable housing project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the [Affordable Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), a dwelling unit shall mean a habitable residential unit serving as a residence having an occupancy of greater than 30 days consecutively that is a complete independent living facility which includes permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, a [kitchen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and sanitation, or that is a [shared housing unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in a [shared housing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); but the term does not include [household dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

For the purposes of the [Opportunity Corridors Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), [Corridor Transitions Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.4.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), [Transit Oriented Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.5), and a [faith-based organization project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [shared equity project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [public land project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the [Affordable Housing Incentive Program (Sec. 9.2.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), a dwelling unit shall mean a habitable residential unit serving as a residence having an occupancy of greater than 30 days consecutively that is a complete independent living facility which includes permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, a [kitchen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and sanitation; but the term does not include [household dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [shared housing unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Dwelling Units Per Lot: Pursuant to [Sec. 6C.1.1. (Dwelling Units Per Lot)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/6#6C.1.1), dwelling units per lot is defined as the maximum number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s allowed on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

### E

Easement: Easement is defined as a non-possessory right given to a [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or entity to use another's property for a limited purpose, such as for [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to other properties.

Eating & Drinking: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.3. (Eating & Drinking)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3), eating & drinking is defined as the sale of prepared, ready-to-consume meals or drinks for consumption by the public.

Eating & Drinking: Alcohol Service: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.3.A. (Eating & Drinking: Alcohol Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3), eating & drinking: alcohol service is a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that involves the serving and dispensing of alcoholic beverages primarily for consumption on-site. Eating & drinking: alcohol service includes the provision of alcoholic beverages to customers in a dining setting, while gathered at a bar or tasting room, or in conjunction with another [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), such as an entertainment venue, stadium, hotel, [indoor recreation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), brewery or distillery. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the sale of alcoholic beverages for off-site consumption, without prepared food orders, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.12.B. (Retail: Alcohol)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12).

Eating & Drinking: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.3.A. (Eating & Drinking: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3), eating & drinking: general is defined as an eating & drinking [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that involves serving and sale of prepared food and drinks for on or off-site consumption. Eating & drinking: general [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s includes table service at a restaurant, counter service for off-site consumption, and self-service cafeteria dining. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the dispensing of alcoholic beverages for consumption on-site, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, see [Sec. 5D.6.3.B. (Eating & Drinking: Alcohol Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the sale of alcoholic beverages for off-site consumption, without prepared food orders, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.12.B. (Retail: Alcohol)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12).

Efficiency Dwelling Unit: Efficiency dwelling unit is defined as a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) serving as a residency having an occupancy of greater than 30 days consecutively, and that contains only one [habitable room](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), is limited to 455 square feet in [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), may include a [kitchenette](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), but may not include a full [kitchen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). The [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) may include an exterior entry or an entry from a common [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) corridor.

Electric Vehicle Charging Station: An electric vehicle charging station is defined as one or more electric vehicle charging spaces served by an electric vehicle charger or other charging equipment allowing charging of electric [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Elevation: Elevation is defined as the position or location of something along a vertical direction above or below a given vertical datum.

Elevation Projection: Elevation projection is defined as an orthographic projection of the exterior face of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), represented as a two-dimensional drawing of the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Elevation projections have an [angle of elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of zero degrees (horizontal).

Eligible Tenant: For the purposes of [Div. 11.5. (Condominiums, Community Apartments, & Stock Cooperatives)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.5), eligible tenant is defined as any tenant who was a [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the property both on the date of [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and the date of approval of such map, or at any time after that, and who does not intend to purchase a unit in the [conversion project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Emergency: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2) emergency is defined as a sudden, unexpected occurrence demanding immediate action to prevent or mitigate loss or damage to life, health, property or essential public services.

Enclosed: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.1.4.A.1. (Enclosed)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.1.4), an enclosed space is considered to be enclosed when the perimeter of the space has an enclosure of at least 66.7 percent.

Enclosure: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.1.4. (Enclosure)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.1.4), enclosure is defined as the measurement of how closed off an [occupiable space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is to its surroundings.

End Stall: An end stall is defined as the last [parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in a row, beyond which the [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not continue.

Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.4. (Entertainment Venue, Indoor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.4), entertainment venue, indoor is defined as any indoor assembly [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed or intended for entertainment, includes live music venues, performing arts theaters, movie theaters, dance clubs, comedy clubs, karaoke lounges, and banquet halls.

Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Local: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.4.A. (Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.4), entertainment venue, indoor: local is defined as any [entertainment venue, indoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed for an assembly capacity of less than 3,000 persons. For [entertainment venue, indoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s designed for an assembly capacity of 3,000 or greater, see [Sec. 5D.6.4.B. (Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.4). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include activities established in [Sec. 5D.6.13. (Sexually Oriented Business)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.13). For the inclusion of alcoholic beverages for on-site consumption, see [Sec. 5D.6.3.B. (Eating & Drinking: Alcohol Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3).

Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Regional: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.4.B. (Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.4), entertainment venue, indoor: regional is defined as any [entertainment venue, indoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed for an assembly capacity of 3,000 persons or greater. For [entertainment venue, indoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s designed for an assembly capacity of less than 3,000 persons, see [Sec. 5D.6.4.A. (Entertainment Venue, Indoor: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.4). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include activities established in [Sec. 5D.6.13. (Sexually Oriented Business)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.13). For the inclusion of alcoholic beverages for on-site consumption, see [Sec. 5D.6.3.B. (Eating & Drinking: Alcohol Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3).

Entrance Spacing: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.5.1.C.2. (Entrance Spacing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.5.1), entrance spacing is defined as the [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) between [street-facing entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s meeting the standards of [Sec. 3C.5.1.C.1. (Street-Facing Entrance General Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.5.1).

Entry Feature: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.5.2. (Entry Feature)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.5.2), entry features are defined as improved design standards applied to each entrance along the public realm.

Entry Feature Option: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.5.2.C.2. (Entry Feature Options)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.5.2), entry feature options are defined as packages of design standards applied to each entrance along the public realm.

Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Area: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2) an Environmentally Sensitive Habitat Areas (ESHA) is defined as any officially mapped area in which plant or animal life or their habitats are either rare or especially valuable because of their special nature or role in an ecosystem and which could easily be disturbed or degraded by human activities and developments, and any area identified as a wetland, an environmentally sensitive habitat or as a sensitive coastal resource area, in a certified [local coastal program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), a certified land use plan or a certified [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Equine: Equine is defined as any horse, pony, donkey, burro, or mule which is 12 months of age or older, and is issued a current Equine License by the City Department of Animal Services. An animal which is under 12 months of age, and is the offspring of or is unweaned and being nursed by a female equine lawfully kept on the property where said animal is kept, shall not be considered an equine.

Evaluation Of Non-Compliance: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.6.1. (Evaluation Of Non-Compliance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.6.1), evaluation of non-compliance is the procedure to modify, discontinue, or revoke any discretionary zoning approval where needed to remedy non-compliance with the conditions of any conditional use or similar [quasi-judicial approval](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Existing Building: An existing building is defined as a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) lawfully constructed and completed under a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), if a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was required.

Existing Grade: Existing grade is defined as the [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) prior to [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Existing Uses: An existing use is defined as any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) enumerated in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) for which any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or portion of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d at the time the property is first classified in a zone, or subsequently allowed through [Div. 13B.3. (Ministerial Action)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.3), [Div. 13B.1. (Legislative Action)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.1), or [Div. 13B.2. (Quasi-Judicial Review)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.2).

Extended Home-Sharing: For the purposes of [Sec. 5C.3.2.B.4. (Extended Home-Sharing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), extended home-sharing is defined as home-sharing that is permitted for an unlimited number of days in a calendar year.

Exterior Face: Exterior face is defined as the outermost surface of any object such as a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Exterior Material Option: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.10.3. (Exterior Material Options)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.10.3), exterior material option is defined as building products allowed for use as primary or accessory [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) finish material.

Exterior Modification: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.5. (Exterior Modification)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), exterior modification is defined as work to the exterior of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Exterior Wall: Exterior wall is defined as any [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which forms the envelope of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), separating its [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from its exterior.

Extremely Low Income Household: Extremely low income household is defined as a [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with an annual income that does not exceed the amount designated for that category as defined in [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 50106](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=50106.&lawCode=HSC).

### F

Facade: Facade is defined as the [above-grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), non-roof portions of the exterior [building envelope](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), which includes cornices, bay windows or architectural projections, of any [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Facade Area: Facade area is defined as any surface area of a [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Facade Modification: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.5.a. (Facade Modification)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15) facade modification is an [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes a change to a [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving a modification of its existing design or outward appearance.

Facade Plane: See [Building Face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Faces: See [facing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Faith-Based Organization Project: Faith-based organization project is defined as a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) containing [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s located on land owned entirely, whether directly or through a wholly owned company or corporation, by a religious institution at the time of [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) filing and developed by or in partnership with a qualified developer. This includes ownership through an affiliated or associated nonprofit public benefit corporation organized pursuant to the Nonprofit Corporation Law (California Corporations Code, Sec. 5110. et seq.).

Facing: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.6. (Facing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.6), facing is defined as the exterior portions of a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that are exposed to a specified object or site element.

Feasible: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.1. (Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.1) and [Sec. 13B.9.1.A.1. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.1), feasible is defined as capable of being accomplished in a successful manner within a reasonable period of time, taking into account economic, environmental, social and technological factors.

Fence: A fence is defined as a constructed vertical barrier of wood, masonry, wire, metal, or other manufactured material, or combination of materials erected to enclose, screen, or separate areas. A fence differs from a [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in not having a solid foundation along its entire length.

Fill: Pursuant to [LAMC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Sec. 91.7003. (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-177778), fill is defined as a deposit of earth material placed by artificial means.

Final Map: A final map is defined as a map prepared in accordance with the provisions of [Article 11. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11), and the [Subdivision Map Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) subject to e recordation with the Los Angeles County Recorder upon final approval by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Final Tract Map: See [final map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Financial Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.5. (Financial Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.5), financial services is defined as professional services involving the investment, lending, or management of money and assets in a [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) setting rather than a private [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) setting. For private [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) settings, see [Sec. 5D.6.9. (Office)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.9).

Financial Services: Alternative: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.5.B. (Financial Services: Alternative)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.5), financial services: alternative is defined as [financial services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s involving for-profit lending facility offering small, unsecured, short-term loans, such as bail bonds, or a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that primarily consists of check cashing services for a fee, or any business where articles of personal property may be left as security in exchange for a loan of money. Financial services: alternative include pawnshops, precious metal buyback centers, short-term credit lenders, and title loan centers. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include remittance services, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.5. (Financial Services: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.5).

Financial Services: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.5.A. (Financial Services: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.5), financial services: general is defined as [financial services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that provide [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) banking services. Financial services: general include only those institutions engaged in the transfer and circulation of money, such as banks and credit unions. For [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s such as check-cashing businesses and payday lenders, see [Sec. 5D.6.5.B. (Financial Services: Alternative)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.5).

Finished Floor Elevation: Finished floor elevation is defined as the elevation of the uppermost surface of the structural floor.

Finished Grade: Finished grade is defined as the final [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which conforms to the approved plan, or where no [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) work is proposed, the [existing grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Fire Protection: For the purposes of [Article 11. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11), fire protection is defined as such fire hydrants and other protective devices as required by the Chief Engineer of the Fire Department.

First Public Road Paralleling the Sea: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2), first public road paralleling the sea is defined as that road nearest to the sea, as defined in [Sec. 30115 of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=PRC&division=20.&title=&part=&chapter=2.&article=), which: (a) is lawfully open to uninterrupted public use and is suitable for that use; (b) is publicly maintained; (c) is an improved, all-weather road open to [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) traffic in at least one direction; (d) is not subject to any restrictions on use by the public except when closed due to an emergency or when closed temporarily for military purposes; and (e) does, in fact, connect with other public roads, providing a continuous access system, and generally parallels and follows the shoreline of the sea to include all portions of the sea where the physical features, such as bays, lagoons, estuaries and wetlands cause the waters of the sea to extend landward from the generally continuous coastline.

Flatwork: For the purposes [Sec. 14.2.5.A. (Horizontal Encroachments)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), flatwork is defined as constructed objects 30 inches in height or less, measured from [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Examples of flatwork may include, but are not limited to: pavement, sidewalk, multi-use path, patio, low deck, or stairs or ramps 30 inches in height or less.

For the purposes of [Sec. 14.2.5.B. (Vertical Encroachments)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), flatwork is defined as constructed objects 30 inches in height or less. Examples of flatwork may include, but are not limited to: decking, walkways, patios, or planters.

Flood Hazard: Flood hazard is defined as a hazard to land or improvements due to overflow water having sufficient velocity to transport or deposit debris, scour the surface soil, dislodge or damage [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or erode the banks of water courses.

Floor Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.7. (Floor Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.7), floor area is defined as the cumulative amount of [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) floor space on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), within a room, or within a [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) space.

Floor Area Ratio: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.1. (Floor Area Ratio (FAR))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.1), floor area ratio or FAR is defined as the measurement of the total [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of all [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in relation to the size of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Focal Entry Feature: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.8.3. (Focal Entry Feature)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.8.3), focal entry features are design standards applied to enhance the primary entrance of a [building frontage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Focal Entry Feature Option: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.8.3.C.2. (Focal Entry Feature Options)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.8.3), focal entry feature options refer to packages of design standards options applied to enhance the primary entrance of a [building frontage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Food & Drink Preparation Area: Food & drink preparation area is defined as all [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within an eating & drinking [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where employees prepare food or beverages or are reserved for employee use, including kitchens, bartender stations, dishwashing facilities, storage, refrigeration closets, employee office, and break rooms.

Footcandle: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.10.1.D. (Measurement)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.10.1), a footcandle is a unit of illuminance. One footcandle is equivalent to one lumen per square foot and shall be measured using a light meter.

Foundation Inactive Wall Treatment Alternatives: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.4.2.E.3. (Foundation Inactive Wall Treatment Alternatives)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.2), foundation inactive wall treatment alternatives are defined as permanent design improvements located between exposed [foundation wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and the public realm, designed to improve visual interest and the pedestrian experience.

Foundation Wall: A foundation wall is defined as any [above-grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) portion of a [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located below the finished [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Freeway: Pursuant to [Sec. 8.3.2. (Freeway)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.3.2), freeway is defined as any property owned by the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) that is used for highway purposes.

Freight Loading Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.2.2.C.2. (Freight Loading Areas)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2), freight loading area is defined as areas designated for the on-site loading and unloading of freight vehicles.

Freight Railway Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.5.2. (Freight Railway Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.2), a freight railway facility is defined as any railway facility accommodating the transportation of cargo by train on a railway network. Freight railway facilities include freight railway track networks and accompanying railway yards, stations, and maintenance facilities. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include cargo transfer between vehicles; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.5.3. (Freight Transfer Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.3).

Freight Transfer Facility: Pursuant [Sec. 5D.5.3. (Freight Transfer Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.3), freight transfer facility is defined as a facility intended for the transshipment of freight between different modes of transport, including ship transport, rail transport, and road transport, and accompanying warehousing used in connection with such activities. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the storage of empty cargo containers; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s; see [Sec. 5D.7.5.E. (Storage, Outdoor: Cargo Container)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

Frequency: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.8. (Frequency)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.8), frequency is defined as the rate at which something occurs or is repeated over a given distance.

Front Yard: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.16.B.1. (Front Yard)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.16), a front yard is the area between a [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and an imaginary line running parallel to the [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). The imaginary line shall be drawn 15 feet back from the portion of the [primary street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [lot line-facing facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) nearest to the [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), measured perpendicularly to the [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Frontage Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.B.1. (Frontage Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), a frontage lot line is any [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that triggers [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) requirements. Frontage lot lines include all [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Frontage Planting Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.3.1. (Frontage Planting Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.3.1), a frontage planting area is defined as the area in a [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated and designed for plants.

Frontage Screen: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.8.1. (Frontage Screens)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.8.1), a frontage screen is defined as a device or combination of elements, including [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, trees and other plants, along a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conceals, obstructs or protects the public realm from [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, activities, or site elements.

Frontage Screen Type: Pursuant to, [Sec. 4C.8.1.C.2. (Frontage Screen Types)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.8.1), frontage screen types are defined as packages of standards for required [frontage screen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Frontage Yard: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.16.C.1. (Frontage Yard)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.16), frontage yard is defined as a category of [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s referring to all [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that [abut](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including [front yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [side street yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and [special yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Frontage Yard Fence & Wall: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.3.2. (Frontage Yard Fence & Wall)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.3.2), frontage yard fence & wall is defined as [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and hedges that are allowed in a [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Frontage Yard Fence & Wall Type: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.3.2.C.2. (Frontage Yard Fence & Wall Types)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.3.2), frontage yard fence & wall types refer to a package of standards, specified by the applied [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), that applies to [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and hedges located in a [frontage yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Fueling Station: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.2. (Fueling Station)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.2), a fueling station is defined as any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) dedicated to the sale and dispensing of [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) fuel.

Fueling Station: Large Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.2.B. (Fueling Station: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.2), fueling station: large vehicle is defined as any [fueling station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) dedicated to dispensing fuel for large vehicles. Large vehicles include [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s possessing three or more axles, such as trailer trucks, construction vehicles, motor homes, and recreation vehicles.

Fueling Station: Standard Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.2.A. (Fueling Station: Standard Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.2), fueling station: standard vehicle is defined as any [fueling station](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) dedicated to dispensing fuel for standard vehicles. Standard vehicles include [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s possessing two or fewer axles, such as cars, motorcycles, sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks, and vans.

Full-service Grocery Store: Full-service grocery store is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) store which stocks a minimum inventory in the following food groups and non-perishable items: fresh and frozen meats and poultry; canned, fresh, and frozen fruits and vegetables; dairy products; cereals; canned fish; bread products; infant food and formula; shampoo; pain medication; diapers; and feminine hygiene products.

Fully Shielded Luminaire: Fully shielded luminaire is defined as a luminaire that allows no light emission above a horizontal plane through the luminaire.

Future Street or Alley: Future street or alley is defined as any real property which the owner has offered for dedication to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for street or [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) purposes, but which has been rejected by the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), subject to the right of the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to rescind its action and accept by resolution at any later date and without further action by the owner, all or part of the property as a public street or [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

### G

General Commercial Use: Pursuant to [Div. 5D.6. (General Commercial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6), general commercial uses are defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that involve business activity serving the general public, including [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), professional and personal services, hospitality, and entertainment.

General Plan: The General Plan is the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)’s comprehensive framework that sets forth policies, goals, and objectives to guide the physical development of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), while outlining the vision and priorities of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). It consists of 11 citywide elements in addition to a Land Use Element, composed of 34 Community Plans. The General Plan serves as the legal basis for all land use policy decisions. Preparation and maintenance of the General Plan is mandated by the State, pursuant to [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 65300](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&division=1.&title=7.&part=&chapter=3.&article=5.).
