General Plan Land Use Designation: General Plan Land Use Designations are designations established in Appendix A to the [Framework Element](https://planning.lacity.gov/plans-policies/framework-element), which broadly identifies intensities, densities, heights, and general uses allowed where the designations are mapped on the General Plan Land Use Map, and implemented through the corresponding zoning districts from the Zoning Code, as shown in correspondence tables in Appendix A or as otherwise provided in the community plan.

Gore-Shaped Lot: A gore-shaped lot is defined as an irregularly shaped [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes an angle of 65 degrees or less between intersecting [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Grade: Grade is defined as the [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or contour of the ground surface of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Grade Plane: See [grade plane elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Grade Plane Elevation: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.9. (Grade Plane Elevation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.9), grade plane elevation is defined as a reference plane, representing the average [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the existing ground level adjoining a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and its [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, from which the height of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall be measured.

Grading: Grading is defined as any cut or fill, combination of cut and fill, or recompaction of soil, rock, or other earth materials.

Grocery Store: For the purposes of [Article 15. (Fees)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15), grocery store is defined as a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is for a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of which greater than 1/2 of the [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is devoted to the sale of food items intended for consumption or use off the premises, excluding alcoholic beverages.

Ground Floor: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10.C. (Ground Floor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), ground floor is defined as the [finished floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Ground Floor Elevation: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.6.2. (Ground Floor Elevation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.6.2), ground floor elevation is defined as the finished floor height associated with the [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) having its [finished floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) nearest to the [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Ground Story: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10.A. (Ground Story)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), ground story is defined as the lowest [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) meeting the criteria of either Continuous Ground Story (Typical) or Ground Story Modules pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10. (Story)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), depending on [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) conditions.

Ground Story Facade: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10.B. (Ground Story Facade)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), ground story facade is defined as the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the full height of the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Ground Story Height: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.6.1. (Ground Story Height)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.6.1), ground story height is defined as the floor-to-floor height of the [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) having its [finished floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) nearest to the [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Ground Story Inactive Wall Treatment Alternatives: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.4.2.E.3. (Ground Story Inactive Wall Treatment Alternatives)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.2), ground story inactive wall treatment alternatives are permanent design improvements located between segments of [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) active [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and the public realm, designed to improve visual interest and the pedestrian experience.

Ground Story Windows: Ground story windows are defined as any windows on the [ground story facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Ground Surface: Ground surface is defined as any hardscape or softscape surface which is [at-grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and is exterior to any building.

Ground-Mounted Equipment: Ground-mounted equipment is defined as any [mechanical equipment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [utility equipment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is fixed to the ground at or below [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in order to serve a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or facility on the same [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Sec. 4C.12.2. (Ground-Mounted Equipment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.12.2) for applicable development standards.

### H

Habitable Room: Habitable room is defined as an [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) space in a [residential building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) commonly used for living purposes, but not including any lobby, hall, closet, storage space, water closet, bath, toilet, slop sink, general utility room, [kitchen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) area, or service porch. A recess from a room or an alcove (other than a dining area), or a [mezzanine](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) having 50 square feet or more of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and located where it could be partitioned off to form a habitable room, shall be considered a habitable room.

Habitable Space: Habitable space is defined as any [occupiable space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed and intended for living, sleeping, eating, or cooking. Restrooms, toilet rooms, closets, halls, storage or utility spaces, and similar areas are not considered habitable spaces.

Health Center: For the purposes of [Sec. 9.3.4.C.3. (Health Center Incentive Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3.4), a health center is defined as a healthcare facility certified by the United States Department of Health and Human Services, Health Resources and Services Administration (HRSA) as a Federally Qualified Health Center (FQHC), or FQHC Look-Alike as defined by the HRSA.

Hearing Officer: A hearing officer is defined as any [Department](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of City Planning staff member conducting a public hearing on behalf of the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Heavy Commercial Use: Pursuant to [Div. 5D.7. (Heavy Commercial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7), heavy commercial uses are defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that involve the servicing and sale of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and businesses dedicated primarily to storage.

Heavy Industrial Use: Pursuant to [Div. 5D.9. (Heavy Industrial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9), heavy industrial uses are defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s involving manufacturing, processing of animal products, waste, or extraction activities, which requires siting away from the general public due to potentially adverse impacts on the immediate surroundings.

Height in Feet: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.2. (Height in Feet)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.2), height in feet is defined as the vertical dimension of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) measured in feet.

Height in Stories: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.3. (Height in Stories)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.3), height in stories is defined as the vertical dimension of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) measured in [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Heliport: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.5.4. (Heliport)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.4), heliport is defined as any public-use, special-use, or personal-use airport, as defined by the [California Code of Regulations, Title 21. Sec. 3527. (Definitions)](https://dot.ca.gov/-/media/dot-media/programs/aeronautics/documents/ccr_title_21_section_3525_through_3560.pdf), suitable only for use by helicopters.

High-Rise Sign 1: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.2. (High-Rise Sign 1)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), a high-rise sign 1 is a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located at least 100 feet [above-grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and attached to the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

High-Rise Sign 2: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.3. (High-Rise Sign 2)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), a high-rise sign 2 is a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located at least 100 feet [above-grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and attached to the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within close proximity to the top of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

High Quality Transit Service: High quality transit service is defined as a transit route with a service frequency of 15 minutes or less during peak commute hours in one direction. For the purpose of determining service interval frequency, a bus route may include a combination of overlapping bus lines when part of a “colinear” or “family” line as determined in coordination with Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG and local transit agencies, may be considered as one service route for the purpose of calculating service interval frequency.

Higher Opportunity Area: Higher opportunity area is defined as including High and Highest Resource Areas as defined and identified by the California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (TCAC).

Hillside Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 1.5.6. (Hillside Area Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.5.6), a hillside area is defined as any area shown on the Hillside Area Map.

Historic: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), historic is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including street features, furniture or fixtures, which depicts, represents or is associated with persons or phenomena which significantly affect or which have significantly affected the functional activities, heritage, growth or development of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), state, or nation.

Historic Preservation Overlay Zone: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), Historic Preservation Overlay Zone is defined as any area of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) containing [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s having [historic](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), architectural, cultural or aesthetic significance and designated as a Historic Preservation Overlay Zone.

Historic Resource: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.12. (Redevelopment Plan Procedures)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12) of this Code, historic resource is defined as designated or surveyed resources including properties listed in or formally determined eligible for listing in the National Register of Historic Places, the California Register of Historical Resources, locally designated [Historic-Cultural Monument](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s (HCMs) and [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s ( [HPOZ](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s); and properties identified as significant per eligibility criteria in SurveyLA and the [Community Redevelopment Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) surveys or any subsequent City sanctioned or accepted surveys.

Historic Resources Survey: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), a Historic Resources Survey is a document which identifies all contributing and non-contributing [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and all contributing [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, individually or collectively, including street features, furniture or fixtures, and which is certified as to its accuracy and completeness by the Cultural Heritage Commission.

Historic-Cultural Monument: Pursuant to [Sec. 22.171.10. (Procedures for Designation of Monuments)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-65320) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), a Historic-Cultural Monument (HCM) is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as a City Historic-Cultural Monument.

Historical Property Contract: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), a historical property contract is defined as a contract between an owner or owners of a Historical-Cultural Monument or a [contributing element](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), which meets all requirements of [Sec. 50281 and 50282 of the California Government Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?division=1.&chapter=1.&part=1.&lawCode=GOV&title=5.&article=12.) and [Sec. 19.140 et seq.](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-45914) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Historical Resource: As defined by [California Public Resources Code, Sec. 21084.1.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PRC&sectionNum=21084.1.), and as determined by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), in consultation with the Office of Historic Resources, a historical resource means those resources that meet the definition of a historical resource in [Sec. 21084.1 (Historical Resources) of the Public Resources Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PRC&sectionNum=21084.1.) and [Sec. 15064.5(a) (Determining the Significance of Impacts to Archaeological and Historical Resources)](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I87D9F3AA5B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3?viewType=FullText&listSource=Search&originationContext=Search+Result&transitionType=SearchItem&contextData=(sc.Search)&navigationPath=Search%2fv1%2fresults%2fnavigation%2fi0a89c5da00000193f99814c5e12f30cf%3fppcid%3d6fd0f3f74f664f618c4e9b8e3a3fa4f0%26Nav%3dREGULATION_PUBLICVIEW%26fragmentIdentifier%3dI87D9F3AA5B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3%26startIndex%3d1%26transitionType%3dSearchItem%26contextData%3d%2528sc.Default%2529%26originationContext%3dSearch%2520Result&list=REGULATION_PUBLICVIEW&rank=1&t_T2=15064.5&t_S1=CA+ADC+s) of the [CEQA Guideline](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Homeless Person: Homeless person as defined in the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. Sec. 11301 et seq.).

Horizontal Band Articulation: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.6.3. (Horizontal Band Articulation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.6.3), horizontal band articulation is defined as a continuous band of material running horizontally across a [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Horizontal Encroachment: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.1.5.A. (Horizontal Encroachments)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.1.5), a horizontal encroachment is defined as a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or assembly that extends horizontally into a space where [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are typically prohibited.

Horizontal Illuminance: Horizontal illuminance is defined as the amount of light falling on a horizontal plane, as measured with a light meter in units of [footcandle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Hospital: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.5. (Hospital)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.5), hospital is defined as an inpatient or outpatient healthcare facility that provides direct medical treatment to patients.

Hospital: Local: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.5.A. (Hospital: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.5), hospital: local is defined as an inpatient or outpatient acute or subacute care facility with a capacity of 100 or fewer beds that provides direct medical treatment to patients. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include outpatient facilities not providing acute or sub-acute care, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.8. (Medical Clinic)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.8).

Hospital: Regional: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.5.B. (Hospital: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.5), hospital: regional is defined as an inpatient acute care and sub-acute care facility with a capacity of more than 100 beds that provides direct medical treatment to patients. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include inpatient facilities providing sub-acute care with a capacity of fewer than 100 beds, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.5.A. (Hospital: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.5).

Host: For the purposes of [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), host is defined as an individual who is registered for home-sharing pursuant to [Sec. 5C.3.2. (Home-Sharing Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2).

Hosting Platform: For the purposes of [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), hosting platform is defined as a [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that participates in short-term rental business by collecting or receiving a fee, directly or indirectly through an agent or intermediary, for conducting a booking service transaction using any medium of facilitation.

Household: Household is defined as one or more persons living together in a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), with common access to, and common use of all living, kitchen, and eating areas within the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Household Business: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.2. (Household Business)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2), a household business is a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that combines a [dwelling](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with productive uses and entrepreneurial activities within a unit or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Household Business: Family Child Care: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.2.A. (Household Business: Family Child Care)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2), a household business: family child care is defined as the provision of non-medical care and supervision for children in the provider's primary residence for periods of less than 24 hours per day. No more than 14 children shall be in care, unless [Use District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) standards specify otherwise. Any children under the age of 10 years who reside within the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and are in care count toward the maximum number of children in care. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall comply with all regulations set forth in [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 1597.465. (Family Day Care Homes)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1597.465#:).

Household Business: Home Occupation: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.2.B. (Household Business: Home Occupation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2), household business: home occupation is defined as the incidental use of a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the intent of conducting a business enterprise by a primary [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Home occupation business enterprises are limited to instructional services, personal services, [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and [industrial homework](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Household Business: Home-Sharing: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.2.C. (Household Business: Home-Sharing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2), household business: home-sharing is defined as the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [primary residence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for [lodging](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for periods of 30 days consecutively or less, and no more than 120 days annually. The [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for home-sharing shall be in conjunction with a [dwelling](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). The [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for home-sharing shall meet the registration and eligibility requirements pursuant to [Sec. 5C.3.2. (Home-Sharing Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2).

Household Business: Joint Living & Work Quarters: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.2.D. (Household Business: Joint Living & Work Quarters)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2), household business: joint living & work quarters is defined as the adaptive reuse of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), which is part of an [adaptive reuse project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), from commercial or industrial uses to [household business: live/work](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Household Business: Live/Work: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.2.E. (Household Business: Live/Work)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2), household business: live/work is defined as the combination of a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with a work space designated for productive uses and entrepreneurial activities within a single [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Household Dwelling Unit: Household dwelling unit is defined as a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) serving as a residency having an occupancy of greater than 30 days consecutively, and that includes a [kitchen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [kitchenette](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Housing Development Project: As the term "housing development" is defined in subdivision (i) of [California Government Code, Sec. 65915.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=65915.&lawCode=GOV), a development project with five or more [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s including mixed-use developments; and [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or common interest developments as defined in [California Civil Code, Sec. 4100.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=4100)

### I

Illuminated Canopy Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.4. (Illuminated Canopy Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), an illuminated canopy sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) integrated into an enclosed internally illuminated canopy that is attached to the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

In-Kind: In-kind is defined as a replacement with the same material type, design, dimension, texture, detailing, and exterior appearance.

Incentive: For purposes of [Sec. 9.2.1. (State Density Bonus Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), [Sec. 9.2.2. (Affordable Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), [Sec. 9.2.3. (Opportunity Corridors Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), [Sec. 9.2.4. (Corridor Transitions Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), and [Sec. 9.2.5. (Transit Oriented Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.5), incentive is defined as a reduction in a site [development standard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or a modification to a site zoning code or architectural design requirement that results in identifiable and actual cost reductions to provide for affordable housing costs as defined in California Government Code Sec. 65915(k).

Inclusionary Housing Project: Inclusionary housing project is defined as a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the construction of 10 or more [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s which is subject to the requirements established in [Sec. 5C.3.1. (Inclusionary Housing Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.1).

Individual with a Disability: For the purposes of [Reasonable Accommodation (Sec. 13B.5.5.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.5), as defined under the [Acts](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), individual with a disability is any person who has a physical or mental impairment that limits one or more major life activities, anyone who is regarded as having that type of impairment or, anyone who has a record of that type of impairment.

Indoor Recreation: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.2. (Indoor Recreation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.2), indoor recreation is defined as any indoor use providing sports, fitness, leisure, amusement, or recreational facilities. Indoor recreation includes the following [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s when fully indoors: sports courts, health clubs, spas, fitness, martial arts, and dance studios, gymnasiums, aquatics centers, bowling alleys, billiard halls, gaming arcades, ice skating and roller rinks, skate parks, play facilities, and amusement rides.

Indoor Recreation: Commercial: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.2.B. (Indoor Recreation: Commercial)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.2), indoor recreation: commercial is defined as any indoor recreational [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) owned or operated by a private or commercial entity. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include associated spectator facilities with seating capacity greater than 500 seats, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.4.1. (Amphitheater or Stadium)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.1).

Indoor Recreation: Public: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.2.A. (Indoor Recreation: Public)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.2), indoor recreation: public is defined as any indoor recreational [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) owned or operated by or in partnership with a public institution.

Industrial Homework: Industrial homework is the same as defined in [California Labor Code, Sec. 2650](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=2650.&lawCode=LAB).

Instructional Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.6. (Instructional Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.6), instructional services are defined as any establishment primarily engaged in offering avocational or recreational educational courses to adults or children for the purposes of play, amusement, or relaxation, including education offered for the intent of teaching the fundamentals, skills, or techniques of a hobby or activity. Includes establishments offering programs in art, cooking, drama, driving, language, music, sewing, tutoring, or other similar forms of self-improvement. For vocational and other educational [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, see [Sec. 5D.3.9. (School)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.9).

Integrated Parking: Integrated parking is defined as a [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within or attached to a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is primarily used for a non-parking [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, such as [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or commercial [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. For a [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to be considered an integrated parking [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), the [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall not be greater than the [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Intensification of Use: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.1.15.B.6.b. (Intensification of Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.1.15), intensification of use is defined as work that increases the intensity of a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), such as an increase in [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, seating capacity, or the number of people in care.

Interim Lodging Unit Housing Project: Interim lodging unit housing project is defined as the physical re-purposing or adaptation of an existing [lodging unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), for [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as [supportive housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [transitional housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for persons experiencing homelessness or those at risk of homelessness.

Interior: Interior is defined as all [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) areas included within surrounding [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Interior Wall: Interior wall is defined as any [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is within the [building envelope](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and that is not separating the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)'s [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from its exterior.

Inundation: Inundation is defined as ponded water, or water in motion, of sufficient depth to damage property due to the presence of the water or to the deposit of silt.

### J

Junior Accessory Dwelling Unit: See [Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning), Sec. 12.03. (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lapz/0-0-0-886) of this Code.

### K

Kitchen: Kitchen is defined as an area designed to be used for the preparation of food that includes a sink and has all of the following standards: 1) a refrigerator rough-in greater than 30 inches in width; 2) a gas connection or 240V electrical connection; 3) an oven and range; and 4) counter space in excess of 10 square feet.

Kitchenette: Kitchenette is defined as an area designed to be used for the preparation of food that includes a sink and meets all of the following standards: 1) a refrigerator rough-in 30 inches in width or less; 2) no gas connection or 240V electrical connection; 3) counter space 10 square feet or less.

### L

Landing Platform: Landing platform is defined as the portion of a floor [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to an elevator, ramp, stair, or door, designed to provide a stable space to stand.

Landscaping: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), landscaping is defined as the design and organization of landforms, hardscape, and softscape, including individual groupings of trees, shrubs, groundcovers, vines, pathways, arbors, etc. As the term is used in the remainder of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A), landscaping is defined as any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) non-building structure features including; standalone [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, site furniture, [flatwork](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), ground treatments, vegetation, landforms, stormwater management features, outdoor lighting, water features, or outdoor [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and circulation.

Large Species Tree: Large species tree is defined as a tree with a minimum 30-foot canopy spread at maturity.

Leachates: Leachates is defined as any liquid which has come into contact with or percolated through composting or curing materials and contains extracted or dissolved substances therefrom, or any other liquid which has been generated by the decomposition process.

Leader: Leader is defined as the tip of the main stem of a plant.

Light Industrial Use: Pursuant to [Div. 5D.8. (Light Industrial)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8), light industrial uses are defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s involving the production, warehousing, or manufacturing of goods, materials, and products in an intensive manner that require a significant separation from [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and commercial districts.

Light Trespass: Light trespass is defined as light that falls beyond the property it is intended to illuminate.

Linkage Fee: Pursuant to [Sec. 15.4.3. (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#15.4.3), linkage fee is defined as the fee assessed on certain development projects in order to mitigate the impact of the additional demand for affordable housing caused by such activity.

Living Wall: Living wall is defined as a system permanently attached to the exterior [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), supporting vegetation with its growing medium and integrated irrigation system.

Loading Space: Loading space is defined as a designated space within a [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that accommodates the short-term parking of a [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the purposes of loading and unloading passengers, goods, or materials.

Local Coastal Program: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.1. (Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.1), Local Coastal Program is the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)'s land use plans and other applicable general plan elements, zoning ordinances, zoning district maps, and proposed implementing actions, which when taken together, meet the requirements of, and implement the provisions and policies of, the California Coastal Act of 1976.

Local Public Agency: For purposes of [Sec. 9.4.1. (Permanent Supportive Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.1), [Sec. 9.4.2. (Interim Conversions of Lodging Units Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.2), local public agency is defined as an agency, identified on a list maintained by the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that funds [supportive housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [transitional housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for persons experiencing homelessness or at risk of homelessness.

Local Street: Local street is defined as any [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated as a local street on the Citywide General Plan Circulation System maps of the [Circulation Element](https://planning.lacity.gov/odocument/523f2a95-9d72-41d7-aba5-1972f84c1d36/Mobility_Plan_2035.pdf) of the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Lodging: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.7. (Lodging)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.7), lodging is defined as commercial overnight accommodations for transient occupancy, often for periods of 30 consecutive days, or less. Lodging uses shall not serve as a primary residence. Lodging uses include, hotels, motels, hostels, and bed and breakfast establishments. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.2.2.C. (Household Business: Home-Sharing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2). For [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) housing accommodations see [Div. 5D.2. (Residential Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2).

Lodging Unit: Lodging unit is defined as any [habitable room](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or rooms, designed or used for transient occupancy by a single party, often for a period of 30 consecutive days or less. Lodging units must be associated with the [lodging](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) commercial [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Los Angeles City Oil Field Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 8.2.4.B.3.d. (Los Angeles City Oil Field Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.4) is defined as all land in the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within the areas identified on the maps in [Ord. No. 156,166](https://clkrep.lacity.org/onlinedocs/1980/80-3951_ORD_156166_12-08-1981.pdf) located in [Council File No. 80-3951](https://cityclerk.lacity.org/lacityclerkconnect/index.cfm?fa=ccfi.viewrecord&cfnumber=80-3951), and shall include all oil producing zones beneath those areas, but no deeper than the third zone beneath the surface of the earth.

Los Angeles Fire Department Equipment: Los Angeles Fire Department Equipment is defined as any equipment owned or installed for the use of the Los Angeles Fire Department.

Lot: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.11. (Lot)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.11) a lot is defined as one or more [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s of land identified for the purpose of development and meets all the standards of [Sec. 14.2.11. (Lot)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.11).

Lot Amenity Alternatives: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.5. (Lot Amenity Alternatives)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.5) lot amenity alternatives are defined as space types with a predetermined set of design standards that may be used as an allowable alternative to the standard [lot amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) requirements of a [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B).

Lot Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.1. (Lot Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.1), lot amenity space is defined as an area on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated to be used for active or passive recreation, including [common outdoor amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and [public amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Lot Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.1.1. (Lot Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.1.1), lot area is defined as the amount of land area within the boundaries of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Lot Area Per Household Dwelling Unit: Pursuant to [Sec. 6C.1.3. (Lot Area per Efficiency Dwelling Unit)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/6#6C.1.3), lot area per efficiency dwelling unit is defined as the maximum number of [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s allowed on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) based on [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Lot Area Per Efficiency Dwelling Unit: Pursuant to [Sec. 6C.1.2. (Lot Area per Household Dwelling Unit)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/6#6C.1.2), lot area per household dwelling unit is defined as the maximum number of [household dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s allowed on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) based on [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Lot Line: Lot line is defined as the legal boundaries of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), as determined pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12. (Lot Line Determination)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12).

Lot Line-Facing Facade: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.6.B. (Lot Line-Facing Facade)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.6), lot line-facing facade is defined as the portions of any frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.C.3. (Frontage Applicable Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2) having no permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) (not including [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s) located between the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and a [common lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Lot Modification: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.3. (Lot Modification)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), lot modification is defined as the modification of the [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s of any existing [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) through the [Subdivision Map Act](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [Article 11. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11), including the division of land as defined in [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66424](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=66424.).

Lot Tie: Lot tie is defined as a legally binding covenant to hold multiple [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s as one.

Lot Width: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.1.2. (Lot Width)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.1.2), lot width is defined as the length of [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s bounding a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Low Impact Development: Low impact development refers to the Low Impact Development (LID) program, which establishes requirements for stormwater and urban runoff control. The program is administered by LA Sanitation and Environment (LASAN) and is authorized by [Chapter VI., Sec. 64.72. (Stormwater and Urban Runoff Pollution Control Measures for Development Planning and Construction Activities)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-162923) of this Code.

Low Income Household: A low income household is a [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) whose annual income, adjusted for family size, does not exceed 80 percent of the area median income as designated for this category in the [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 50079.5](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=50079.5.&lawCode=HSC).

Lower Income Household: A lower income household is a [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) whose annual income, adjusted for family size, does not exceed 80 percent of the area median income as designated for this category in California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 50079.5. Lower income household includes [very low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [extremely low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. For the purposes of [Div. 13B.12. (Redevelopment Plan Procedures)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12) of this Code, lower income household is defined as the meaning ascribed thereto in the Development Guidelines and Controls for Residential Hotels in the City Center and Central Industrial redevelopment project areas, adopted by the former [CRA](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on June 15, 2006.

Lower Income Student: Lower income student is defined as a student who has a [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) income and asset level that does not exceed the level for Cal Grant A or Cal Grant B award recipients as set forth in California Education Code Sec. 69432.7(k)(1). The eligibility of a student to occupy a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for lower income students shall be verified by an affidavit, award letter, or letter of eligibility provided by the institution of higher education in which the student is enrolled or by the California Student Aid Commission that the student receives or is eligible for financial aid, including an institutional grant or fee waiver from the college or university, the California Student Aid Commission, or the federal government.

Lower Opportunity Area: Low Resource Areas as defined and identified by the California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (TCAC).

Luminaire: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.10.1. (Outdoor Lighting)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.10.1), luminaire is defined as the complete lighting unit (fixture), consisting of a lamp or lamps, and ballasts (when applicable), together with the parts designed to distribute the light (reflector, lens, diffuser), to position and protect the lamps, and to connect the lamps to the power supply.

### M

Machine Shop: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.1. (Machine Shop)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.1), a machine shop is defined as any facility engaged in the maintenance, repair, custom fabrication and finishing of products, parts, props, equipment, or machinery primarily using metal and woodworking machinery and tools. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the servicing of consumer goods when occupying less than 3,000 square feet in area; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.10. (Personal Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.10). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) repair and maintenance; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.1. (Motor Vehicle Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the fabrication of heavy machinery used for manufacturing, [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, aircraft or watercraft; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.9.2.A. (Manufacturing, Heavy: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2).

Main Traveled Roadway of a Freeway: Main traveled roadway of a freeway is defined as the portion of a [freeway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including interchange [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s connecting one [freeway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with another, which is designed for the movement of large volumes of vehicular traffic, efficiently and safely at high speed. Does not include service [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, landscape areas, or ingress or egress ramps connecting the [freeway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with other streets.

Maintenance & Repair: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.9. (Maintenance & Repair)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), maintenance & repair is defined as work that does not qualify as a [site modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [major remodel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [exterior modification](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and does not impact the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)'s ability to meet any applicable zoning requirements. Replacement of deteriorated or damaged parts of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is considered maintenance & repair; however, in a Character Frontage District, [CPIO](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), Conservation District, or [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), direct replacement may have additional requirements and processes. Maintenance & repair includes repair of site components such as restriping existing parking stripes, resealing [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, pothole repair, or replanting plants.

For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), maintenance & repair is defined as any work done to correct the deterioration, decay of, or damage to a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or any part thereof, including replacement [in-kind](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where required, and which does not involve a change in the existing design, materials, or exterior paint color.

Major Remodel: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.2. (Major Remodel)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), major remodel is defined as work that includes significant removal, disassembly, or replacement of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or portions of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that does not add to or change the [building footprint](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and meets the standards in [Sec. 14.2.15.B.2. (Major Remodel)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15).

Major Transit Stop: Major transit stop is defined pursuant California Public Resources Code Sec. 21064.3, and also includes a [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) containing a rail or bus rapid transit station or the intersection of two or more bus routes with a service interval of 20 minutes or less during the morning and afternoon peak commute periods in either direction. The stations or bus routes may be existing, under construction or included in the most recent Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Regional Transportation Plan (RTP). A bus route may include a combination of overlapping bus lines and may be considered as one service route for the purpose of calculating service interval frequency when part of a “colinear”, “family”, or augmented line as determined in coordination with SCAG and transit agencies.

Majority: For the purposes of [Article 13. (Administration)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13), majority is defined as a majority number of the members of the respective body, not the majority of members present.

Manager Unit: See [caretaker unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Manufacturing, Heavy: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.2. (Manufacturing, Heavy)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2), manufacturing, heavy is defined as any [heavy industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the making or processing of materials or components into finished products.

Manufacturing, Heavy: Chemical Products: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.2.B. (Chemical Products)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2), manufacturing, heavy: chemical products is defined as any [manufacturing, heavy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) producing basic chemicals or manufacturing products by predominantly chemical processes. Includes, but is not limited to, production of acid, alkali, organic chemical, salt, dry color, pigment, synthetic fiber, fertilizer, explosives, or paint. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include those [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.9.2.C. (Manufacturing, Heavy: Petroleum & Coal Products)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2).

Manufacturing, Heavy: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.2.A. (Manufacturing, Heavy: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2), manufacturing, heavy: general is defined as manufacturing that requires significant health, safety, or environmental precautions due to potential adverse impacts from the manufacturing process on immediate surroundings. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes, but is not limited to, the manufacturing of heavy machinery, [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, aircraft and watercraft, primary metal products, wood or paper products, metal fabrication, or manufacturing involving the processing, mixing, or refinement of inorganic raw materials. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include those [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.9.2.B. (Manufacturing, Heavy: Chemical Products)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include those [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.9.2.C. (Manufacturing, Heavy: Petroleum & Coal Products)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2).

Manufacturing, Heavy: Petroleum & Coal Products: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.2.C. (Manufacturing, Heavy: Petroleum & Coal Products)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2), manufacturing, heavy: petroleum & coal products is defined as any [manufacturing, heavy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that processes petroleum, coal, plastic, or rubber materials into products, including the refining of petroleum, gas, or other hydrocarbons.

Manufacturing, Light: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3. (Manufacturing, Light)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), manufacturing, light is defined as any [light industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the making or processing of materials or components into new products.

Manufacturing, Light: Alcoholic Beverage: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3.B. (Manufacturing, Light: Alcoholic Beverage)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), manufacturing, light: alcoholic beverage is defined as any [manufacturing, light](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where beer, wine, or other alcoholic beverages are fermented, distilled, and/or processed for distribution and sale on a wholesale basis. For [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) sale of any alcoholic beverage, see [Sec. 5D.6.12.B. (Retail: Alcohol)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12).

Manufacturing, Light: Artistic & Artisanal: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3.C. (Manufacturing, Light: Artistic & Artisanal)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), manufacturing, light: artistic & artisanal is defined as a small-scale [manufacturing, light](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where skilled craftspersons are integral to the creation of each product, materials, substances, or components, and may include, but are not limited to the use of hand tools or light mechanical equipment such as commercial mixers, sewing machines, wax melters, bottle sealers, paste filling machines, and button press machines. Manufacturing, light: artistic & artisanal [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are less than 5,000 square feet in area, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s larger than 5,000 square feet in area see [Sec. 5D.8.2. (Manufacturing, Light: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2).

Manufacturing, Light: Cosmetic & Pharmaceutical: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.2.D. (Manufacturing, Light: Cosmetic & Pharmaceutical)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2), manufacturing, light: cosmetic & pharmaceutical is defined as any [manufacturing, light](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where cosmetics, soaps, or pharmaceutical drugs are produced. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes, but is not limited to, manufacturing of makeup products, deodorants, shampoos, hair dyes, perfumes, skin moisturizers, medications, or supplements.

Manufacturing, Light: Electronics: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.2.E. (Manufacturing, Light: Electronics)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2), manufacturing, light: electronics is defined as any [manufacturing, light](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involved in the manufacturing or assembly of computer or electronic products, electrical equipment, appliances, fixtures, or electronic product components. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes testing and repair incidental to the product or component assembly.

Manufacturing, Light: Food & Drink: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3.F. (Manufacturing, Light: Food & Drink)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), manufacturing, light: food & drink is defined as any [manufacturing, light](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where food or drink products are processed or manufactured. The food and beverage products manufactured in these facilities are typically sold to wholesalers or retailers for distribution to consumers. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes, but is not limited to, the processing and packaging of the following: sodas & juices, coffee & tea, ice, dairy products, fruit, nut, & vegetable products, grain & oilseeds, baked or fried goods, sugar and confectionery products, animal food, and tobacco products. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes food & drink products composed of previously rendered animal products. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include meat processing, the rendering of animal products, or animal slaughtering, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.9.1. (Animal Products Processing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.1). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include breweries, distilleries, and wineries, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.8.2.B. (Manufacturing, Light: Alcoholic Beverage)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2).

Manufacturing, Light: Garment & Accessory: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3.G. (Manufacturing, Light: Garment & Accessory)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), manufacturing, light: garment & accessory is defined as any manufacturing, light [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the cutting, stitching or assembly of materials to produce finished clothing, footwear, and accessories. Specific activities include, but are not limited to, sewing of finished textiles, printing or stenciling of designs on garments, assembly of accessories or footwear, or the knitting of finished garments. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include those [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.8.2.H. (Manufacturing, Light: Textile)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2).

Manufacturing, Light: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.2.A. (Manufacturing, Light: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2), Manufacturing, light: general is defined as the manufacturing of finished goods intended to be sold as consumer goods to the general public, including devices and instruments used in a workplace. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes, but is not limited to, the manufacturing and assembly of the following: medical equipment and supplies; semiconductors and electronic instruments; signs and printed material; musical instruments; jewelry; toys; furniture; crates; boxes; and barrels. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include those [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.9.2.A. (Manufacturing, Heavy: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.2).

Manufacturing, Light: Textile: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3.H. (Manufacturing, Light: Textile)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), manufacturing, light: textile is defined as any [manufacturing, light](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving mechanized production of fibers and fabrics used to create materials for the production of garments and accessories. Specific activities include, but are not limited to, textile spinning, weaving, dying, printing, or finishing. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include those [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in [Sec. 5D.8.2.G. (Manufacturing, light: Garment & Accessory)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.2).

Marquee Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.5. (Marquee Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), a marquee sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) attached to the periphery of a marquee.

Mayor: Mayor is defined pursuant to [Sec. 200. (City Officers)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-364) of the [City Charter](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-2).

Maximum Allowable Residential Density: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.19. (Maximum Allowable Residential Density)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.19) maximum allowable residential density is defined as the greatest number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s allowed on a [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as defined in California Government Code Sec. 65915(o)(6).

Mechanical Equipment: Mechanical equipment is defined as any building mechanical services equipment including heating, cooling, and ventilation equipment; electrical systems, plumbing or piping; or any sustainable energy systems.

Mechanical Exhaust Outlet: Mechanical exhaust outlet is defined as any pneumatic conveyor or port which expels any air or gas as part of the function of any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) mechanical systems.

Medical Clinic: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.8. (Medical Clinic)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.8), medical clinic is defined as an outpatient healthcare facility that provides direct medical, dental, or therapeutic services to patients. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include healthcare facilities providing acute, subacute or inpatient healthcare; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.8.A. (Hospital: Local)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8) and [Sec. 5D.3.8.B. (Hospital: Regional)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.8).

Mezzanine: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10.H. (Mezzanine)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), mezzanine is defined as an intermediate level within a story of a building.

Mineral & Ore Extraction: Pursuant to [5D.9.6. (Mineral & Ore Extraction)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.6), mineral & ore extraction is defined as any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) engaged in the extraction of metallic minerals, nonmetallic minerals, or other natural compounds. This use includes the exploration or development of any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for such purposes, and any preparation of those resources until the point of shipment from the producing property. This use includes metal ore mining, nonmetallic mineral mining, and quarrying. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include extraction, recovery, or production of oil, natural gas, or any other hydrocarbon materials, for these activities see [Sec. 5D.9.7. (Oil, Gas, or Hydrocarbon Well)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.7).

Ministerial Action: See [ministerial decision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Ministerial Decision: Ministerial decision is defined as a decision based on the non-discretionary application of objective standards. See [Sec. 13A.2.1.B. (Procedural Categories)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.1).

Mobile Home: Mobile home is defined as a structure transportable in one or more sections, designed and equipped to be used as a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [accessory dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This structure shall comply with all applicable provisions of the [California Health and Safety Code, Div. 13. (Housing), Part 2. (Manufactured Housing)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayexpandedbranch.xhtml?tocCode=HSC&division=13.&title=&part=2.&chapter=&article=). The term “mobile home” shall not include a factory-built home, [recreational vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or commercial coach.

Mobile Home Park: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.3. (Mobile Home Park)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.3), mobile home park is defined as any [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or portion of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) used to provide rental or lease sites for two or more individual manufactured homes, [mobile home](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or [park trailer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) used to provide housing accommodations.

Model Dwelling: Model dwelling is defined as a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed to be temporarily used as an example of a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which have been built or are proposed to be built in the same [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or multiple unit development. See [Sec. 11.1.3.M. (Model)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.1.3).

Moderate Income Household: Moderate income household is defined as a [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with an annual income that does not exceed the amount designated for that category as defined in California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 50093.

Moderate Opportunity Area: Moderate opportunity area is defined as moderate resource areas and areas experiencing moderate rates of rapid change as defined and identified by the California Tax Credit Allocation Committee (TCAC).

Module: Module is defined as each of a set of parts or independent units that can be used to construct, or as a construct for, a more complex system. See [Sec. 14.2.10.A.2. (Ground Story Modules)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10). See [Sec. 2C.4.3. (Height in Stories)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.3). See Sec. 14.2.9.D. (Building Module Method).

Monument: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), monument is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated as a City [Historic-Cultural Monument](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Monument Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.6. (Monument Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), monument sign is defined as a freestanding [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is wholly independent of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for support, erected directly upon the original [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or that is raised no more than 12 inches from the [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to the bottom of the [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Motor Vehicle: Motor vehicle is the same as defined in the [Code of Federal Regulations, Title 40., Sec. 85.1703. (Definition of Motor Vehicle)](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-85/subpart-R/section-85.1703).

Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.3. (Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.3), motor vehicle sales & rental is defined as any [heavy commercial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that sells, rents, or leases [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Household Moving Truck Rental: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.3.C. (Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Household Moving Truck Rental)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.3), motor vehicle sales & rental: household moving truck rental is defined as any motor vehicle sales & rental [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the rental of household moving rental trucks or utility trailers. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the outdoor storage of vehicles that do not comprise an establishment's rental inventory, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see, [Sec. 5D.7.5.C. (Storage, Outdoor: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Large Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.3.B. (Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.3), motor vehicle sales & rental: large vehicle is defined as any motor vehicle sales & rental [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving indoor or outdoor display of three or more new or used large vehicles for sale, rental, or lease. Large vehicles include [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s possessing three or more axles, such as trailer trucks, construction vehicles, motor homes, and [recreational vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, in addition to recreational boats and watercraft. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the outdoor storage of [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that do not comprise an establishment's sale or rental inventory, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see, [Sec. 5D.7.5.C. (Storage, Outdoor: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Standard Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.3.A. (Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental: Standard Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.3), motor vehicle sales & rental: standard vehicle is defined as any motor vehicle sales & rental [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving indoor or outdoor display of three or more new or used standard vehicles for sale, rental, or lease. Standard vehicles include [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s possessing two or fewer axles, such as cars, motorcycles, sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks, and vans. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the outdoor storage of [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that do not comprise an establishment's sale or rental inventory, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see, [Sec. 5D.7.5.B. (Storage, Outdoor: Standard Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

Motor Vehicle Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.1. (Motor Vehicle Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), motor vehicle services are defined as a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the diagnosing of malfunctions, repair, or maintenance of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Motor Vehicle Services: Car Wash: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.1.D. (Motor Vehicle Services: Car Wash)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), motor vehicle services: car wash is defined as any [motor vehicle services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) engaged in cleaning, washing, or waxing of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, such as passenger cars, trucks, vans, and trailers. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include wash facilities for large vehicles, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.1.C. (Motor Vehicle Services: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1).

Motor Vehicle Services: Heavy: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.1.B. (Motor Vehicle Services: Heavy)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), motor vehicle services: heavy is defined as any [motor vehicle services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving auto body repair or rebuilding, painting, or servicing of standard [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes the repair or rebuilding of a vehicle’s frame, roof, doors, fenders, bumpers, hood, trunk, automobile painting, and electric vehicle battery reconditioning and replacement.

Motor Vehicle Services: Large Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.1.C. (Motor Vehicle Services: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), motor vehicle services: large vehicle is defined as any [motor vehicle services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) performed for large vehicles, classified for this purpose as a vehicle having three or more axles, such as trailer trucks, construction vehicles, motor homes, and recreation vehicles.

Motor Vehicle Services: Light: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.1.A. (Motor Vehicle Services: Light)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), motor vehicle services: light is defined as any [motor vehicle services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the mechanical or electrical repair, diagnosis, maintenance or servicing of standard [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes automotive emissions testing; electrical diagnostic, battery testing, and charging; tire removal, replacement, and repair; mechanical adjustment; oil change; lubrication; sound system or alarm service and installation; and window repair. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s defined in the following Sections: [Sec. 5D.7.1.B. (Motor Vehicle Services: Heavy)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), [Sec. 5D.7.1.C. (Motor Vehicle Services: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1), or [Sec. 5D.7.1.D. (Motor Vehicle Services: Car Wash)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1).

Motor Vehicle Use Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.2.2. (Motor Vehicle Use Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.2), motor vehicle use area is defined as portions of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed and intended for use by [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, including areas to be used by [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s for circulation, maneuvering, loading, staging, queuing, service areas and areas to be used for the sale or storage of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Movable Tiny House: See [Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning), Sec. 12.03. (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lapz/0-0-0-886) of this Code.

Multi-Story Building: Multi-story building is defined as a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with one or more [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) constructed above the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

### N

Native Plant: Native plant is defined as any plant species listed on [Calscape](https://calscape.org/) as occurring in the South Coast region.

Natural Feature: For the purposes of Div 13B.8. (Historic Preservation), natural feature is defined as any [significant tree](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), plant life, geographical or geological feature identified individually or collectively on the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as contributing to the cultural or [historic](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) significance of the [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Nature Reserve: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.3. (Nature Reserve)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.3), nature reserve is defined as an area managed so as to protect its flora, fauna, and physical features. Nature reserve includes ecological preserve, marine preserve, natural resource preserve, and water conservation area.

New Construction: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.1. (New Construction)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), new construction is defined as work that includes the construction of a new [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), whether structurally detached or attached from other existing [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s on the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). New construction includes an addition to or relocation of an [existing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or the relocation of existing [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), to another location on the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or to any other [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Relocation of [existing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s includes any activity that lifts any portion of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) off of its foundation. New construction does not include ground mounted [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) mounted [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Non-Contributing Element: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), non-contributing element is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that is identified in the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as a non-contributing element, or not listed in the [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Non-Contributor: Non-contributor is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is identified as a non-contributor in an [historic resources survey](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or an official nomination form accepted by the relevant agency for a designated federal, state, or local historic district, including [non-contributing element](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s in a [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or is a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or landscape feature included in a district boundary with no identification.

Non-Solid Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.4.A.5.
