(Non-Solid Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.4), non-solid area is defined as the portions of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s along the perimeter of a space that have no permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or component obstructing the space from its surroundings. For the purpose of measuring the [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a space, portions of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) are considered non-solid area where no permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or component is located within five feet of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), measured perpendicular to the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and away from the subject space.

Non-Urbanized Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 8.2.4.B.2.a. (Non-Urbanized Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.4), non-urbanized area is defined as all those portions of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) has determined will not be detrimentally affected by the drilling, maintenance, or operation of [oil, gas, or hydrocarbon well](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. In making its determination, the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on appeal, shall give due consideration to the amount of land subdivided, the physical improvements, the density of population, and the zoning of the district.

Nonconforming: See [nonconforming lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [nonconforming structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [nonconforming use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [nonconforming sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [nonconforming yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Nonconforming Building: See [nonconforming structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Nonconforming Lot: Nonconforming lot is defined as a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conformed to the zoning regulations, if any, at the time it was established, but does not conform to current requirements of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A). See [Sec. 12.8.2. (Lot Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12#12.8.2).

Nonconforming Sign: Nonconforming sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conformed to the zoning regulations, if any, at the time it was established, but does not conform to current requirements of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A). See [Sec. 12.4.2. (Sign Exceptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12#12.4.2).

Nonconforming Structure: Nonconforming structure is defined as a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conformed to the regulations, if any, at the time it was established, but does not conform to current requirements of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A). See Div. 12.1. (General Nonconforming Provisions).

Nonconforming Use: Nonconforming use is defined as a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conformed to the zoning regulations, if any, at the time it was established, but does not conform to current requirements of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A). See [Div. 12.5.1. (Use Exceptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12#12.5.1).

Nonconforming Yard: Nonconforming yard is defined as an existing [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conformed to the zoning regulations, if any, at the time it was established, but does not conform to current requirements of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A). See [Div. 12.1. (General Nonconforming Provisions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12#12.1).

Non-Residential Use: Non-residential use is defined as any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) not listed and defined in [Div. 5D.2. (Residential Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2). Non-residential use includes [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s listed and defined in [Div. 5D.3. (Public & Institutional Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3), [Div. 5D.4. (Open Space & Recreation Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4), [Div. 5D.5. (Transportation Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5), [Div. 5D.6. (General Commercial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6), [Div. 5D.7. (Heavy Commercial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7), [Div. 5D.8. (Light Industrial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8), [Div. 5D.9. (Heavy Industrial Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9), and [Div. 5D.10. (Agricultural Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.10).

### O

Occupiable: See [occupiable space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Occupiable Space: Occupiable space is defined as any area designed and intended for human occupancy with a minimum [clear height](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of seven feet.

Off-Site Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.3. (Off-Site Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.3), off-site sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that displays any message directing attention to a business, product, service, profession, commodity, activity, event, [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), institution, or any other commercial message, which is generally conducted, sold, manufactured, produced, offered or occurs elsewhere than on the premises where the [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is located.

Office: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.9. (Office)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.9), office is defined as any workspace accommodating administrative, creative and business services. Office [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s may be operated independently or combined with other [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, provided each of the other [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s is permitted and meets the applicable standards. An office [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes workspace accommodating the following activities: administrative, clerical, legal, accounting, design, consulting, graphics and sound editing, and dry lab research.

Oil Drilling District (O): An oil drilling district established pursuant to [Sec. 8.2.4. (Oil Drilling Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.4).

Oil Well Class I or A: Oil well class I or A is defined as any well associated with an [oil, gas, or hydrocarbon well](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) drilled, conditioned arranged, used or intended to be used for the production of petroleum.

Oil Well Class II or B: Oil well class II or B is defined as any well associated with an [oil, gas, or hydrocarbon well](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) drilled, conditioned, arranged, used or intended to be used only for the subsurface injection into the earth of oil field waste, gases, water or liquid substances.

Oil, Gas, or Hydrocarbon Well: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.7. (Oil, Gas, or Hydrocarbon Well)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.7), oil, gas, or hydrocarbon wells are defined as any well or hole already drilled, being drilled or to be drilled into the surface of the earth which is used or intended to be used in connection with coring or the drilling for prospecting for or producing petroleum, natural gas or other hydrocarbon substances, or is used or intended to be used for the subsurface injection into the earth of oil field waste, gases, water or liquid substances, including any such existing hole, well or casing which has not been abandoned in accordance with the requirements of [Chapter V. (Public Safety and Protection), Sec. 57.5706.3.16. (Abandonment of Oil Wells)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-351526) and the mitigation monitoring program and well plugging and abandonment mitigation measures adopted with [Ordinance No. 187,709 (Oil and Gas Drilling Ordinance)](https://clkrep.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2017/17-0447-S2_ord_187709_1-18-23.pdf). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include any well operated by a public utility regulated by the California Public Utilities Commission.

On-Site Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.4. (On-Site Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.4), on-site sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is other than an [off-site sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

One Hundred Percent Affordable Housing Project: A one hundred percent affordable housing project is a [housing development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as specified in California Government Code Sec. 65589.5; involves the construction of, addition to, or remodeling of any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that would result in the creation of five or more additional [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s; reserves all new [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, renovated [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s retrofitted for accessibility, exclusive of any [manager unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or staff units for [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s utilizing California Government Code Sec. 65913.16, as [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, including bonus units; and restricts all units, including bonus units, for [lower income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, except that up to twenty percent may be for [moderate income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Opacity: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.13. (Opacity (%))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.13), opacity is defined as the degree to which an object or material is impervious to rays of light or obstructs visibility.

Open Space & Recreation Use: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4. (Open Space & Recreation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4), open space & recreational uses are defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that provide opportunities for recreation, sport, and the enjoyment of open space and nature.

Open Space, Public: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.4. (Open Space, Public)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.4), open space, public is defined as [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), outdoor areas for passive recreation, which include spaces such as parks, plazas, walking trails, lawns, and picnic benches.

Open to the Sky: Open to the sky is defined as having no intervening [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) between the finished floor or [ground surface](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and the sky.

Opposing Lot Line: Opposing lot line is defined as [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that do not intersect at any point. Determinations as to whether irregular lot lines are opposing shall be made in accordance with [Sec. 14.2.14. (Irregular Lot Lines)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.14).

Original Art Mural: Original art mural is defined as a one-of-a-kind, hand-painted, hand-tiled, or digitally printed image on the [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that does not contain any [commercial message](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Outdoor Dining: Outdoor dining is defined as any [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [uncovered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) portion of an eating and drinking establishment which is [unenclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and which is used primarily for the consumption of food or drinks by the patrons of the eating and drinking establishment. Includes [outdoor dining area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that are on or above the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Does not include rooftop dining.

Outdoor Dining Area: Outdoor dining area is defined as any portion of any eating & drinking [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on private property designed and intended for the service and consumption of food and drinks, that has less than 75 percent [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) (regardless of [covered area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) percentage), or less than 25 percent [covered area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) (regardless of [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) percentage).

Outdoor Display: Outdoor display is defined as any exhibition of goods for [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) sale which are outdoors.

Outdoor Furniture: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.n. (Outdoor Furniture)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), outdoor furniture is defined as permanent or movable furniture not located within an [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) space. Examples of outdoor furniture may include, but are not limited to: benches, tables, or bike or scooter parking racks.

Outdoor Recreation: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.5. (Outdoor Recreation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.5), outdoor recreation is defined as any outdoor [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) providing sports, fitness, leisure, amusement, or recreation facilities. Outdoor recreation includes the following [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s when outdoors: sports courts and fields, aquatic centers, skate parks, play facilities, and amusement rides.

Outdoor Recreation: Commercial: Pursuant to Sec. 5D.4.5.B. (Outdoor Recreation: Commercial), outdoor recreation: commercial is defined as any outdoor recreational [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) owned or operated by a private or commercial entity. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include associated spectator facilities with seating capacity greater than 500 seats, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.4.1. (Amphitheater or Stadium)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.1).

Outdoor Recreation: Golf Course: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.5.C. (Outdoor Recreation: Golf Course)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.5), outdoor recreation: golf course is defined as an area of land designed and intended for the game of golf with a series of holes each including tee, fairway, and putting green, and often one or more natural or artificial hazards. A outdoor recreation: golf course [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes any course having a total par of 65, or greater. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) also includes a clubhouse incidental to a standard-sized golf course. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include miniature golf, pitch & putt, driving range, or 3-par courses, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.4.5.A. (Outdoor Recreation: Public)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.5) or [Sec. 5D.4.5.B. (Outdoor Recreation: Commercial)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.5).

Outdoor Recreation: Public: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.4.5.A. (Outdoor Recreation: Public)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.5), outdoor recreation: public is defined as any outdoor recreational [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) owned or operated by or in partnership with a public institution.

Outdoor Storage Screening: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.8.3. (Outdoor Storage Screening)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.8.3), outdoor storage screening is defined as [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s surrounding outdoor storage areas in which goods, material, and equipment, new or used, are held outside of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for future use.

Owner: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), owner is defined as any [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), association, partnership, firm, corporation or public entity identified as the holder of title on any property as shown on the records of the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or on the last assessment roll of the County of Los Angeles, as applicable. For purposes of this Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation), “owner” also refers to an appointed representative of an association, partnership, firm, corporation, or public entity which is a recorded owner.

### P

Parallel Parking: For purposes of on-site parking, parallel parking is defined as a [parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) having its length parallel to its [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Parcel: Parcel is defined as a piece of land with defined boundaries intended for the purpose of ownership, lease, or finance.

Parcel Map: Parcel map is defined as a map for the division of land meeting the requirements of [Sec. 11.4.5. (Parcel Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.4.5).

Park Fee: Park fee is defined as Quimby in-lieu fees and park mitigation fees pursuant to [Sec. 10.4.2. (Types of Fees)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10#10.4.2).

Park Trailer: Park trailer is the same as defined in [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 18009.3](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=18009.3.).

Parking: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.6. (Parking)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.6), parking is defined as a facility intended for the temporary storage of operable [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s belonging to a site's occupants, employees, or visitors and is designed to meet the standards of [Sec. 4C.4.4. (Parking Area Design)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.4). Includes [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and surface [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include long term [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) storage, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.5. (Storage, Outdoor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

Parking Area: Parking area is defined as a [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is used for parking [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Examples include, [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Parking Bay: For a double-loaded aisle, parking bay is defined as the width of two rows of [parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s including the width of the [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in-between. For a single-loaded aisle, parking bay is defined as the width of a single row of [parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s including the width of the [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Parking Garage: Parking garage is defined as any [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is primarily used for [parking](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For a [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to be considered a parking garage, [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall be greater than or equal to the [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Sec. 4C.4.6. (Parking Structure Design)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.6).

Parking Lot: Parking lot is defined as a [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that has no [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) below or above it.

Parking Setback: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.2.1. (Parking Setback)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.2.1), parking setback is defined as an area on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) along a [frontage lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are prohibited, including [primary street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) parking setbacks, side street parking setbacks, and [special lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) parking setbacks.

Parking Stall: See [automobile parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Parking Structure: Parking structure is defined as a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes [parking](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Parking structure includes [parking garage](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [integrated parking](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. See [Sec. 4C.4.6. (Parking Structure Design)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.4.6).

Parkway: Parkway is defined as the area between the edge of the [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and the [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) property line excluding any area occupied by a sidewalk. Parkway shall also include any area within a [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is not open to vehicular travel.

Passenger Loading Area: Passenger loading area is defined as areas designated for the on-site or curbside loading and unloading of passenger [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Passenger Transit Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.5.5. (Passenger Transit Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.5), a passenger transit facility is defined as any facility that includes a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) accommodating [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) passenger transport [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s which regularly load and unload passengers along a fixed route. A passenger transit facility include bus terminals, light rail stations and right-of-ways, subway stations and right-of-ways, and passenger train stations and right-of-ways.

Pedestrian Access: Pedestrian access is defined as a means of approaching or entering a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as a pedestrian in accordance with [Div. 4C.1. (Pedestrian Access)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.1).

Pedestrian Access Package: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.1.1.C.1. (Pedestrian Access Packages)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.1.1), pedestrian access package is defined as a combination of standards regulating pedestrian [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from the [public sidewalk](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) into and through a [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Pedestrian Accessway: Pedestrian accessway is defined as a pedestrian path designed to accommodate pedestrian [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) into a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and to one or more [building entrance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, in accordance with [Div. 4C.1. (Pedestrian Access)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.1).

Pedestrian Amenity & Public Amenity-Facing Facade: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.6.C. (Pedestrian Amenity & Public Amenity-Facing Facade)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.6), pedestrian amenity & public amenity-facing facade is defined as the portions of any frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.C.2. (Frontage Applicable Facade)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2) having no permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) (not including [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s) located between the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and a [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [public amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Pedestrian Amenity Allowance: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.1.4. (Pedestrian Amenity Allowance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.1.4), pedestrian amenity allowance is defined as the width of [pedestrian amenity space](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the [build-to zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that can be counted toward the [build-to width](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) requirement.

Pedestrian Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.2. (Pedestrian Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3), pedestrian amenity space is defined as a type of amenity space that is outdoors, located at ground-level, is accessible to pedestrians and all tenants of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and meets all the standards in [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.2. (Pedestrian Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3). See [Div. 3C.1. (Build-To)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.1) for additional provisions related to pedestrian amenity spaces.

Pedestrian Amenity-Facing Facade: See pedestrian amenity & public amenity-facing facade.

Pedestrian Passageway: Pedestrian passageway is defined as a [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) pedestrian pathway that provides pedestrian through [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from the [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) into and directly through a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), in accordance with [Sec. 4C.1.1.C.3.a. (Pedestrian Passageway)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.1.1).

Pedestrian Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.7. (Pedestrian Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), pedestrian sign is defined as a small [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) attached perpendicular to the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that hangs from a bracket or support.

Pedestrian Walkway: Pedestrian walkway is defined as any [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated as a pedestrian walkway on the Citywide General Plan Circulation System maps of the [Circulation Element](https://planning.lacity.gov/odocument/523f2a95-9d72-41d7-aba5-1972f84c1d36/Mobility_Plan_2035.pdf) of the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Perennial: Perennial is defined as a plant that lives more than two years, including woody species and other plants that do not die back annually.

Perimeter Plane: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.4.A.3. (Perimeter Plane)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.4), perimeter plane is defined as an imaginary vertical plane along the perimeter of a space used to measure the [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a space. A perimeter plane shall be projected for a height of eight feet measured from the floor or [ground surface](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the space.

Permanent Supportive Housing: Permanent supportive housing is defined by [Div. 10. (Contracts), Article 25. (Permanent Supportive Housing and Facilities Infrastructure Stabilization Ordinance), Sec. 10 51.1.(j). (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-90691) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Permission Level: A permission level is a letter or symbol provided within a [Use District table](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to indicate how an individual [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is permitted, as established in [Div. 5A.3. (Use Permissions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5A.3).

Permit: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.1. (Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.1), permit is defined as any license, certificate, approval, or other entitlement for use granted, conditionally granted, or denied by any public agency, which is subject to the provisions of [Sec. 13B.9.1. (Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.1).

Perpendicular Line: For the purposes of [Sec. 4C.11.3.D.1. (Lots with Multiple Street Frontages)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.3), perpendicular line is defined as, a straight line between the point on a [sign face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is closest to the street and the point where the line intersects the [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at a 90 degree angle, as illustrated in [Sec. 4C.11.3.D.1. (Lots with Multiple Street Frontages)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.3).

Person: For the purposes of the [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), person shall have the same meaning as that term is defined in [Chapter II. (Licenses, Permits, Business Regulations), Sec. 21.7.2. (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-126755) of this Code. As the term is used in the remainder of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) person means, an individual, joint venture, joint stock company, partnership, association, club, company, corporation, business trust, or organization and any other legal or natural person, or the manager, lessee, agent, servant, officer, or employee of any of them.

Personal Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.10. (Personal Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.10), personal services are defined as any commercial [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) providing an in-person service directly to individuals seeking cosmetic services, counseling services, document services, or servicing of consumer goods. Personal services include: cosmetic services such as hair cutting and styling, nail salon, day spas, licensed massage therapy, tattooing and piercing; counseling services, such as non-medical counseling, legal counseling, financial counseling, psychic counseling; document services such as printing, form and application assistance, notary services, photo developing, visa and passport services; garment services, such as garment tailoring and alterations, laundromat, dry cleaning; and consumer goods repair services when occupying less than 3,000 square feet in area, such as electronics repair, jewelry repair, shoe repair, appliance repair, furniture restoration, and bicycle repair. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include consumer goods repair services when occupying 3,000 square feet in area, or greater, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.8.1. (Machine Shop)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.1). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include maintenance and repair of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.1. (Motor Vehicle Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.1).

Plant Cultivation: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.10.2. (Plant Cultivation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.10.2), plant cultivation is defined as any [agricultural use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes the growing of plants.

Plant Cultivation: Community Garden: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.10.2.A. (Plant Cultivation: Community Garden)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.10.2), plant cultivation: community garden is defined as a [plant cultivation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designed and intended for multiple [household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or organizations to cultivate plants for domestic use. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) may include shared facilities for storage and maintenance or services incidental to the [agricultural use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) such as an educational space.

Plant Cultivation: Farming: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.10.2.B. (Plant Cultivation: Farming)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.10.2), plant cultivation: farming is defined as the cultivation of produce, ornamental plants, herbs, seeds, or fungi, for off-site sale or distribution. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes, but is not limited to, truck gardening, indoor farming, or vertical farming. For the sale of produce on-site beyond a farm stand pursuant to [Sec. 5C.2.8.G.1. (Supplemental Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.2.8), see [Sec. 5D.6.12.E. (Retail: Food & Beverage)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12).

Planting Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.6.4.C.2. (Planting Areas)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.6.4), planting area is defined as an area on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) designated and designed for plants.

Planting Hole: Planting hole is defined as a hollow space dug within a [planting area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to accommodate the placement of a plant.

Platform Agreement: For the purposes of [Sec. 5C.3.2. (Home-Sharing Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), platform agreement is defined as a signed agreement between a [hosting platform](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), which, among other things, provides that the platform will collect and submit the [Transient](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) Occupancy Tax to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on behalf of [host](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s listed for [short-term rental](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Pole Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.8. (Pole Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), pole sign is defined as a freestanding [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is wholly independent of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for support, permanently affixed to the ground using one or more poles or posts.

Postmortem Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.11. (Postmortem Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.11), postmortem services are defined as any establishment engaged in the provision of services involving the care, preparation, or arrangement of human or animal remains, and conducting memorial services. Postmortem service establishments include crematoriums, funeral homes, mortuaries, and pet crematoriums. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include a [cemetery](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.1. (Cemetery)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.1).

Preliminary Parcel Map: Preliminary parcel map is defined as a map made for the purpose of showing the design of a proposed [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) creating four or fewer [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, four or fewer [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or four or fewer units in a [community apartment project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and prepared pursuant to [Sec. 11.4.2. (Preliminary Parcel Map Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.4.2).

Prepare: Whenever this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) directs an agency or official to prepare a document, prepare means prepare directly or cause to be prepared.

Primary Residence: For the purposes of the [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), primary residence is defined as the sole residence from which the [host](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) conducts home-sharing and in which the [host](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) resides for more than six months of the calendar year. For all other purposes in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A), primary residence is defined as a place of residence for an individual or group of individuals to live for more than six months out of the year.

Primary Roof Form: Primary roof form is defined as the form of the roof which covers at least 80 percent of the [building footprint](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Primary Street: See [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Primary Street Lot Line: Primary street lot line is defined as a [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that has been designated as the primary street lot line per [Sec. 14.2.12.C.1. (Primary Street Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12).

Primary Use: For the purposes of [Article 5. (Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5), primary use is defined as the principal or predominant [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) relative to any other [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s sharing the same [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as determined by the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that occupies the most [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that covers the most [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) when concerning outdoor [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Principal Material Coverage: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.10.1. (Principal Material Coverage)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.10.1), principal material coverage is defined as the building products used as the primary [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) finish materials of the exterior [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Principal Structure: Principal structure is defined as any [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is not an [accessory structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Private Club: Private club is defined as any facility organized solely for the promotion of some common interest and which is accessible to club members and their guests only. Private club includes business, fraternal, political, and social organizations.

Private Outdoor Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.4. (Private Outdoor Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3), private outdoor amenity space is defined as a type of amenity space that is [uncovered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [unenclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and is available to an assigned unit or tenant space, and meets all the standards in [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.4. (Private Outdoor Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3).

Private Road Easement: Private road easement is defined as a [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land not dedicated as a public street, over which a private [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for road purposes is proposed to be, or has been, granted to the owners of property contiguous or [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to the road, that intersects or connects with a public street or a [private street](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). The instrument creating such [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall be, or shall have been, duly recorded with the Los Angeles County Recorder.

Private Street: Private street is defined as a [private road easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as defined herein which has been determined by the [Advisory Agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to be adequate for [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and for the purposes set forth in [Article 10. (Streets & Parks)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/10), or [Article 11. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11) of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A).

Problem Areas: Problem areas are defined as those portions of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) determined by resolution of the Board of Public Works to be actually or potentially dangerous by reason of geological conditions, being subject to inundation or overflow by storm water, or because of any other potentially dangerous condition, including areas subject to rapid spread of fire.

Producing Zone (Oil Drilling Districts): Producing zone (Oil Drilling Districts) is defined as a reservoir or series of reservoirs of sufficient thickness and productivity of hydrocarbons as to form an economic source of supply and which is segregated from other reservoirs, or series of reservoirs, by natural boundaries or barriers to such an extent as to make its separate development either economically or mechanically desirable in accordance with good oil field practice.

Project: As the term is used in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) project is defined by [Sec. 14.2.15.A. (Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15). The definition for project is modified for the purposes of the following Sections:

1\. For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.11.1. (Environmental Review Procedures)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.11.1), project is defined by the [California Public Resources Code, Sec. 21065.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=21065.&lawCode=PRC) and [CEQA Guideline](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [Sec. 15378](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I8E24AB655B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3?viewType=FullText&listSource=Search&originationContext=Search+Result&transitionType=SearchItem&contextData=(sc.Search)&navigationPath=Search%2fv1%2fresults%2fnavigation%2fi0a89c5da00000193f999e4bde12f316b%3fppcid%3d3ee7674b3ce74e7e9e0ce5b16265e88e%26Nav%3dREGULATION_PUBLICVIEW%26fragmentIdentifier%3dI8E24AB655B4D11EC976B000D3A7C4BC3%26startIndex%3d1%26transitionType%3dSearchItem%26contextData%3d%2528sc.Default%2529%26originationContext%3dSearch%2520Result&list=REGULATION_PUBLICVIEW&rank=2&t_T2=15378&t_S1=CA+ADC+s).

2\. For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), see [Sec. 13B.8.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8.1) or [Sec. 8.2.6.B.1. (Definition of Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.6).

3\. For the purposes of [Sec. 8.2.2. (Community Plan Implementation Overlay (CPIO))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.2) see [Sec. 8.2.2.B.1. (Definition of Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.2).

4\. For the purposes of [Sec. 8.2.3. (Sign District (SN))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.3) see [Sec. 8.2.3.B.1. (Definition of Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.3).

5\. For the purposes of [Sec. 8.2.5. (Community Design Overlay (CDO))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.5) see [Sec. 8.2.5.B.1. (Definition of Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.5).

6\. For the purposes of [Sec. 8.2.7. (Conservation Districts (CD))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.7) see [Sec. 8.2.7.B.1. (Definition of Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.7).

7\. For the purposes of [Sec. 8.2.8. (Transportation Communication Network District (TCN))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.8) see [Sec. 8.2.8.B.1. (Definition of Project)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.8).

Project Activities: See [project activity](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Project Activity: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15. (Project Activities)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), project activity is defined as the type of work composing a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). A [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) may be composed of one or more project activity.

Project Adjustment: For the purposes of review of a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for compliance with a [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), project adjustment is defined as a decision on a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granting a minor adjustment from certain [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) regulations, subject to the limitations specified by [Div.13B.4. (Specific Plan Implementation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.4).

Project Compliance: For the purposes of review of a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for compliance with a [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), project compliance is defined as a decision by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) complies with the regulations of the applicable [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), either as submitted, or with conditions imposed to achieve compliance.

Project Exception: For the purposes of review of a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for compliance with a [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), project exception is defined as a decision on a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by the [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granting relief from applicable [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) regulations.

Project Site: Project site is defined as the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on which a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is located.

Projecting Balcony: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.7.1.D. (Projecting Balcony)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.7.1), projecting balcony is defined as an [unenclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [occupiable](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) platform, located at an [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) above the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that is fixed to or integrated with an exterior [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and projects beyond the [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) immediately below. Balconies include protective barriers such as railings or parapets and may be [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [uncovered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Projecting Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.9. (Projecting Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), projecting sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) attached approximately perpendicular to the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that does not meet the standards for a [pedestrian sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Projection: For the purposes of [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, projection is defined as the [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by which a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) extends beyond the [building face](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Div. 4C.11. (Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11).

Proposed Use: For the purposes of [Article 5. (Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5), proposed use is defined as any [project activity](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the establishment of a new [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), the modification of an existing [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), expansion of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) dedicated to an existing [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or relocation of an existing [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Protected Unit: A protected unit includes a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that meets any of the following criteria:

1\. A [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is or was subject to a recorded covenant, ordinance, or law that restricts rents to levels affordable to [lower income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [very low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s within the past five years,

2\. A [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is or was subject to the Rent Stabilization Ordinance, pursuant to Chapter XV. (Rent Stabilization Ordinance) of this Code, or any other form of rent or price control through a public entity’s valid exercise of its police power within the past five years;

3\. A [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is or was rented by a [lower income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or very low income households within the past five years,

4\. A [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that was withdrawn from rent or lease in accordance with the Ellis Act, pursuant to California Government Code, Chapter 12.75 (Residential Real Property), Sec. 7060-7060.7, within the past 10 years.

Protected Vegetation: Protected vegetation is defined as any protected tree or [shrub](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as defined in [Chapter IV. (Public Welfare), Sec. 46.01. (Definition)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-132260) of this Code.

Protective Barrier: Protective barrier is defined as a building component or assembly located at, or near, the open sides of elevated floor surfaces, that is designed to reduce the risk of fall from the [occupiable](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) space. Protective barrier includes guardrails, railings, and parapets.

Public & Institutional Use: Pursuant to [Div. 5D.3. (Public & Institutional Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3), public & institutional uses are defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s dedicated to serving the public through the provision of government services, utilities, healthcare, education, and culture.

Public Access Easement: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.17. (Public Access Easements)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.17), public access easement is an [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), established between a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) owner or owners and the City of Los Angeles, as found on the [Public Access Easement Map (Sec. 1.5.11.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.5.11), affecting a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s for the purpose of ensuring public [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to the portions of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) covered by the [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Public Agency: Public Agency is defined pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 20056.

Public Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.3. (Public Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3), public amenity space is defined as a type of amenity space that is outdoors and, although privately owned, is open to the public, and meets all the standards in [Sec. 2C.3.3.C.3. (Public Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.3).

Public Amenity-Facing Facade: See pedestrian amenity & public amenity-facing facade.

Public Art Installation: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.1.E.3.d. (Public Art Installation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.1), public art installation is defined as a facility, amenity or [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that does not contain any [commercial message](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and which is either an "approved public arts project" as defined by [Sec. 19.85.4. (Direct Expenditure on Approved Public Arts Projects)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-44991) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or approved pursuant to [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Sec. 91.107.4.6. (Arts Development Fee)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-172789) of this Code.

Public Facility: Public facility is defined as any facility, including, but not limited to, [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, property, recreation areas, and roads, which are owned, leased, or otherwise operated, or funded by a governmental body or public entity. See [Sec. 9.3.4.C.7. (Civic Facility Incentive Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3.4).

Public Land Project: A public land project is defined as a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) containing [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s located on [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s owned by a [public agency](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Public Project: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.9. (Coastal Development)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9), public project is defined as any development initiated by the Department of Public Works or any of its bureaus, any development initiated by any other department or agency of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and any development initiated or to be carried out by any other governmental agency which is required to obtain a local government permit. Public project shall not include any development by any department or agency of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or any other governmental entity which otherwise requires action by or approval of the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [Area Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or the Office of Zoning Administration, or any development by any department or agency of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or any other government entity for which a permit from the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is required. Public project shall also not include any development on tidelands, submerged lands, or on public trust lands, whether filled or unfilled. (Definition Amended by Ord. No. 173,268, eff. 7/1/00, Oper. 7/1/00.).

Public Right-of-Way: Public right-of-way is defined as the area on, below, or above any surface owned by, or under the control of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the purpose of providing public [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for a mode of transportation or mobility. Public right-of-way includes [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), median, sidewalk, [parkway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), bicycle path, and recreational trail.

Public Safety Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.7. (Public Safety Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.7), public safety facility is defined as any government facility that provides public safety services. Public safety facility includes fire stations and police stations.

Public Sidewalk: Public sidewalk is defined as any sidewalk within a [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Public Way: Public way is defined as a street, [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or other [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land leading to a street or [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that has been deeded, dedicated, or otherwise permanently appropriated to the public, for public use, that has a clear width and height of not less than 10 feet. Public way includes any street, channel, viaduct, subway, tunnel, bridge, [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or other way, in which a public agency or the public has a right of use.

Publicly Accessible: Publicly accessible is defined as the ability of the public to [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) a facility.

### Q

Qualified Developer: Qualified developer is defined pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 65913.16(b)(9)(A-C) exclusive of (D), and shall also include a Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) identified on the United States Department of the Treasury’s CDFI Fund list of Certified CDFIs at the time of [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) filing, provided the CDFI maintains a non-profit status pursuant to United States Internal Revenue Code Sec. 501(c)(3).

Qualified Nonprofit Housing Corporation: Qualified nonprofit housing corporation is defined pursuant to [Sec. 501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code](https://www.irs.gov/privacy-disclosure/tax-code-regulations-and-official-guidance) that has received a welfare exemption under [Sec. 214.15 of the Revenue and Taxation Code](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=214.15&lawCode=RTC#:) for properties intended to be sold to low-income families who participate in a special no-interest loan program.

Qualified Permanent Supportive Housing Project: Qualified permanent supportive housing project is defined as a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where all [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s meet the standards of [Sec. 9.4.1. (Permanent Supportive Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.1).

Quasi-Judicial Approval: Quasi-judicial approval is defined as an action that applies rules to specific facts and is subject to procedural due process principles and includes but is not limited to the approvals provided for in [Div. 13B.2. (Quasi-Judicial Review)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.2), [Div. 13B.4. (Specific Plan Implementation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.4), and [Div. 13B.5. (Quasi-Judicial Relief)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5).

Queuing: Queuing is defined as the channeling of [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) traffic into lanes to accommodate the temporary stopping of two or more [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that are waiting to enter into an area or obtain goods or services from a [drive-through facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Queuing Depth: Queuing depth is defined as the portion of a [drive aisle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is designated for ingress vehicular traffic on a [site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and meets the standards of [Sec. 4C.2.1.C.2.b. (Queuing Depth)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.2.1).

Queuing Space: Queuing space is defined as the space within a [drive-through lane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) needed to accommodate the temporary stopping of a single [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

### R

Rear Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.C.4. (Rear Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), rear lot line is defined as a [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that does not abut a street or [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and is opposite and most distant from a [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and meets the criteria pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.C.4. (Rear Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12).

Rear Yard: See [Sec. 14.2.16.B.4. (Rear Yard)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.16).

Reasonable Accommodation: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.5.5. (Reasonable Accommodation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.5), reasonable accommodation is defined as providing an [individual with a disability](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or developers of housing for an [individual with a disability](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), flexibility in the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land use and zoning regulations or policies (including the modification or waiver of certain requirements), when it is necessary to eliminate barriers to housing opportunities.

Reconstruction: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), reconstruction is defined as the act or process of reproducing by [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) the exact form, features and details of a vanished [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), landscape, [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or object as it appeared at a specific period of time, on its original or a substitute [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Recorded Parcel Map: Recorded parcel map is defined as a [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that has been recorded in accordance with [Sec. 11.4.5. (Parcel Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.4.5).

Recreational Vehicle: Recreational vehicle is defined pursuant to [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 18010](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=18010).

Recyclable Materials: Recyclable materials are defined as items or materials to be recycled or reused, including yard waste, paper, plastic, glass, metal, newspaper, and cardboard.

Recycling Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.12.7. (Recycling Areas)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.12.7), recycling area is defined as an outdoor [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or a room within a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is designated for the collection of [recyclable materials](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) generated by the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)(s) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Recycling Center: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.10.3. (Annual Inspection Monitoring (Type 1))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.10.3), recycling center is defined as any recycling collection or buyback site, recycling sorting facility, or other recycling oriented site which does not do any processing other than mechanical compaction to reduce the volume of recyclable containers for economy of storage.

Recycling Chute: Recycling chute is defined as any vertical smooth shaft used to convey [recyclable materials](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from the upper floors of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to a recyclable storage bin or room at the bottom end of the chute.

Recycling Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.4. (Recycling Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.4), recycling facility is defined as any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes the recovery and processing of recyclable or reusable materials.

Recycling Facility: Collection: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.4.A. (Recycling Facility: Collection)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.4), recycling facility: collection is defined as any [recycling facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where [recyclable materials](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) including, but not limited to, paper, plastic, glass, metal, newspaper, or cardboard, are deposited or redeemed for monetary value. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes baling or crushing operations for the purposes of efficient storage and transfer, but shall not include sorting or processing activities other than for temporary storage purposes. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes [reverse vending machine](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and buyback centers.

Recycling Facility: Sorting & Processing: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.4.B. (Recycling Facility: Sorting & Processing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.4), recycling facility: sorting & processing is defined as any [recycling facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that accepts [recyclable materials](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for on-site sorting or processing. For the purpose of this definition, processing shall mean the process of changing the physical characteristics of a recyclable material, including the shredding, smelting, grinding and crushing of cans, bottles, and other materials, other than for temporary storage purposes. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes the transfer and processing of scrap metals.

Recycling Receptacle: Recycling receptacle is defined as a container which is suitable for the collection of [recyclable materials](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Redevelopment Plan Amendment: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, Redevelopment plan amendment is defined as an amendment to a Redevelopment Plan adopted by the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by ordinance after the effective date of Ordinance No. 186,325.

Redevelopment Plan Area: See [redevelopment project area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Redevelopment Plan Project: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, redevelopment plan project is defined as any proposed development activity within a [redevelopment project area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with an [unexpired](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) Redevelopment Plan that includes the issuance of a building, grading, demolition, sign or change of use permit. A redevelopment plan project shall not include activity that consists solely of [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) remodeling, [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) rehabilitation or [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) repair work. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following types of projects shall be considered a redevelopment plan project: (i) development activity involving an [Historic Resource](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including any [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) remodeling, [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) rehabilitation, or [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) repair work that affects the exterior; and/or (ii) development activity involving a [Residential Hotel/Single Room Occupancy Hotel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) (SRO), vacant [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) housing [lower income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s in the City Center Project Area and the Central Industrial Project Area, including any [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) remodeling, [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) rehabilitation or [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) repair work that may result in the loss of a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Redevelopment Plan Project Adjustment: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, redevelopment plan project adjustment is defined as a “minor variation” or “variation” as these terms are used in each Redevelopment Plan and is a decision by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that a [redevelopment plan project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) substantially complies with the relevant [redevelopment regulations](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) except for a minor deviation therefrom, either as submitted or with conditions imposed to achieve substantial compliance with the applicable [redevelopment regulations](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Redevelopment Plan Project Administrative Review: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, redevelopment plan project administrative review is defined as the issuance of a ministerial approval by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for a [redevelopment plan project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that complies with the applicable [redevelopment regulations](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Redevelopment Plan Project Compliance: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, redevelopment plan project compliance is defined as a decision by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that a [redevelopment plan project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) complies with the applicable [redevelopment regulations](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), either as submitted or with conditions imposed to achieve compliance with the [redevelopment regulations](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Redevelopment Project Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, redevelopment project area is defined as the area included within the specific geographic boundaries identified as a project area in a Redevelopment Plan and shall be referred to as “Redevelopment Plan Area.”

Redevelopment Regulations: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, redevelopment regulations are defined as all the land use provisions of the Redevelopment Plans and design for development guidelines adopted pursuant to such Redevelopment Plans that govern land use or development that were transferred to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) pursuant to California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 34173(i).

Registered Civil Engineer: Registered civil engineer is defined as a civil engineer licensed and registered by the State of California.

Rehabilitation: Pursuant to [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), rehabilitation is defined as the act or process of returning a property to a state of utility, through repair or [alteration](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), which makes possible an efficient contemporary use while preserving those portions or features of the property which are significant to its historical, architectural and [cultural](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) values.

Religious Institution: Religious institution is defined pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 65913.16(b)(10).

Renovation: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.9. (Renovation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), renovation is defined as a modification to the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including the [basement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that does not expand the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Renovation includes [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) remodels or tenant improvements.

Rental Unit: For the purposes of [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), rental unit is defined as a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or portion thereof. For all other purposes in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) rental unit is defined as a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) available for rent.

Renter: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), renter is defined as any [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), association, partnership, firm, corporation, or public entity which has rented or leased a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or other [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within an [HPOZ](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for a continuous time period of at least three years. The “renter” also refers to an appointed representative of an association, partnership, firm, corporation, or public entity which is a renter. See [Sec. 13B.8.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8.1).

Replace: Replace is defined as provided in California Government Code Sec. 65915(c)(3)(B) and (C).

Research & Development: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.3. (Research & Development)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.3), research & development is defined as any [light industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) requiring a wet laboratory where chemicals, drugs, or other material or biological matter are handled in liquid solutions or volatile phases, requiring direct ventilation, and specialized piped utilities. Research & development does not include [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s requiring a dry laboratory, for these [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.9. (Office)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.9).

Resident: Resident is defined as one who legally resides at the subject [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Residential: See [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Residential Amenity Space: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.3.2. (Residential Amenity Space)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.3.2), residential amenity space is defined as an area which is designed and intended to be used by occupants of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s for recreational, domestic, or vocational purposes.

Residential Building: Residential building is defined as a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), designed or used for human habitation.

Residential Care Facility for Elderly: Residential care facility for elderly is defined pursuant to [California Code of Regulations, Title 22. (Social Security), Div. 6. (Licensing of Community Care Facilities), Sec. 87101 (r)(5) (Definitions)](https://govt.westlaw.com/calregs/Document/I071CAC8091E611EFABBBCA16E500CAE4?viewType=FullText&listSource=Search&originationContext=Search+Result&transitionType=SearchItem&contextData=(sc.Search)&navigationPath=Search%2fv1%2fresults%2fnavigation%2fi0a89c5da00000194046e49f0e132529c%3fppcid%3d439352f0e0da4338a38e7c269d21c499%26Nav%3dREGULATION_PUBLICVIEW%26fragmentIdentifier%3dI071CAC8091E611EFABBBCA16E500CAE4%26startIndex%3d1%26transitionType%3dSearchItem%26contextData%3d%2528sc.Default%2529%26originationContext%3dSearch%2520Result&list=REGULATION_PUBLICVIEW&rank=1&t_T2=87101&t_S1=CA+ADC+s).

Residential Conversion Project: Residential conversion project is defined as an existing apartment house, apartment hotel, hotel, or multiple dwellings used exclusively for [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) purposes, proposed for conversion to a [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [community apartment project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to be [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) purposes through approval of a [tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For purposes of this definition, the term existing means that the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was constructed prior to 1945 or, where built after 1945, a [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) has been issued for the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) prior to the time of map [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Residential Hotel/Single Room Occupancy Hotel: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, residential hotel/single room occupancy hotel is defined as the meaning ascribed thereto in the Development Guidelines and Controls for Residential Hotels in the City Center and Central Industrial [redevelopment project area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, adopted by the former [CRA](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on June 15, 2006, and/or the Residential Hotel Ordinance (Ordinance No. 179,868) of the City of Los Angeles.

Residential Project: Residential project is defined as a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) containing any number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Residential to Commercial/Industrial Conversion Project: Residential to commercial/industrial conversion project is defined as an existing hotel or multiple dwellings [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) purposes proposed for conversion to a [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which is to be [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d exclusively for commercial or industrial purposes through approval of a [tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). For purposes of this definition, the term existing means that the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was constructed prior to 1945 or, where built after 1945, a [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was issued for the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) prior to the time of map [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Residential Use: A residential use is any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) listed and defined in [Div. 5D.2. (Residential Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2).

Restoration: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.8. (Historic Preservation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), restoration is defined as the act or process of accurately recovering the form, features and details of a property as it appeared at a particular period of time by means of the removal of later work or by the replacement of missing earlier work.

Restaurant: An eating & drinking establishment that provides a dining environment where customers are seated and served made-to-order meals prepared in a full-service kitchen on-site.

Restricted Affordable Unit: Restricted affordable unit is defined as a [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for which rental amounts or mortgage amounts are restricted so as to be affordable to and occupied by an [acutely low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [extremely low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [very low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [moderate income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), as verified by the Los Angeles Housing Department.

Retail: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12. (Retail)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail is defined as a commercial [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involved in the sale or dispensing of consumer goods to the general public, including any associated indoor or outdoor display and point of sales.

Retail: Alcohol: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.B. (Retail: Alcohol)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: alcohol is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the sale or dispensing of alcoholic beverages for off-site consumption and are licensed or seeking a license to sell or otherwise dispense alcoholic beverages for off-site consumption, as defined by the [California State Alcoholic Beverage Control Act (ABC)](https://www.abc.ca.gov/). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the on-site consumption of alcoholic beverages, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.3.B. (Eating & Drinking: Alcohol Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.3).

Retail: Farmers' Market, Certified: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.C.
