(Retail: Farmers' Market, Certified)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: farmers' market, certified is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involved in the sale or dispensing of agricultural products by producers or certified producers directly to consumers or to individuals, organizations, or entities that subsequently sell or distribute the products directly to end users and is certified by the Los Angeles County Agricultural Commissioner.

Retail: Firearms: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.D. (Retail: Firearms)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: firearms is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where firearms, ammunition, or related accessories are sold.

Retail: Food & Beverage: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.E. (Retail: Food & Beverage)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: food & beverage is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) primarily involved in the [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) sale of food and beverages for off-site consumption. Retail: food & beverage includes grocery stores, produce markets, seafood and meat markets, bakeries, delis, and on-site seating areas for dining accessory to the primary [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include alcoholic beverage sales; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.12.B. (Retail: Alcohol)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12).

Retail: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.A. (Retail: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: general is defined as any [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) primarily involved in the sale or rental of new or used consumer goods to the general public. Retail: general includes but is not limited to, the sale or rental of household goods, clothing, books, toys, art supplies, pet supplies, house plants, medicine, consumer electronics, appliances, hardware, building supplies, mattresses, and furniture. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the sale or rental of [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.3. (Motor Vehicle Sales & Rental)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.3).

Retail: Large Format: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.F. (Retail: Large Format)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: large format is defined as any [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with a non-residential tenant size of 100,000 square feet or greater. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) may include but is not limited to any of the following types of [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) when occupying a non-residential tenant size of 100,000 square feet or greater: superstore, department store, wholesale club, furniture store, and home improvement store. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include any [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with a non-residential tenant size of less than 100,000 square feet, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.12.A. (Retail: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12).

Retail: Merchant Market: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.G. (Retail: Merchant Market)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: merchant market is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that includes ten or more tenants or vendors within a shared facility with common entrances and walkways, where goods, products, groceries, and prepared food are offered or displayed for sale or exchange, and may include on-site seating areas for dining as incidental to the market use.

Retail: Pet Shop: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.H. (Pet Shop)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: pet shop is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) possessing a pet shop permit issued by the Department of Animal Services where domestic animals such as dogs, cats, rabbits, rodents, birds, fish, amphibians, and small reptiles are kept and offered for commercial sale, for hire, or adoption. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s where the overnight keeping of dogs or cats exceeds 30 percent of the [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a facility, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.1.B. (Animal Services: Kennel)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.1). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the breeding and raising of animals, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.10.1.G. (Animal Keeping: Small Animals)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.10.1).

Retail: Seasonal Market: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.I. (Seasonal Market)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: seasonal market is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the seasonal outdoor [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) sale of ornamental holiday decor, primarily ornamental pumpkins and Christmas trees.

Retail: Smoke & Vape Shop: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.12.J. (Smoke & Vape Shop)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12), retail: smoke & vape shop is defined as a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) primarily involving the sale of tobacco products, substances intended for smoking, or smoking accessories, including but not limited to cigars, pipes, vaporizing devices, or other smoking paraphernalia. The [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) may include an [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) smokers’ lounge that is solely dedicated to smoking tobacco products. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include medicinal or recreational cannabis establishments, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see the [Department of Cannabis Regulation](https://cannabis.lacity.gov/).

Retaining Wall: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.9.2. (Retaining Walls)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.9.2), retaining wall is defined as a freestanding continuous [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), as viewed from the top, intended to support earth, which is not attached to a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Reverse Vending Machine: Reverse vending machine is defined as an automated mechanical device which accepts one or more types of empty beverage containers including aluminum cans, glass and plastic bottles, and which issues a cash refund or a redeemable credit slip with a value not less than the container’s redemption value, as determined by the State of California. A reverse vending machine may sort and process containers mechanically, provided that the entire process is enclosed within the machine. See [Sec. 5D.9.4.A. (Collection)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.4).

Reviewing Agency: Reviewing agency is defined as the agency or official charged with reviewing an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for an approval under this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) which includes the [Zoning Administrator](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), the Director of Planning, or the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Revised Tentative Tract Map: Revised tentative tract map is defined as a tract map for which a [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) has been previously approved which involves a revised arrangement of the streets, [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s within property or a modification of the boundary of the property pursuant to [Article 11. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11).

Right-of-way: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8) right-of-way is defined as the dedicated area that includes [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, medians, and/or sidewalks. For the remainder of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) see [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Roadway: Roadway is defined as that portion of a [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for a street or [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) used for, or intended to accommodate, the movement of [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, including provided or planned on-street bike lanes.

Roof Form: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.11.1. (Roof Form)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.11.1), roof form is defined as the shape of the external upper covering of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including the frame for supporting the roofing.

Roof Projection: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.b. (Roof Projection)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), roof projections are defined as roof elements that overhang or cantilever beyond the [building footprint](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and do not include posts or columns. Types of roof projections include, but are not limited to: eaves, roof overhangs, gutters, awnings, or canopies.

Roof Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.10. (Roof Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), a roof sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) erected on a roof of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Roof Sign: Open Panel: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.11. (Roof Sign: Open Panel)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), a roof sign: open panel is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) erected on a roof of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) consisting of channel letters, graphic segments, open lighting elements, or other open forms affixed to a non-solid panel [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) support [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Roof Structure: A roof structure is defined as the [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) forming the upper covering of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Roof-Mounted Equipment: Roof-mounted equipment is defined as all [mechanical equipment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [utility equipment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located on a roof, with the exception of solar panels and their required appurtenances. See [Sec. 4C.12.1. (Roof-Mounted Equipment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.12.1).

Roofline Cornice: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.6.5.C.4. (Roofline Cornice)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.6.5), a roofline cornice is defined as a continuous molded projection that crowns a [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), often as part of a parapet.

Rooftop Planting Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.6.4.C.2.b. (Rooftop Planting Area Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.6.4), rooftop planting areas are defined as areas where plants are provided on or over a built [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including but not limited to, a roof, a bridge, a balcony or a [parking structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and complies with all of the standards in [Sec. 4C.6.4.C.2.b. (Rooftop Planting Area Standards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.6.4).

Root Ball: Root ball is defined as the intact ball of earth or growing medium containing the roots of a nursery plant.

Root Collar: A root collar is defined as the line of junction between the root of a plant and its stem or trunk.

Root Flare: A root flare is defined as the area at the base of the plant’s stem or trunk where the stem or trunk broadens to form roots; the area of transition between the root system and the stem or trunk.

Root Mass: Root mass is defined as a plant's overall amount of root growth.

### S

Safety Barrier: For the purposes of [vertical encroachment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.e. (Safety Barriers)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), a safety barrier is defined as a vertical barriers that is 45 inches in height or less and required for safety and protection by [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-172082) of this Code to protect occupants from falling from walking surfaces including but not limited to parapets, railings, or banisters. For the purposes of the remainder of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A), a safety barrier is defined as anything put in place to prevent people from moving easily from one place to another for the purpose of mitigating risk including [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, parapets, and railings.

Sales Floor Area: Sales floor area is defined as the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) devoted to the [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) sale of merchandise where customers can view, select, and carry merchandise from an inventory display to the point of sale. Areas not included in sales floor area include, showrooms, restrooms, [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) space, storage areas, open-air [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) areas.

Salvage Yard: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.3. (Salvage Yard)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.3), a salvage yard is defined as any [heavy industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) having any portion of the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located outdoors where a junk dealer or automobile dismantler operates, or where partially dismantled, obsolete, or wrecked automobiles are stored. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) storage, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.5. (Storage, Outdoor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

School: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.9. (School)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.9), school is defined as an institution of academic learning and social development that provides facilities for teaching and instruction to accommodate a student body such as preschool, K-12, post-secondary education, and associated athletic and recreational facilities. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include avocational, recreational, or other educational or instruction-based [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.6. (Instructional Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.6). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include a campus auditorium or stadium facilities with a seating capacity greater than 3,000 seats, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.4.1. (Amphitheater or Stadium)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.4.1).

School: K-12: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.9.B. (School: K-12)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.9), school: K-12 is defined as an institution of learning which offers instruction in grades Kindergarten through 12th grade, and associated recreation and athletic facilities serving its students.

School: Post-Secondary: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.9.C. (School: Post-Secondary)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.9), school: post-secondary is defined as an institution offering a formal educational program beyond K-12, including programs whose intent is academic, vocational, or continuing professional education. School: post-secondary includes college, technical school, trade school, and university.

School: Preschool/Daycare: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.9.A. (School: Preschool/Daycare)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.9), school: preschool/daycare is defined as a facility providing care, supervision, and educational services to children during the day. A school: preschool/daycare includes all forms of early childhood education, daycare, and after school supervision. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include in-home child care, for such uses see [Sec. 5D.2.2.A. (Household Business: Family Child Care)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.2).

Screening: Screening is defined as an arrangement of [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, vegetation, or site elements that are intended to block or obscure views into a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Div. 4C.8. (Screening)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.8).

Screening Plants: Screening plants are defined as plants that are arranged for the purposes of obscuring views into a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Screening Structure: A screening structure is defined as a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) obstructing visibility from outside an [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) area to another space, object, or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Sea: For the purposes of Sec. 13B.9.1. (Coastal Development Permit (Pre-Certification)) sea is defined as the Pacific Ocean and all harbors, bays, channels, canals, estuaries, salt marshes, sloughs and other areas subject to tidal action through any connection with the Pacific Ocean, excluding nonestuarine rivers, streams, tributaries, creeks, and flood control and drainage channels.

Sea Level Rise Area: Sea level rise area is defined as an area of the coast that is vulnerable to five feet of sea level rise, as determined by the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, the Ocean Protection Council, the United States Geological Survey, the University of California, and as accepted for use by the Director of Planning, or as determined by a local coastal hazards vulnerability assessment.

Senior Care Facility: Senior care facility is defined as any assisted living, senior independent living, or [skilled nursing home](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for [senior citizen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. See [Sec. 9.4.3. (Senior Care Facilities Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.4.3).

Senior Citizen: Senior citizen is defined as individuals who are at least 62 years of age, except that for projects of at least 35 units, a threshold of 55 years of age may be used, provided all applicable [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), state, and federal regulations are met.

Senior Citizen Housing Development: Senior citizen housing development is defined as a development that has at least 35 [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, as defined in California Civil Code Sec. 51.3 and Sec. 51.12, or a [mobile home park](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that limits residency based on age requirements for housing for older persons pursuant to California Civil Code Sec. 798.76 or Sec. 799.5.

Sensitive Use: Unless otherwise provided in this Code or [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) guidelines for a specific purpose, sensitive use is defined as any permitted [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) group, a [hospital](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), a [school](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in the open space & recreation use group shall be considered a sensitive use.

Service Floor Area: Service floor area is defined as all indoor [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) within an eating & drinking [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where the customer can be served, including an indoor dining or lounge area, bar-top and bar seating area, service counter, customer waiting area, customer restrooms, and indoor paths of travel accessible to customers.

Service Road: A service road is defined as that part of a major or secondary highway, containing a [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that affords [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) property, but is [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and approximately parallel to, and separated from the principal [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Sexually Oriented Business: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.13. (Sexually Oriented Business)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.13), sexually oriented business is defined as any commercial [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) sale, rental or exhibition, of any goods or services that are characterized by an emphasis on the exposure or display of [specified sexual activities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [specified anatomical parts](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Each sexually oriented business [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall constitute a separate sexually oriented business, even if operated in conjunction with another sexually oriented business at the same establishment, for the intent of meeting applicable use standards.

Sexually Oriented Business: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.13.A. (Sexually Oriented Business: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.13), sexually oriented business: general is defined as any [sexually oriented business](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), other than a [sexually oriented business: sexual encounter](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) establishment. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes but is not limited to adult arcades, adult bookstores, adult cabaret theaters, adult motion picture theaters, or striptease venues.

Sexually Oriented Business: Sexual Encounter: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.6.13.B. (Sexually Oriented Business: Sexual Encounter)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.13), sexually oriented business: sexual encounter is defined as any [sexually oriented business](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), other than [lodging](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) offering public accommodations, which, for any form of consideration, provides a place where two or more persons may congregate, associate or consort in connection with [specified sexual activities](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or the exposure of [specified anatomical parts](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where a medical practitioner, psychologist, psychiatrist, or similar professional licensed by the State of California engages in sexual therapy, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.8. (Medical Clinic)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.8).

Shared Equity Project: Shared equity project is defined as a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) containing [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that is located on land owned by a public agency, Community Land Trust, as defined in the California Revenue and Taxation Code Sec. 402.1(a)(11)(C)(ii), or a Limited-equity Housing Cooperative or Workforce Housing Cooperative Trust, as defined in California Civil Code Sec. 817, except that [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, in addition to being sold or rented to income qualified persons, may also be held by the non-profit corporation for the purpose of making [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s for [lower income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s financially stable. The land must be owned by the public agency, Community Land Trust, Limited-equity Housing Cooperative, or Workforce Housing Cooperative Trust at the time of [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) filing through the issuance of a [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Shared Housing Building: A residential or mixed-use [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), with five or more [shared housing unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and one or more common [kitchen](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and dining areas designed for permanent residence of more than 30 days by its tenants as defined in California Government Code Sec. 65915(o)(7)(A).

Shared Housing Unit: One or more [habitable room](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, not within another [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that includes a bathroom, sink, refrigerator, and microwave, and is used for permanent residence in a [shared housing building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and is as further defined in Government Code Sec. 65915(o)(7)(B). A shared housing unit shall comply with the definition of “ [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)” for purposes of zoning and allowable density.

Sheltered: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.2.A.3. (Sheltered)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.2) a space or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is considered sheltered if no portion of its area is [open to the sky](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Sheltering Structure: Sheltering structure is defined as any [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including [entry feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, canopies, or roofs, that creates a covered, unenclosed space.

Shopfront Cornice: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.6.5.C.3. (Shopfront Cornice)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.6.5), shopfront cornice is defined as a continuous molded projection located above a series of display windows on the [ground story facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Shopping Cart: A shopping cart is defined as a basket of any size, mounted on wheels, rollers or a similar device, including parts, provided by a retail establishment for the purpose of transporting groceries or merchandise of any kind within a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) establishment or associated [parking area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Shopping Cart Containment Plan: Shopping cart containment plan is defined as a plan sheet that includes a specific written plan with a corresponding site plan that identifies areas of shopping cart containment to prevent customers from removing [shopping cart](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s from the premises. See [Sec. 4C.12.8. (Shopping Cart Containment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.12.8).

Shopping Cart Corral: Shopping cart corral is defined as a stable [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that provides an [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the collection of [shopping cart](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Shoreline Project: Shoreline project is defined as any development in streams, wetlands, and other waters of the United States, and may include depositing of fill and dredged material, jetties, marinas, and piers.

Short-Term Rental: For the purposes of the [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), short-term rental is defined as a [rental unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), rented in whole or in part, to any [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)(s) for use of 30 consecutive days or less. Rental units within [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)-approved [lodging](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s shall not be considered a short-term rental.

Showroom Area: Showroom area is defined as the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) devoted to the display of heavy/large goods, such as furniture, mattresses, major household appliances, carpet, cars, or wholesale fabric where the assistance of a sales associate, special order, or delivery of goods is required.

Shrub: Shrub is defined as a small to medium sized perennial woody plant. Unlike herbaceous plants, shrubs have persistent woody stems above the ground. They are distinguished from trees by their multiple stems and shorter height and for purposes of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A) are less than 15 feet.

Side Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.C.5. (Side Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), side lot line is defined as any [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) not determined to be a [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [rear lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or [special lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Side Street Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.C.2. (Side Street Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), side street lot line is defined as a [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) separating a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from a side street [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Any [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) not determined to be a [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is considered a side street lot line.

Side Street Yard: Pursuant to Sec. 14.2.16.B.3. (Side Street Yard), side street yard is defined as the area between a side street lot line and an imaginary line running parallel to the side street lot line. The imaginary line shall be drawn 15 feet back from the portion of the side street lot line-facing facade nearest to the side street lot line, measured perpendicularly to the lot line.

Side Yard: Pursuant to Sec. 14.2.16.B.5. (Side Yard), side yard is defined as the portions of a lot between a side lot line and a principal structure. All portions of a lot that do not meet the yard designation criteria for any other yard shall be designated as a side yard.

Sidewalk Grade: Sidewalk grade is defined as the [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the sidewalk surface at any given point.

Sign: Sign is defined as any whole or part of a display board, [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), screen, or object, used to announce, declare, demonstrate, display, or otherwise present a message and attract the attention of the public.

Sign Face: Sign face is defined as the surface upon which the [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) message is placed.

Significant Tree: Significant tree is defined as any tree which measures 12 inches or more in diameter at 4.5 feet above the average natural grade at the base of the tree or is more than 35 feet in height.

Sill: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.9.2.C.4. (Sill)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.2), sill is defined as the bottommost horizontal exterior surface of a [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) including a ledge or other [architectural detail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that projects from the surrounding [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Simulated Divided-Lite: Simulated divided-lite is defined as a way to create the look of authentic divided lites, simulated divided-lite bars are permanently adhered to both sides of glass. See [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.5. (](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1) Symmetrical Lite Pattern).

Site: See [project site](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Site Modification: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.4. (Site Modification)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), site modification is defined as work including modifications to existing, or the addition of, new horizontal site improvements and landscaping, including trees, [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, street furniture, lighting fixtures, [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [flatwork](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), ground mounted [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and [parking lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) resurfacing or the reconfiguration of existing [parking stall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Skilled Nursing Home: Skilled nursing home is defined as [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) housing that is licensed by the California Department of Health, and provides acute, intermediate, or long-term skilled nursing care, and consists only of [efficiency dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s for its [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Full-time medical services may be provided on the premises. It may be a component of a [senior care facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See Sec. 5D.2.4.B. (Supportive Housing: Medical Care).

Slope: Slope is defined as the plane or incline of land, usually expressed as a percentage:

vertical distance

% slope = ----------------- x 100

horizontal distance

Small Species Tree: Small species tree is defined as a tree with a minimum 15-foot canopy [spread at maturity](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Social Service Center: Social service center is defined as any facility that provides services for the benefit of the community, on a voluntary basis, including the following: employment services, job training, business incubation, youth development, educational services, medical and mental health care, substance abuse treatment, food aid, or other similar services. See [Sec. 9.3.4.C.6. (Social Service Incentive Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3.4).

Social Services: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.10. (Social Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.10), social services are defined as [publicly accessible](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) administrative services and governmental services that support public welfare through social programs. Social services may be operated by a government entity, a non-profit or a non-governmental organization, and includes welfare service, foster family services, day treatment, adult day care, special needs care, and all other non-residential community care facilities.

Soil Depth: Pursuant to Sec. 4C.6.4.D.4. (Soil Depth), soil depth is defined as the shortest vertical dimension of growing medium provided, for all portions of a planting area.

Soil Volume: Pursuant to Sec. 4C.6.4.D.5. (Soil Volume), soil volume is defined as the total volume of growing medium provided. Drainage layers and other elements located within a container or planter that are not growing medium are not included in the calculation of soil volume.

Solid Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.4.A.4. (Solid Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.4), solid area is defined as the portions of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that have a permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or component physically obstructing the space from its surroundings. For the purpose of measuring the [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a space, portions of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) are considered solid area where a permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or component is located within five feet of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), measured perpendicular to the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and away from the subject space.

Solid Perimeter: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.4.A.6. (Solid Perimeter)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.4), solid perimeter is defined as the length of a perimeter of a space that consists of [solid area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the entire height of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Soundstages & Backlots: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.4. (Soundstages & Backlots)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.4), soundstages & backlots are defined as any [light industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) providing facilities for the construction and use of indoor or outdoor filming sets and adjoining backlot facilities, including supporting [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) workspace, [machine shop](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and warehousing related to filming or film production.

Special Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.C.3. (Special Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), special lot line is defined as any [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) mapped as a special lot line on the Special Lot Line map, pursuant to [Sec. 1.5.8. (Special Lot Line Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.5.8) and designated within an applied [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B) or [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B) that specifies standards for a special lot line.

Special Lot Line-Facing Facade: Special lot line-facing facade is defined as any [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) which [faces](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) a [special lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Special Use Program: Special use program is defined as programs established for [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that require a detailed and prescriptive set of performance standards for safe, orderly, and efficient operation, in addition to any general [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) standards and supplemental standards that may be included in the [Use District table](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Div. 5C.3. (Special Use Programs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3).

Special Yard: Pursuant to Sec. 14.2.16.B.2. (Special Yard), special yard is defined as the area between a special lot line and an imaginary line running parallel to the special lot line. The imaginary line shall be drawn 15 feet back from the portion of the special lot line-facing facade nearest to the primary street lot line, measured perpendicularly to the lot line.

Special Zone: A Special Zone is a set of self-contained development regulations, adopted by ordinance, tailored and applied to a designated area having unique characteristics that may not lend themselves to established [zoning district](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and regulations. See [Div. 8.3. (Special Zones)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.3).

Specific Adverse Impact: Pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 65589.5(d)(2), specific adverse impact is defined as a significant, quantifiable, direct, and unavoidable impact, based on objective, identified written public health or safety standards, policies, or conditions as they existed on the date the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) was deemed complete.

Specific Plan: Specific Plan is defined as a zoning tool, adopted by ordinance, to provide detailed standards, and regulations, together with a map or description defining the locations where such standards, and regulations apply.

Specified Anatomical Parts: The same as defined in [Chapter X. (Business Regulations), Sec. 103.01. (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-191042) of this Code.

Specified Sexual Activities: The same as defined in [Chapter X. (Business Regulations), Sec. 103.01. (Definitions)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=11003.2.&lawCode=BPC) of this Code.

Spread at Maturity: Spread at maturity is defined as the horizontal width of a [shrub](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or the crown of a tree at maturity. See Sec. 4C.6.4.D.3. (Canopy Diameter, Spread, and Height at Maturity).

Standard Hillside Limited Street: Standard hillside limited street is defined as a street (public or private) with a minimum width of 36 feet, and paved to a minimum roadway width of 28 feet, as determined by the Bureau of Engineering.

Standards Package: Standards package is defined as a group of related development standards which is applied through [Development Standards Districts (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B).

Stock Cooperative: The same as defined in [California Business and Professions Code, Sec. 11003.2](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=11003.2.&lawCode=BPC).

Storage, Indoor: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.4. (Storage, Indoor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.4), storage, indoor is defined as the indoor holding of goods, merchandise, supplies, material, machinery, equipment, or other items for future use.

Storage, Indoor: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.4.A. (Storage, Indoor: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.4), storage, indoor: general is defined as any [storage, indoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is incidental to another [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [storage, indoor: self-service](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for such uses see [Sec. 5D.7.4.B. (Storage, Indoor: Self-Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.4). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include indoor storage that functions as the primary [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and is not incidental to another [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), for such uses see [Sec. 5D.8.6. (Wholesale Trade & Warehousing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.6).

Storage, Indoor: Self-Service: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.4.B. (Storage, Indoor: Self-Service)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.4), storage, indoor: self-service is defined as any [storage, indoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that offers secure self-storage for household goods in individual rooms, compartments, lockers, or containers, to which clients bring goods for storage and retrieve them at any time during normal business hours.

Storage, Outdoor: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5. (Storage, Outdoor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor is defined as the outdoor holding of goods, merchandise, supplies, material, machinery, equipment, [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or other items for future use. Includes contractors' equipment storage yards and lumber yards.

Storage, Outdoor: Cargo Container: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5.E. (Storage, Outdoor: Cargo Container)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor: cargo container is defined as any [storage, outdoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the keeping of empty cargo containers. Storage, outdoor: cargo container may include storage of container chassis and commercial truck cabs, repair facilities, warehouses, and [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, incidental to the movement or storage of cargo containers. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the storage of cargo containers that are not empty, or [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s which are part of any freight transfer, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.5.3. (Freight Transfer Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.3).

Storage, Outdoor: Donation Bin: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5.D. (Storage, Outdoor: Donation Bin)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor: donation bin is defined as any [storage, outdoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), involving a box, canister, receptacle, or other container that can be opened and closed, and is used for collecting salvageable personal property, including, but not limited to, clothing, shoes, books, and household items for periodic off-site processing or redistribution. For purposes of this definition, salvageable personal property shall not include [recyclable materials](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) not intended for re-use, including, but not limited to, newspapers, plastic, glass, aluminum, electronics, toxic or hazardous materials, and solid waste. For purposes of this definition, donation bins are limited dimensionally to 82-inches in height, 50-inches in depth, and 60-inches in width. For bins that are larger in size, see [Sec. 5D.9.4.A. (Recycling Facility: Collection)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.4).

Storage, Outdoor: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5.A. (Storage, Outdoor: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor: general is defined as any [storage, outdoor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is in conjunction with another [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This use does not include the keeping of empty cargo containers, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.5.E. (Storage, Outdoor: Cargo Container)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include inactive large vehicles, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.C. (Storage, Outdoor: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include towing and storage for official [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) impound, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.5.F. (Storage, Outdoor: Official Motor Vehicle Impound)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include inactive standard vehicles, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.7.5.B. (Storage, Outdoor: Standard Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5).

Storage, Outdoor: Large Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5.C. (Storage, Outdoor: Large Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor: large vehicle is defined as the outdoor storage of large vehicles that are not actively used by the site's occupants, employees, or visitors. Large vehicles include [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s possessing three or more axles, such as trailer trucks, construction vehicles, motor homes, and [recreational vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s as well as recreational boats and watercraft. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes storage of inoperable [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s where [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are actively used by the site's occupants, employees, or visitors; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.6. (Parking)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.6).

Storage, Outdoor: Official Motor Vehicle Impound: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5.F. (Storage, Outdoor: Official Motor Vehicle Impound)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor: official motor vehicle impound is defined as any [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) towing and storage service that involves [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)-approved vendors that support the public safety mission of the Los Angeles Police Department and Department of Transportation.

Storage, Outdoor: Standard Vehicle: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.7.5.B. (Storage, Outdoor: Standard Vehicle)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.7.5), storage, outdoor: standard vehicle is defined as the outdoor storage of standard vehicles that are not actively used by the site's occupants, employees, or visitors. Standard vehicles include [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s possessing two or fewer axles, such as cars, motorcycles, sport utility vehicles, pickup trucks, and vans. Includes storage of inoperable [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s where [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are actively used by the site's occupants, employees, or visitors; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.3.6. (Parking)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.6).

Stories: See [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Story: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10. (Story)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), story is defined as the portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) included between the upper surface of a floor and the upper surface of the floor next above, except that the top most story is that portion of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) included between the upper surface of a floor and the upper surface of the ceiling structure above.

Street Centerline: Street centerline is defined as a line that is aligned to the center of a street as established and maintained by the Department of Public Works, Bureau of Engineering.

Street Designation: Street designation is defined as the classification assigned to a [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or other [public right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) based on Citywide General Plan Circulation System maps of the [Circulation Element](https://planning.lacity.gov/odocument/523f2a95-9d72-41d7-aba5-1972f84c1d36/Mobility_Plan_2035.pdf) for the purposes of providing dimensional and performance standards.

Street Frontage: For the purposes of [Div. 4C.11. (Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11), street frontage is defined as the length of a line separating a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from one street.

Street Lot Line: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.12.B.2. (Street Lot Line)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.12), street lot line is defined as any [lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that [abut](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s a street [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Street lot lines include all [primary street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [side street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and [alley lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Street Step-Back: Pursuant to [Sec. 2C.6.1. (Street Step-Back)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.6.1), street step-back is defined as a step-like recess in the massing of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that requires upper [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to be pushed back from the lower [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) from the street.

Street Visible Area: For the purposes of [Historic Preservation (Div. 13B.8.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.8), street visible area is defined as any portion of the front, side, and rear [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that can be seen from any [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) street, [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or sidewalk, or that would be visible but are currently obstructed by [landscaping](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), fencing, or freestanding [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. It also includes undeveloped portions of the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) would be visible from the [adjacent](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) street or sidewalk; [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that are generally visible from non-adjacent streets due to steep topography; or second [stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) visible over adjacent one [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Street Wall: Street wall is defined as the condition created along a street by the fronts and consistent setbacks of [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, and enhanced by the continuity and the height of the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Street Yard: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.16.C.2. (Street Yard)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.16), street yard is defined as a category of [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s referring to all [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that [abut](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) a street [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) including [front yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [side street yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Street-Facing Entrance: Pursuant to Sec. 3C.5.1. (Street-Facing Entrance), street-facing entrance is defined as a door providing access from the public realm to the interior of a building.

Street-Facing Facade: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.6.D. (Street-Facing Facade)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.6), street-facing facade is defined as the portions of any frontage applicable [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), pursuant to [Sec. 3A.2.2.C.2. (Frontage Applicable Facades)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3A.2.2), having no permanent [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) (not including [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s) located between the [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and a [street lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [special lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Structural Floor: Structural floor is defined as the assembly of building components that compose a floor, which includes any structural members, subfloor, and similar elements. Structural floor does not include finish or underlayment materials such as carpets, tiles, or membranes.

Structural Modification: Structural modification is defined as any change to the existing load-bearing members of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including bearing walls, columns, beams, or girders.

Structure: Structure is defined as any constructed object more than 30 inches in height. For constructed objects 30 inches or lower in height, see [flatwork](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Structure Footprint: See [building footprint](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Student Housing Development: Student housing development is defined pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 65915(b)(1)(F).

Subdivider: The same as defined in [California Government Code, Sec. 66423. (Subdivider)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66423.&lawCode=GOV).

Subdivision: The same as defined in [California Government Code, Sec. 66424. (Subdivision)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66424.&lawCode=GOV). Subdivision includes a [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Subdivision Approval: Subdivision approval is defined as any approval under [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7).

Subdivision Committee: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.7.1.D. (Subdivision Committee)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7.1), subdivision committee is defined as an advisory committee composed of the following officers of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or their duly authorized representatives: the [City Engineer](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); the Superintendent of Building; the Chief Engineer of the Department of Fire; the Chief Engineer and General Manager of the Department of Water and Power; the General Manager of the Department of General Services; the General Manager of the Department of Recreation and Parks; the General Manager of the Department of Transportation; and the Director of the Bureau of Street Lighting of the Department of Public Works.

Subdivision Design: Subdivision design is defined as a set of design features, elements, and infrastructure incorporated into a [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) including: street alignments, [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and widths; drainage and sanitary facilities and utilities, including alignments and [grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s; location and size of all required [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and [right-of-way](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s; fire roads and firebreaks; [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and size configuration; traffic [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); [grading](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#); [dedication of land](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for park and recreation purposes; and such other specific requirements in the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and configuration of the entire [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) as may be necessary or convenient to insure conformity to or implementation of the [General Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or any adopted [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Subdivision Improvement: The same as defined in [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Sec. 66419. (Improvement)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66419.&lawCode=GOV). For standards to subdivision improvements see Sec. 11.3.3. (Subdivision Improvements).

Subdivision Map Act: The Subdivision Map Act, [California Government Code, Title 7. (Planning and Land Use), Div. 2. (Subdivisions)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?division=2.&chapter=1.&lawCode=GOV&title=7.&article=1.), commencing with [California Government Code, Sec. 66410](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66410&lawCode=GOV).

Subject Use: As used in [Article 5. (Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5), a "subject use" refers to a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is subject to applicable use rules, permissions, standards, supplemental findings, or special use programs.

Substandard Hillside Limited Street: Substandard hillside limited street is defined as a street which does not meet the minimum requirements of a standard hillside limited street (public or private), because it has a width less than 36 feet or is paved to a [roadway](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) width of less than 28 feet, as determined by the Bureau of Engineering.

Supergraphic Sign: Supergraphic sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), consisting of an image projected onto a [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or printed on vinyl, mesh or other material, with or without written text, supported and attached to a [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by an adhesive, by using stranded cable and eye-bolts, or with other materials and methods, and that does not comply with the following provisions of this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A): [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.9. (Projecting Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.5. (Marquee Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), [Sec. 4C.11.2. (Temporary Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.2), [Sec. 4C.11.1.E.2. (Original Art Murals, Vintage Original Art Murals and Public Art Installations)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.1).

Superintendent: Pursuant to Sec. 13B.10.3.A.2. (Definitions), Superintendent is defined as the Superintendent of Building or his or her authorized representative.

Supplemental District: Supplemental District is defined as a limited set of topic-specific development regulations, adopted by ordinance, and is indicated in a third zoning bracket in the [zone string](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and applied to a designated area in order to establish additional regulations that build upon and enhance regulations applied through [zoning district](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. See [Div. 8.2. (Supplemental Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2).

Supportive Housing: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.4. (Supportive Housing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.4), supportive housing is defined as a [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that provides housing accommodations and support services on a voluntary basis to [resident](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s on an ongoing basis.

Supportive Housing: General: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.4. (Supportive Housing: General)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.4), supportive housing: general is defined as a [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with no limit on length of stay for [person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s with low incomes and/or who have one or more disabilities who may require support from on-site or off-site supportive services for daily living. Eligible populations may include seniors, children within the foster care system, emancipated minors, families with children, elderly persons, young adults aging out of the foster care system, individuals exiting from institutional settings, individuals receiving rehabilitation or mental health support, veterans, and persons or families experiencing homelessness. The housing accommodations are linked to on-site or off-site [supportive services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including, but not limited to: subsidized, permanent housing; intensive case management; medical or mental health care; substance abuse treatment; employment services; benefits advocacy; or other services or service referrals necessary to obtain and maintain housing. Any [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) used for [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) workspace accommodating the administration of [supportive services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) shall be incidental to the [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Medical services shall not be provided on the premises, unless otherwise permitted by the applied [Use District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Supportive housing: general includes a [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [community care facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), assisted living, and [permanent supportive housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). [Residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s with six or fewer beds shall be classified as a [dwelling](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) rather than supportive housing: general. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include non-residential community care facilities, for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Social Services (Sec. 5D.3.10.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.10).

Supportive Housing: Medical Care: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.4.B. (Supportive Housing: Medical Care)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.4), supportive housing: medical care is defined as a [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of long, and short-term occupation, which may be licensed by the California Department of Health, to provide 24-hour non-acute medical services and supportive care on the premises. Supportive housing: medical care includes congregate living health facilities, [skilled nursing home](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) mental health facilities, and hospice care. Any [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) used for [office](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) workspace accommodating the administration of medical services and supportive care shall be incidental to the [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Supportive housing: medical care facilities may include [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, common dining areas, or other community rooms.

Supportive Housing: Transitional: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.2.4.C. (Supportive Housing: Temporary)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.2.4), Supportive housing: temporary is defined as a facility providing temporary housing accommodations or services, including low barrier navigation, to persons or families experiencing homelessness. Supportive housing: temporary may provide housing for persons or families experiencing homelessness for a time period not to exceed six months within a calendar year. Supportive housing: temporary shall be provided by a government agency or private non-profit organization which provides, or contracts with recognized community organizations to provide, emergency or temporary shelter or services for persons or families experiencing homelessness.

Supportive Services: Supportive services are defined as services that are provided on a voluntary basis to residents of [supportive housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [transitional housing](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), including, but not limited to, intensive case management, medical and mental health care, substance abuse treatment, employment services, benefits advocacy, and other services or service referrals necessary to obtain and maintain housing. See Sec. 9.4.1. (Permanent Supportive Housing Incentive Program).

Surrounding Grade: Surrounding grade is defined as the [elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) measured along the perimeter of an object, assembly, or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Surveyed Historic Resource: Surveyed historic resource is defined as any [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), object, site, landscape, or [natural feature](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) identified through an historic resources survey as eligible for listing as either an individual resource or as a contributor to a historic district under a local, state or federal designation program, including but not limited to listing in the National Register of Historic Places or California Register of Historical Resources, or designation as a [Historic-Cultural Monument](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or as a [Historic Preservation Overlay Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). This term does not include a non-contributor to an eligible historic district.

Surveyor: Surveyor is defined as a licensed land surveyor authorized to practice in California.

Sustainable Energy Systems: Sustainable energy systems is defined as any equipment which uses renewable energy sources, such as solar or wind power, to generate electricity, heating or cooling.

Symmetrical Lite Pattern: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.5. (Symmetrical Lite Pattern)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1), symmetrical lite pattern is defined as [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) panes that are arranged or designed so that the left-side of the [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) composition is a mirror image of the right-side of the [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) composition.

### T

Target Population: For the purposes of [Article 9. (Public Benefit Systems)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9), target population is defined as persons with qualifying lower incomes who:

1\. Have one or more disabilities, including mental illness, HIV or AIDS, substance abuse, or other chronic health condition, and are homeless as defined by any Los Angeles City, Los Angeles County, State of California, or federal guidelines; or

2\. Are chronically homeless, as defined by any Los Angeles City, Los Angeles County, State of California, or federal guidelines.

Targeted Planting Area: Targeted planting area is defined as a [planting area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with boundaries established pursuant to [Sec. 1.5.5.B. (Boundaries)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.5.5).

Targeted Planting List: Targeted planting list is defined as the document containing planting requirements established to implement the Targeted Planting Areas Map. See [Sec. 1.5.5. (Targeted Planting Map)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.5.5).

Temporary Construction Wall: Temporary construction wall is defined as a temporary solid [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or barrier of wood or similar material that provides protection for pedestrians and is erected and maintained on the perimeter of a construction or demolition site, which may be required by [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Sec. 91.3306. (Protection of Pedestrians)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-201509) of this Code.

Temporary Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.2. (Temporary Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.2), temporary sign is defined as any [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that is to be maintained for a limited duration, including paper signs, posters, pennants, banners, ribbons, streamers, spinners, and other [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that are not permanently affixed to the ground or [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Temporary Use: Pursuant to [Sec.14.2.15.B.7. (Temporary Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), temporary use is defined as a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) with any [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) defined in [Part 5D. (Use Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D) that does not exceed 180 days and meets the requirements of [Chapter IX. (Building Regulations), Sec. 91.106.1.3. (Temporary Permits)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-172464) of this Code.

Tentative Tract Map: Tentative tract map is defined as a map made for the purpose of showing the design of a proposed [subdivision](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) creating five or more [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, five or more [condominium](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or five or more units in a [community apartment project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [stock cooperative](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and prepared pursuant to [Sec. 11.2. (Tentative Tract Maps)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/11#11.2).

Through Lot: Through lot is defined as a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) two parallel or approximately parallel streets, a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) situated at the intersection of two streets having an angle of intersection of 35 degrees or less, or a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) three or more streets. A through lot does not include those [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) a street and also [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) a navigable public canal or waterway parallel or approximately parallel to said street.

Tier 1 Bonus Floor Area Ratio: Tier 1 bonus floor area ratio is defined as the bonus [floor area ratio](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granted pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.1.C.2. (Tier 1 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.1).

Tier 1 Bonus Height: Tier 1 bonus height is defined as the bonus [height in feet](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granted pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.2.C.2. (Tier 1 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.2) or the bonus [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granted pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.3.C.2.b. (Tier 1 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.3).

Tier 2 Bonus Floor Area Ratio: Tier 2 bonus floor area ratio is defined as the tier 2 bonus floor area ratio granted pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.1.C.2. (Tier 2 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.1).

Tier 2 Bonus Height: Tier 2 bonus height is defined as the bonus [height in feet](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granted pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.2.C.2.3. (Tier 2 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.2) or the bonus [height in stories](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) granted pursuant to [Sec. 2C.4.3.C.2.c. (Tier 2 Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2C.4.3).

Tract Map: Tract map is defined as either a [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [final tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Transient: For the purposes of the [Home-Sharing Program (Sec. 5C.3.2.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5C.3.2), transient shall have the same meaning as that term is defined in [Chapter II. (Licenses, Permits, Business Regulations), Sec. 21.7.2. (Definitions)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-126755) of this Code.

Transition Screen: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.8.2. (Transition Screens)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.8.2), transition screen is defined as a device or combination of elements along a [common lot line](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that conceals, obstructs or protects [abutting](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s from impactful [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, activities, or site elements.

Transitional Foster Youth: Transitional foster youth is defined pursuant to California Education Code Sec. 66025.9.

Transitional Housing: Transitional housing is defined as a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where housing linked to [supportive services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is offered, usually for a period of up to 24 months, to facilitate movement to permanent housing for persons with low incomes who may have one or more disabilities, and may include but are not limited to, adults, emancipated minors, families with children, elderly persons, young adults aging out of the foster care system, individuals exiting from institutional settings, veterans, and persons or families experiencing homelessness.

Transmit: See [transmitted](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Transmitted: Transmitted is defined as a notification of a decision in writing, by mail, or electronically. See [Sec. 13A.2.5.D. (Transmittal)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.5).

Transparent Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 3C.4.1. (Transparent Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.1), transparent area is defined as the amount of transparent area on a [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Transportation Demand Management: Transportation demand management is defined as the modification of travel behavior through programs of incentives, services, and policies, including encouraging the use of alternatives to single-occupant [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s such as public transit, cycling, walking, [carpool](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) ing/ [vanpool](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) ing, and changes in work schedule that move trips out of the peak period or eliminate them altogether (such as telecommuting or compressed work weeks).See [Div. 4C.5. (Transportation Demand Management)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.5).

Transportation Use: Pursuant to [Div. 5D.5. (Transportation Uses)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5), transportation use is defined as [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that facilitate major modes of transportation for the loading or unloading of passengers and freight.

Trash Chute: Trash chute is defined as any vertical smooth shaft used to convey rubbish, trash, or garbage from the upper floors of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) to a trash storage bin or room at the bottom end of the chute.

Tree Expert: Tree expert is defined as a person with at least four years of experience in the business of transplanting, moving, caring for, and maintaining trees and who is a certified arborist with the International Society of Arboriculture, and who holds a valid California license as an agricultural pest control advisor; or a landscape architect; or a registered consulting arborist with the American Society of Consulting Arborists.

Trip Reduction: For the purposes of [Article 9. (Public Benefit Systems)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9) trip reduction is defined as the reduction in the number of work-related trips made by single-occupant [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

### U

Uncovered: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.2.A.2. (Uncovered)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.2), uncovered is defined as an instance where 25 percent or more of a space or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)'s area is [open to the sky](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Areas containing overhead, non-solid [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, such as lattice and pergolas, may be considered uncovered provided that 25 percent or more of their area is [open to the sky](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Underground Parking: Underground parking is defined as [motor vehicle use area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s located below the [finished floor elevation](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Underground Structure: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.j. (Underground Structures)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), underground structure is defined as a [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located entirely below [finished grade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Examples of underground structures include, but are not limited to: cellars, [basement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [underground parking](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, stormwater storages, or cisterns.

Unenclosed: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.4.A.2. (Unenclosed)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.4), unenclosed is defined as an instance when the perimeter of a space has an [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of less than 66.7 percent.

Unexpired: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.12.1.C. (Definitions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.12.1) of this Code, unexpired is defined as the applicable redevelopment regulations that are still in effect on the date of approval of a [redevelopment plan project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [redevelopment plan amendment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).
