Unified Development: Unified development is defined as a development consisting of multiple [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s within a common site plan which is unified by a combination of functional linkages, such as pedestrian or vehicular connections, common architectural and landscape features which constitute distinctive design elements of the development, and when viewed from adjoining streets appears to be a consolidated whole. A unified development may include [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that [abut](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or are separated only by an [alley](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or are located across the street from any portion of each other. See [Sec. 14.2.1. (Lot)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.1) for clarification on [lot tie](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Uniformity Ratio: Uniformity ratio is defined as a ratio of the average illumination to minimum illumination.

Upper Story: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10.D. (Upper Story)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), upper story is defined as any [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located above the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Upper Story Facade: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.10.E. (Upper Story Facade)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.10), upper story facade is defined as the portions of the exterior [building envelope](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at the perimeter of each [upper story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for the full height of the [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Upper Story Height: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.5.2. (Upper Story Height)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.5.2), upper story height is defined as the floor-to-floor height of any [story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) located above the [ground story](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Urbanized Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 8.2.4.B.3.b. (Urbanized Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/8#8.2.4), urbanized area is defined as all land in the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), except land in the Heavy Industrial 1 [Use District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and land which has been determined to be [non-urbanized area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by the [City Planning Commission](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or land located in the [Los Angeles City Oil Field Area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Use: Use is defined as the purpose for which land or a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is arranged, designed, or intended, or for which land or a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is, or may be, occupied or maintained.

Use Category: Use category is defined as a group of [use group](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Use District: Use District is defined as the fourth component in a [zone string](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) established in [Part 5B. (Use Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B), which regulates land [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s by assigning [permission level](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s for defined [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s as well as citing applicable performance standards, supplemental procedures for conditional uses, and [special use program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Use District Table: Use District table is defined as a table provided for each [Use District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) established in [Part 5B. (Use Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B) that contains a list of [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s and their assigned [permission level](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, along with any applicable performance standards, conditional use procedures, and [special use program](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that apply to [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s within a [Use District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Use Group: Use group is defined as a group of individual [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s with common [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) characteristics and similar activities.

Use Modification: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.15.B.6. (Use Modification)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.15), use modification is defined as a [change of use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or an [intensification of use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Used Vehicle Sales Area: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.10.4. (Annual Inspection Monitoring (Type 2))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.10.4), used vehicle sales area is defined as an area or [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where any type of used [motor vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or trailer is displayed for sale.

Utilities: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.11. (Utilities)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.11), utilities is defined as utility infrastructure as a primary [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land, necessary for the public provision of services such as water, sewer, power, or communications. For the purposes of this definition, utilities [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s exclude the following off-site systems: transmission lines, pipes, or other systems for conveying and transmitting services within utility [easement](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, as those systems are not regulated as a [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of land by [Article 5. (Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5).

Utilities: Major: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.11.B. (Utilities: Major)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.11), utilities: major is defined as utility infrastructure that requires significant health, safety, and environmental precautions due to potential adverse impacts immediate surroundings, and requires on-site personnel. Utilities: major include non-solar power generation facilities, wastewater treatment, and water supply treatment.

Utilities: Minor: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.11.A. (Utilities: Minor)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.11), utilities: minor is defined as utility infrastructure that does not require significant health, safety, and environmental precautions, and do not require on-site personnel. Utilities: minor includes renewable energy generation, including wind turbines, geothermal systems, and solar photovoltaic systems serving no more than 10 different [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s with supporting on-site storage, control and transmission equipment, storm water retention or detention ponds, aeration and septic systems, reservoirs, lift stations, water supply wells and water tanks or towers, telecommunications switching facilities, and electrical substations.

Utilities: Solar Energy Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.11.C. (Utilities: Solar Energy Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.11), utilities: solar energy facility is defined as utility infrastructure that generates energy for the general public using a solar photovoltaic system primarily for off-site use or sale serving 11 or more [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Utilities: Wireless Facility, Freestanding: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.11.D. (Utilities: Wireless Facility, Freestanding)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.11), utilities: wireless facility, freestanding is defined as a freestanding device or system including a monopole, tower, or antenna for the transmitting or receiving of electromagnetic signals, including, but not limited to, radio waves and microwaves, for cellular technology, personal communications services, mobile services, paging systems and related technologies. Facilities include antennas, microwave dishes, parabolic antennas and all other types of equipment used in the transmission and reception of such signals; structures for the support of such facilities, associated [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or cabinets to house support equipment, and other [accessory structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or development. A utilities: wireless facility, freestanding is a type of telecommunications facility.

Utilities: Wireless Facility, Rooftop: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.11.E. (Utilities: Wireless Facility, Rooftop)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.11), utilities: wireless facility, rooftop is defined as a device or system that is mounted on a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) rooftop for the transmitting or receiving of electromagnetic signals, including, but not limited to, radio waves and microwaves, for cellular technology, personal communications services, mobile services, private antennas, paging systems and related technologies. Facilities include antennas, microwave dishes, parabolic antennas and all other types of equipment used in the transmission and reception of such signals; structures for the support of such facilities, associated [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or cabinets to house support equipment, and other [accessory structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s or development. A utilities: wireless facility, rooftop is a type of telecommunications facility.

Utility Area: Utility area is defined as any area containing [mechanical equipment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [utility equipment](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Utility Equipment: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.i. (Utility Equipment)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), utility equipment is defined as equipment related to publicly-operated or utility-operated systems, including their related wires, conduits and pipes. Examples of utility equipment include, but are not limited to: hydrants, transformers, utility cabinets, water utility devices, cable television boxes, Internet boxes, or phone boxes.

### V

Vacant Lot: Vacant lot is defined as a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on which no [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), temporary or permanent, is erected; or which has no [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s of the land.

Vanpool: Vanpool is defined as a [vehicle](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) carrying six or more persons to and from work on a regular schedule, and on a prepaid basis.

Variance: Pursuant to [Sec. 13B.5.3. (Variance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.5.3), variance is defined as granted relief from a standard or regulation in this Chapter or [Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-107408) on the basis of hardship or difficulties.

Vegetation: For purposes of [Sec. 14.1.5. (Encroachments)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.1.5) vegetation is defined as living organisms, absorbing water and organic substances through its roots and synthesizing nutrients. Examples of vegetation include, but are not limited to: trees, shrubs, flowers, herbs, vegetables, grasses, ferns, or moss.

Vehicle: Vehicle is defined as anything used to transport people or goods, including automobiles, vans, trucks, buses, and motorcycles, bicycles, or any other form of micro-mobility.

Vehicle Entry Restriction Device: Vehicle entry restriction device is defined as any device, such as mechanical gates or ticket dispensers, restricting ingress vehicle traffic during operating hours.

Vertical Band Articulation: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.6.4. (Vertical Band Articulation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.6.4), vertical band articulation is a continuous band of material running vertically up a [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Vertical Circulation: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.B.1.d. (Vertical Circulation)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), vertical circulation is defined as [enclosed](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [covered](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s used for [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) circulation and rooftop [access](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). Examples of vertical circulation may include, but are not limited to: elevator rooms and associated equipment, and stair accesses to a roof.

Vertical Encroachment: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.B. (Vertical Encroachments)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), vertical encroachment is defined as a [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or assembly that extends vertically into a space where [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s are typically prohibited.

Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone: The Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zone (VHFHSZ) are determined through the [Local Hazard Mitigation Plan](https://emergency.lacity.gov/local-hazard-mitigation-plan) (LHMP) wildfire hazard assessment, based on boundaries established by the Los Angeles Fire Department in accordance with state law.

Very Low Income Household: A very low income household is a household whose annual income, adjusted for family size, does not exceed 50 percent of the area median income as designated for this category in [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 50105](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=50105.&lawCode=HSC).

Very Low Vehicle Travel Area: Very low vehicle travel area is defined pursuant to California Government Code Sec. 65915(o)(9).

Vesting Preliminary Parcel Map: Vesting preliminary parcel map is defined as a [preliminary parcel map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for any land division that has printed conspicuously on its face the words "Vesting Preliminary Parcel Map" and is characterized by certain rights to proceed with development when filed and processed in accordance with [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7).

Vesting Tentative Tract Map: Vesting tentative tract map is defined as a [tentative tract map](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for any land division that has printed conspicuously on its face the words “Vesting Tentative Tract Map” and is characterized by certain rights to proceed with development when filed and processed in accordance with [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7).

Vintage Original Art Mural: Vintage original art mural is defined as an [original art mural](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that existed prior to October 12, 2013 (the operative date of [Ord. No. 182,706](https://clkrep.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2009/09-0969-S4_ord_188063_2-10-24.pdf)). See [Div. 4C.11. (Signs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11).

Visual Light Transmittance: Visual light transmittance is defined as the amount of light in the visible portion of the spectrum that passes through a glazing material as defined in manufacturer specifications.

Visual Obstruction: Visual obstruction is defined as any opaque object, assembly, or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that obscures visibility through a [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), on the [interior](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) side of the [transparent area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Sec. 3C.4.1. (Transparent Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3C.4.1).

### W

Waiver: For the purposes of [Sec. 9.2.1. (State Density Bonus)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.1), [Sec. 9.2.2. (Affordable Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.2), [Sec. 9.2.3. (Opportunity Corridors Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), [Sec. 9.2.4. (Corridor Transitions Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), and [Sec. 9.2.5. (Transit Oriented Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.5), waivers are defined as reductions in [development standard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s that will have the effect of physically precluding the construction of a [housing development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) at the densities or with the incentives permitted under those referenced Sections, as specifically discussed in California Government Code Sec. 65915(e). Waivers neither reduce nor increase the number of incentives or [density bonus](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is entitled to in those Sections. The terms [density bonus](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), [incentive](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), and [housing development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), are defined in this [Glossary (Div. 14.3.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.3).

Walking Distance: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.3.A.2. (Walking Distance)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.3), walking distance is defined as the [distance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) measured as the most direct path of travel for a pedestrian.

Wall: Wall is defined as a constructed vertical barrier erected to enclose, screen, or separate areas. A wall differs from a [fence](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in having a solid foundation along its whole length.

Wall Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.12. (Wall Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), wall sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) on the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or [structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), with the exposed face of the [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) in a plane approximately parallel to the plane of the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that has been attached to, painted on, or erected against the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), projected onto the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), or printed on any material which is supported and attached to the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) by an adhesive or other materials or methods.

Waste Enclosure: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.5.A.1.h. (Waste Enclosure)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.5), waste enclosure is defined as waste areas and their required [screening structure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s. Examples of waste enclosures include, but are not limited to: trash compactors, garbage, recycling, or food waste.

Waste Facility: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.5. (Waste Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.5), waste facility is defined as any [heavy industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the receipt, storage, separation, conversion, combustion, processing of solid waste, transfer of waste directly from small to larger vehicles for transport, or operation as a landfill. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes facilities involved in the transfer, processing, and transformation of organic waste, construction and demolition debris, inert material, solid waste.

Waste Facility: Hazardous Waste: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.5.B. (Waste Facility: Hazardous Waste)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.5), waste facility: hazardous waste is defined as any [waste facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) involving the storage, treatment, and disposal of hazardous waste, as defined in the [California Health and Safety Code, Sec. 25117.1. (Definitions)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=25117.1.).

Waste Facility: Organic Waste: Pursuant to Sec. 5D.9.5.A. (Waste Facility: Organic Waste), waste facility: organic waste is defined as any [waste facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that receives any material that comes from a plant or animal and is biodegradable, for chipping and grinding, composting, curing, mulching or similar processing methods. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include any chipping and grinding, composting, curing, or mulching conducted as part of the maintenance of landscaped areas associated with any public & institutional uses or open space & recreation uses.

Waste Facility: Solid Waste: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.9.5.C. (Waste Facility: Solid Waste)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.5), waste facility: solid waste is defined as any [waste facility](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that does not involve any storage, treatment, and disposal of hazardous waste, or that does not exclusively receive organic waste. For such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, see [Sec. 5D.9.5.B. (Waste facility: Hazardous Waste)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.5) and [Sec. 5D.9.5.A. (Waste Facility: Organic Waste)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.9.5).

Water Supply: For the purposes of [Div. 13B.7. (Division of Land)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.7), water supply is defined as the water system supply and distribution facilities necessary to provide a reliable and adequate water supply for private use and public fire protection purposes.

Weighted Solid Perimeter: Pursuant to [Sec. 14.2.4.A.7. (Weighted Solid Perimeter)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.4), weighted solid perimeter is defined as the length of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) weighted by the percent of the [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) area that is composed of [solid area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), for each [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) where [perimeter plane](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s consist of a mix of [solid area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and [non-solid area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Wetland: For the purposes of [Sec. 13B.9.2. (Coastal Development Permit (Post-Certification))](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.9.2), wetland is defined as lands within the [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), which may be covered periodically or permanently with shallow, water and include saltwater marshes, freshwater marshes, open or closed brackish water marshes, swamps, mudflats and fens.

Wholesale Trade & Warehousing: Pursuant to [Sec. 5D.8.5. (Wholesale Trade & Warehousing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.8.5), wholesale trade & warehousing is defined as any [light industrial use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) facility primarily [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) d for the high volume storage of goods for sale in large quantities primarily to businesses, or the storage of products intended for consolidation and distribution to manufacturers, wholesalers, retailers, or end users. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) includes seasonal inventory storage, distribution centers, fulfillment centers, cold storage facilities, and facilities housing goods for sale in bulk to businesses or institutions. This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the sale of goods directly to consumers; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.6.12. (Retail)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.6.12). This [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) does not include the transshipment of freight between different modes of transport, such as rail to trucking transport; for such [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s see [Sec. 5D.5.3. (Freight Transfer Facility)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.5.3).

Whorl: Whorl is defined as the arrangement of three or more buds, leaves, flowers, or twigs at the same node.

Window: Window is defined as an operable or inoperable opening constructed in a [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) that admits light or air into an [enclosure](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and is often framed and spanned with glass or other translucent material.

Window Assembly: Window assembly is defined as a manufactured assembly of a frame, sash, glazing, and necessary hardware, made to fit a [window opening](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Window Display: Window display is defined as a display, behind a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), along the [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) exhibiting items or advertisements designed to attract the attention of passersby, including [window sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

Window Frame: Window frame is defined as the fixed frame of a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), consisting of two jambs, a head, and a [sill](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Window Opening: Window opening is defined as an opening in the [wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) for admitting light and air, usually fitted with a frame in which are set operable sashes containing panes of glass.

Window Recession: Pursuant to [Sec. 3D.9.1.C.3. (Window Recession)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3D.9.1), window recession is defined as the depth that a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is set back from the surrounding [facade](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Window Sash: Window sash is defined as the fixed or movable framework of a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or door in which panes of glass are set.

Window Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C.11.6.C.13. (Window Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.11.6), window sign is defined as a [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), except for a [supergraphic sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#), that is attached to, affixed to, leaning against, or otherwise placed within six feet of a [window](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or door in a manner so that the [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) is visible from outside the [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#).

Wood Waste: Wood waste is defined as any discarded untreated or unpainted wood material, and includes pallets, plywood, and other construction-related scrap lumber, stumps, and tree trimmings.

### X

### Y

Yard: Yard is defined as all portions of a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) between [exterior wall](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s of a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) and a property line. See [Sec.14.2.16. (Yards)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.16).

Yard Sign: Pursuant to [Sec. 4C. 11.6.C.14. (Yard Sign)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C), yard sign is defined as a small [sign](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) placed in a [yard](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) or other amenity space.

### Z

Zone String: Pursuant to [Sec. 1.3.1. (Zone String)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.3.1), zone string is defined as the combination of [zoning district](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s applied to a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) including, [Form District (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B), [Frontage District (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), [Development Standards District (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B), [Use District (Part 5B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B), and [Density District (Part 6B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/6#6B).

Zoning Administrator: Zoning Administrator is defined as the Chief Zoning Administrator or an Associate Zoning Administrator. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) may appoint the Zoning Administrator to act as the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#)’s designee or as a Hearing Officer for the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#). See [Sec. 13A.1.7. (Zoning Administrator)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.1.7).

Zoning District: Zoning district is defined as all zoning districts that compose a [zone string](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) including [Form Districts (Part 2B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/2#2B), [Frontage Districts (Part 3B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/3#3B), [Development Standards Districts (Part 4B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4B), [Use Districts (Part 5B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5B), and [Density Districts (Part 6B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/6#6B). Pursuant to [Sec. 1.3.1.B. (Zoning Districts)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/1#1.3.1), the term zoning district does not include [Specific Plan](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, [Supplemental District](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s, or [Special Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#) s.

# Article 15. Fees

## Div. 15.1. General Rules

This Division (General Rules) identifies the general standards involved in administering the required fees for land use and development requests which are subject to this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A).

### Sec. 15.1.1. Filing of Applications & Appeals

1. ##### Filing Date


See [Sec. 13A.2.3. (Applications)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.3).

2. ##### Time Limit - Appeals


See [Sec. 13A.2.8. (Appeals)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.8).

3. ##### Place of Filing


See [Sec. 13A.2.3. (Applications)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.3).

4. ##### Notice of Public Hearing


See [Sec. 13A.2.4. (Notice of Public Hearing)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13A.2.4).

5. ##### Annual Inflation Adjustment


These fees were established on December 5, 2023 (pursuant to [Ordinance No. 188,063](https://clkrep.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2009/09-0969-S4_ord_188063_2-10-24.pdf)) as the "Base Fee" and shall be automatically adjusted annually for inflation on July 1st. The [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall provide an updated fee schedule on an annual basis, which reflects the annual inflation adjustment calculated in accordance with the latest change in year-over-year Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers (CPI-U), as published by the United States Department of Labor, Bureau of Labor Statistics, in the Los Angeles area from the previous calendar year. This updated fee schedule will have the latest base fee.

1. ###### Base Fees


      For fees in this Article (Fees) which are identified on the “Annual Inflation Adjustment” columns with a solid circle, as shown in the table above, the base fee amounts in this Article (Fees) shall be the fee amount set forth in [Ordinance No. 188,063](https://clkrep.lacity.org/onlinedocs/2009/09-0969-S4_ord_188063_2-10-24.pdf), as reflected and incorporated into this Article (Fees). For previously-adopted fees and for newly-adopted fees, the base fee is the amount of the fee as of the date of introduction of the applicable implementing ordinance.

2. ###### Notice of Updated Fee Schedules


      Notice of the updated fee schedule showing the current fee amounts inclusive of annual adjustments shall be published on the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) website, as well as the Council File, no less than 30 days in advance of July 1 of every year. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall have the authority to adopt guidelines consistent with this Division (General Rules) for the posting of notices of updated fee schedules if the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) determines that guidelines are necessary and appropriate.
6. ##### Appeal Fees


1. Except as expressly provided in Paragraph 2. (Appeal Fees) below, the following fees shall be charged and collected with the filing of all appeals.

      1. Appeal by Applicant

         A fee equal to 85 percent of the total underlying [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) fees or $16,586 for first level appeal and $12,153 for additional level appeals, whichever is less when the appeal is made by the applicant.

      2. Appeal by Aggrieved Person Other than Applicant

         A fee of $166 in the case of an appeal by an [aggrieved person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), other than the applicant.

      3. Appeals for Street Dedication & Improvement

         A fee of $1,674 in the case of an appeal by the applicant or an [aggrieved person](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) other than the applicant.

An appeal filed pursuant to [Sec. 13B.10.2.G. (Appeals)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.10.2) shall be charged a fee in accordance with Paragraph 1. (Appeal Fees) above.
7. ##### Fee Payments


Before accepting for filing any [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or appeal involving any of the matters specified in this Article (Fees), the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall charge and collect for each [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or appeal the applicable filing fees.

8. ##### Fee Exceptions


The fees as provided for in this Article (Fees) shall be subject to the following exceptions:

1. ###### City Departments & Other Governmental Agencies


      The fees contained in this Article (Fees) shall not apply to any governmental agencies, except for the following proprietary [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) departments, the Los Angeles World Airports, the Los Angeles Harbor District, and the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, unless otherwise prescribed by any applicable memorandum of understanding or controlling interagency contract.

2. ###### Variance From Minimum Lot Area Requirements


      No fee shall be required in connection with an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from the minimum [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements of an improved [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), or on appeal from a ruling on the [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) application, where it is shown that the [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) neither conformed with the minimum [lot area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements at the time of issuance of the original [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) nor constituted a nonconforming [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

3. ###### Conditional Use Permits for Non-Profit School: Preschool/Daycare


      No fee shall be required in connection with an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), appeal, or approval of plans for a conditional use for a [school: preschool/daycare](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) pursuant to [Sec 5D.3.9.A. (Preschool/Daycare)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.9) which is determined to be non-profit, including, but not limited to, parent-cooperatives and facilities funded by a governmental agency or owned or operated by a philanthropic institution, religious institution, or similar institution. A facility funded by a governmental agency shall indicate the principal current and anticipated source of funds. Where any uncertainty exists as to the non-profit status of the facility, the applicant shall file a copy of the articles of incorporation or an affidavit, to the satisfaction of a [Zoning Administrator](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), showing that the child-care facility will be non-profit.

4. ###### Non-profit Social Services


      No fee shall be required in connection with an [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), appeal, or approval of plans for a conditional use or [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for a non-profit [social services](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) pursuant to [Sec. 5D.3.10. (Social Services)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.10).

5. ###### Credit for Fees Paid Upon A Reapplication


      1. At the discretion of the appropriate decision-maker, an applicant for any determination for which fees are required by this Article (Fees) may be allowed credit for the fees paid upon a reapplication for the same [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) under a different procedure when the decision-maker finds:

         1. That the applicant made a good-faith attempt to file the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) properly; and

         2. That the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) could be more appropriately approved if filed under a different procedure.
      2. This Subsection (Fee Exceptions) shall not be construed to allow credit to be given at the applicant’s option, nor to allow refunds of any fees paid on the original [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).
6. ###### Continuation of Nonconforming Uses


      No fee shall be required in connection with an initial [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for continuation of a [nonconforming use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) made pursuant to [Sec. 12.1.4.B. (Discontinuance of Nonconforming Use)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/12#12.1.4).

7. ###### Project Exceptions In Conjunction with a Quasi-Judicial Review/Relief


      Regardless of the provisions in [Sec. 15.1.2. (Multiple or Combination Applications)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#15.1.2), where a [project exception](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) and a [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), Conditional Use Permit, or other similar quasi-judicial review/relief are both required for a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), the lower of the fees charged for the project exception and [variance](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), Conditional Use Permit, or other similar quasi-judicial review/relief shall be waived.

8. ###### Full Cost Recovery


      In addition to the fees set forth in this Article (Fees), the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) may negotiate with an applicant, pursuant to [Sec. 5.121.9.3. (Supplemental Fee Agreements) of the](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-70178) [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), for reimbursement of the actual costs associated with the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#)'s processing of discretionary actions or other Planning reviews and processes for [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s involving extraordinary [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s, which require unusually heavy commitments of department resources but not involving a "major project", as that term is defined in [Sec. 5.121.9(b) (Creation of the Fund) of](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-70235) the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

### Sec. 15.1.3. Expedited Permit Fee

1. At the request of the applicant, the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) may charge a fee to offset expenses for additional human and physical resources necessary to expedite the permit process for development projects. A minimum initial deposit of $8,500 or, as adjusted by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), in addition to fees charged elsewhere in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A), shall be collected at the time of the request. In addition, fees shall be paid by the applicant for any additional costs that exceed the initial deposit.

2. The [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall calculate the costs and resultant fee, at the hourly rate in this Section (Expedited Permit Fee), in accordance with [Sec. 5.121.9.3.(b)3. (Supplemental Fee Agreements)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-70178) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) and shall maintain appropriate accounting records of the actual costs. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall resolve any dispute related to the fee. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall exclude from consideration any cost incurred or attributed to the processing of appeals.

3. The [Department](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall cause all money collected pursuant to this Section (Expedited Permit Fee) to be deposited into the Planning Case Processing Fund as prescribed in [Sec. 5.121.9.2.(c) (Supplemental Fee Agreements)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/laac/0-0-0-70178) of the [LAAC](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for purposes of disbursement as permitted therein.

### Sec. 15.4.3. Affordable Housing Linkage Fee

1. ##### Definitions


Terms shall have the meaning ascribed to them in [Div. 14.3. (Glossary)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.3). For the purposes of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) only, certain terms and words are defined as follows:

Additional Housing Units: A net increase in the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s or guest rooms to be added on a [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s of land by issuance of a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), after subtracting the number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s or guest rooms legally removed from the same [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of real property during the year preceding the issuance of the [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

Additional Non-Residential Floor Area: The net increase in the amount of non-residential [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), as defined in [Sec. 14.2.7. (Floor Area)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/14#14.2.7), to be added on a [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s of land by issuance of a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), less the amount of non-residential [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) legally removed from the same [parcel](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of real property during the year preceding the issuance of the [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

Applicant: Any individual, person, firm, partnership, association, joint venture, corporation, limited liability company, entity, combination of entities or authorized representative thereof, who undertakes, proposes or applies to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for a planning or zoning entitlement approval or [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) related to a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

Building Permit Application: Plans submitted to the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) pursuant to [Sec. 13B.10.1.B.2. (Vesting of Development Plan)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/13#13B.10.1).

Development Project: Any activity involving or requiring the issuance of a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that results in [additional housing units](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), [additional non-residential floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), additional single-family residential [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), or a [change of use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from non-residential to [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

Grocery Store: A [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is for a [retail](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of which greater than one half of the [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is devoted to the sale of food items intended for consumption or use off the premises, excluding alcoholic beverages.

Linkage Fee: The fee assessed, pursuant to this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee), on certain [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s in order to mitigate the impact of the additional demand for affordable housing caused by such activity.

2. ##### Applicability


The regulations, requirements, and provisions of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) shall apply to any [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). Unless a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is exempt from this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee), an [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) must pay to the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) the required [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) as a condition of the [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for which a [building permit application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) has been submitted in order to mitigate the need for affordable housing that is generated by or attributable to such projects. The provisions of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) are subject to the requirements set forth in [California Government Code Sec. 66000, et seq](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=66000&lawCode=GOV).

1. ###### Exemptions


      The [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall determine whether any of the following exemptions apply to a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) based on documentation submitted by the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) prior to the issuance of the [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). The fee imposed by this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) shall not apply to construction that includes any the following:

      01. Less than 15,000 square feet of [additional non-residential floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) in any non-residential [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), other than parking garages and parking facilities, as determined by the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

      02. Any for-sale or rental [housing development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) containing [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s where the following requirements are met:

          1. At least 40 percent of the total [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s are dedicated for [moderate income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s, or at least 20 percent of the total [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s are dedicated for [low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s, or at least 11 percent of the total [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s are dedicated for [very low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s, or at least eight percent of the total [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s are dedicated for [extremely low income household](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s; or the project is approved pursuant to [Sec. 9.2.3. (Opportunity Corridors Housing Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.3), or [Sec. 9.2.4. (Corridor Transitions Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.4), or [Sec. 9.2.5. (Transit Oriented Incentive Program)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.2.5).

          2. The [housing development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#)’s [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s are subject to a recorded affordability restriction of at least 55 to 99 years pursuant to [Sec. 4C.15.3. (Restricted Affordable Units)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.15.3) from the issuance of the [Certificate of Occupancy](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), recorded in a covenant acceptable to [LAHD](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), and subject to fees as set forth in [Sec. 15.4.2. (Fees for Enforcement of Housing Covenants)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#15.4.2). Such a covenant shall also subject [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s using this exemption to the replacement policies in [Sec. 4C.15.1. (Housing Projects that Result in the Demolition of Dwelling Units)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.15.1) or [Sec. 4C.15.2. (Non-Housing Projects that Result in the Demolition of Dwelling Units)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/4#4C.15.2), and to [LAHD](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) fees related to housing replacement determinations pursuant to state law, as set forth in this Zoning Code (Chapter 1A).

          3. For the purposes of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee), total [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s includes any units added by a [density bonus](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or other land [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) incentive, consistent with the affordability levels defined in [California Government Code Sec. 65915.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=65915&lawCode=GOV)
      03. Any [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) being constructed by, or on behalf of: (1) a government or public institution such as a school, museum, homeless shelter, or other similar [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s that are intended for community use; or (2) any private school that offers instruction in grades kindergarten through 12th grade.

      04. Any [hospital: local](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) [(Sec. 5D.3.5.A.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.5) or [hospital: regional](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) [(Sec. 5D.3.5.B.)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/5#5D.3.5) healthcare facility.

          2. [New construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of any single-unit detached home located on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) with an applied 1L Density District that is 1,500 square feet or less of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

          3. Any replacement of a single-unit detached home resulting in a net increase of 1,500 square feet or less of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from the prior home that existed on the property.
      06. Either (1) an addition of 1,501 square feet or more of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) to an existing single-unit detached home located on a [lot](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) with an applied 1L Density District, or (2) a replacement of a single-unit detached home resulting in a larger single-unit detached home with a net increase of 1,501 square feet or more of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from the prior home that existed on the property; provided, however, in either event, a covenant shall be recorded against the property prior to the issuance of a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for such [addition](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or replacement requiring the owner of the property to pay the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) if the home is sold within three years of the issuance of such [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). The covenant shall automatically expire at the end of such three-year period, if no sale of the property has occurred during such three-year period. However, in the event of a sale of the property within such three-year period, the covenant shall not expire until a notice of covenant termination is recorded. A notice of covenant termination shall be provided by the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) upon full payment of [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) due, based on the fee schedule in effect at the time of payment. The covenant shall run with the land and bind all successive owners of the property until the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is fully paid.

      08. A [residential project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is subject to a greater affordable housing fee requirement or is required to provide one or more physical housing units pursuant to the Mello Act ( [California Government Code Sec. 65590-65590.1](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=65590.1)), in order to satisfy its inclusionary housing obligations. In that case, the [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) component of the [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall be exempt from the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee). Non-residential portions of mixed-use [Coastal Zone](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s shall be analyzed separately from [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) portions of mixed-use [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s for the purposes of the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee). Non-residential portions of such [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s shall be subject to this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee). The provision of housing units or in-lieu fees to satisfy replacement housing obligations under the Mello Act, (as opposed to inclusionary housing obligations) shall not exempt a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fees).

A residential [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is subject to affordable housing requirements pursuant to any land use policy or ordinance or development agreement that exceeds the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) in either fee amount or on-site affordable housing percentages provided in Subparagraph b. above.

(General Provisions and Zoning), Sec. 11.5.11. (Affordable Housing)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-297069) of this Code.

      12. Any [adaptive reuse project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is a designated [historic-cultural monument](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) and is being converted to a [residential use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).
2. ###### Protests, Adjustments & Waivers


      1. An [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) may protest the imposition of the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) and request that the requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) be adjusted or waived pursuant to [California Government Code Sec. 66020, et seq](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=66020), based on a showing that the [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of the requirements of this Division (Affordable Housing Program Fees) would effectuate an unconstitutional taking of property or otherwise have an unconstitutional application to the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). Protests shall be filed with the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

      2. On or before the date on which payment of the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is due, the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall pay the amount required by this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) and serve a written notice to the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) with all of the following information: (1) a statement that the required payment is tendered, or will be tendered when due, under protest; and (2) a statement informing the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of the factual elements of the dispute and the legal theory forming the basis for the protest or request for adjustment or waiver, along with the substantial evidence that supports the protest or request, including any supporting documentation. The protest must be filed at the time of approval or conditional approval of the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or within 90 days after the imposition of the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). The [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall provide the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) with written notice as required by [California Government Code Sec. 66010(d)(1)](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=65915.).

      3. If the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) determines that [application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of the requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) would effectuate an unconstitutional taking of property or otherwise have an unconstitutional application to a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), the fee requirements shall be adjusted or waived to reduce the obligations under this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) to the extent necessary to avoid an unconstitutional result. The [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall render a decision within 75 days from the date the protest was received.

      4. If an adjustment or waiver is granted, any change in the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall invalidate the adjustment or waiver. If the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) determines that no violation of the federal or state constitution would occur through application of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee), the requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) shall remain fully applicable.

      5. Failure of an [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) to comply with the protest requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) or [California Government Code Sec. 66020, et seq.](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=GOV&sectionNum=66020), shall bar that [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from any action or proceeding or any defense of invalidity or unreasonableness of the imposition of the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).
3. ##### Fee Calculation


1. The [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall adopt, by resolution, a [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) schedule based on an analysis of the cost of mitigating the impact of the additional demand for affordable housing caused by [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s, and on the varying levels of economic feasibility in different geographic areas of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) based on current market conditions. The [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall also adopt, by resolution, a map or maps establishing the respective market areas throughout the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that inform the amount of the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) to be assessed for a given [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

2. For each [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall be calculated as the amount of new or added [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) in the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) devoted to the [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s described in the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) schedule, as determined by the [Department of Building and Safety](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), multiplied by the amount of the applicable fee, as found in the most recent [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) schedule adopted by [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), at the time the [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is issued, minus any deductions or credits.

3. ###### Fee Adjustments and Reports


      1. Annual Inflation Adjustment

         The [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall be adjusted annually for inflation every 1st of July, by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) in accordance with the latest change in year-over-year Consumer Price Index for Urban Consumers (CPI-U) for the Los Angeles-Riverside-Orange County area, or if such index ceases to be published, by an equivalent index chosen by the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). An updated [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) schedule shall be maintained by the [Department of City Planning](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), which shall provide a copy of the adjusted schedule to the [Mayor](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) and [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) each year.

      2. Five-Year Market Area Adjustment

         Every five years, beginning on July 1, 2018, the [Director](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), in association with [LAHD](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall undertake a new market area analysis and adjust market areas and geographies, where necessary, to reflect the most up to date rental and sales price information for each of the market areas. Any change to the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) schedule other than the Annual Inflation Adjustment described in Paragraph a. (Annual Inflation Adjustment) above shall be adopted by resolution of the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).
4. ###### Deductions or Credits


      1. Change of Use

         If the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is the result of a [change of use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) from non-residential to [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) to be paid is the result of subtracting the equivalent fee amount that either was paid or would have been paid, based on the pre-existing [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), from the fee amount required to be paid for the new [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) based on the most recent [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) schedule approved by the [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). Deductions or credits shall not be applied to any portion of a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) comprised of additional [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) resulting from [new construction](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). The calculation of a deduction or credit shall not result in a refund to an [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) or be applied as a credit to another [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) in a different location.

      2. Affordable Housing Units

         Any [restricted affordable unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s may be subtracted from the total number of [dwelling unit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) s in a [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) in determining the required [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

      3. Mixed Use

         The first 15,000 square feet of non-residential [use](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) in a mixed-use [building](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall be excluded from the calculation of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for the purposes of determining the required [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

      4. Transfer of Floor Area Rights

         Any additional [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is obtained by a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) through the provision of public benefit payments pursuant to [Sec. 9.3.5. (Transfer of Development Rights Programs)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/9#9.3.5) shall be excluded from the calculation of [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for purposes of determining the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

      5. Other Affordable Housing Requirements

         In calculating [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for purposes of determining the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), the following shall be excluded from that calculation:

         1. The [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of the [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) portion of a mixed-use [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is subject to affordable housing requirements pursuant to any land use policy or ordinance or development agreement that exceeds the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) requirements of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) in either fee amount or on-site affordable housing percentages provided in [Sec. 15.4.3.B.1.b. (Exemptions)](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#15.4.3) above.

         2. The [floor area](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) of the [residential](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) portion of a mixed-use [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) that is subject to affordable housing and labor requirements pursuant to [Chapter I. (General Provisions and Zoning), Sec. 11.5.11. (Affordable Housing)](https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/latest/lamc/0-0-0-297069) of this Code.
      6. Land Dedication

         If the Los Angeles Housing Department accepts, on behalf of the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), an offer by an applicant to dedicate land off-site from the proposed location of the [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for the purpose of building affordable housing, the value of the land to be dedicated, to be determined as the average of two independent appraisals funded by the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), may be deducted from the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) amount owed for the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#)'s [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). If the value of the dedicated land is more than the [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) owed for the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#)'s [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#), the [City](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) shall bear no responsibility for the difference in value, nor shall that overage be applied as a credit to any future [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).
5. ###### Payment of Linkage Fee


      The [linkage fee](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) is due and payable by the [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) prior to the issuance of a [building permit](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) for a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#). No additional fee shall be required for a [project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) seeking an extension of an expired [building permit application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).

6. ###### Refunds of Linkage Fee


      Any fee paid under the provisions of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) may be refunded to an [applicant](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) if the [building permit application](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) has expired and was not utilized to begin construction of a [development project](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#).
4. ##### Severability


If any provision of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) is found to be unconstitutional or otherwise invalid by any court of competent jurisdiction, that invalidity shall not affect the remaining provisions of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee), which can be implemented without the invalid provisions and, to this end, the provisions of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) are declared to be severable. The [City Council](https://zoning.lacity.gov/browse/15#) hereby declares that it would have adopted each and every provision and portion thereof not declared invalid or unconstitutional, without regard to whether any portion of this Section (Affordable Housing Linkage Fee) would subsequently be declared invalid or unconstitutional.
